title: Quantitative Anatomic Comparison of Microsurgical Transcranial, Endoscopic Endonasal, and Transorbital Approaches to the Orbit and Surrounding Skull-Base Regions.
abstract: Microsurgical transcranial approaches (MTAs) to the orbit and surrounding skull-base region lesions have been progressively complemented by endoscopic endonasal approaches (EEAs) and endoscopic transorbital approaches (ETOAs). This study provides the first quantitative, navigation-based comparison of working volumes and exposure areas of major approaches to the orbit and surrounding skull-base regions.Five alcohol-fixed specimens were dissected. Twenty-six subregions grouped into the orbit, midline, spheno-orbital, and cavernous regions were segmented. Nineteen approaches, including anterior MTAs, anterolateral MTAs, EEAs, and ETOAs, were performed. Exposure areas and working volumes were quantified.Endoscopic endonasal transpterygoid approach (EETPA) provided the greatest exposure of the optic foramen (67.98%, P = .03 vs EEA to the medial orbit). The superior eyelid approach with lateral orbitotomy achieved the widest access to the lateral orbital wall, reaching 98.56% in the middle and 99.42% in the temporal portions (P < .05 vs the orbitozygomatic approach [OZA]). The transcaruncular approach better exposed medial wall (99.41%, P = .04 vs EETPA), and the inferolateral approach gained largest orbital floor exposure (99.18%, P < .001). The extended transbasal approach maximally exposed the planum sphenoidale (99.28%, P = .03 vs orbitozygomatic approach with anterior clinoidectomy [OZA + AC]), while the EETPA the chiasmatic sulcus and the tuberculum sellae (98.76% and 96.47%, P < .001). The OZA + AC dominated most subregions, including greater wing, optic canal roof, and superior orbital fissure (98.49%, 98.18%, and 98.68%, P < .05). The superior eyelid approach with lateral orbitotomy better exposed foramen ovale at 88.89% (P < .01), foramen rotundum at 88.78% (P < .001), intracranial V3 at 92.92% (P = .04), and petrous apex at 93.85% (P < .01), while OZA + AC maximized intracranial V1 and V2 (87.94% and 90.74%, P < .05). The MTAs had largest working volumes (extended transbasal approach 59.35 cm3; OZA + AC 53.69 cm3).ETOAs provide unmatched access to the lateral orbit and cavernous regions, while EEAs excel medially and MTAs, especially OZA + AC, remain indispensable for broad spheno-orbital exposure and maximal working volumes.Copyright © Congress of Neurological Surgeons 2026. llm_summary: Researchers examined different surgical approaches used to access tumors and other problems in the eye socket and the base of the skull, which is a complex area that surgeons must navigate carefully. The study compared three main surgical techniques: traditional open surgery through the skull, minimally invasive surgery through the nose, and minimally invasive surgery through the eye socket, by performing these procedures on preserved specimens and measuring how much area each approach could reach and how much working space each provided. The results showed that different approaches worked best for different parts of the anatomy, with nose-based surgery providing excellent access to the inner eye socket and midline structures, eye socket-based surgery offering superior access to the outer eye socket and surrounding regions, and traditional open surgery providing the largest working space and broad exposure of multiple areas. These findings suggest that surgeons should choose their approach based on the specific location of the problem they need to treat, rather than relying on just one technique for all cases. Future surgical planning should consider these detailed comparisons to select the safest and most effective approach for each individual patient's unique situation.

title: Challenges in establishing epidemiological cut-off values for the Burkholderia cepacia complex.
abstract: The Burkholderia cepacia complex (BCC) is comprised of 24 species of gram-negative bacteria that cause opportunistic infections. While antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) has historically been used to guide treatment for BCC infections, recent work highlighting problems with AST for these organisms led the Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute (CLSI) to remove disk diffusion and minimal inhibitory concentration (MIC) breakpoints for BCC from its M100 standards document. Epidemiological cut-off values (ECVs) may be helpful to clinicians in the absence of breakpoints, as they may be used to determine whether an isolate has a wild-type or non-wild-type phenotype. Here, we present an analysis of BCC ECVs for ceftazidime (CAZ), levofloxacin (LVX), meropenem (MEM), minocycline (MIN), and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX). ECVs were calculated using MIC data from 3 previous studies and 3 independent laboratories for 1,896 BCC isolates. ECVs were 16 μg/mL for CAZ, 8 μg/mL for LVX, 16 μg/mL for MEM, and 8 μg/mL for MIN. The ECV for TMP-SMX varied depending on the analysis from 2, 8, and 16 μg/mL and therefore could not be reliably established. Challenges with establishing ECVs for BCC include limitations with the pooled MIC data set, broad MIC distributions, and high ECVs that are above the obsolete susceptible MIC breakpoints. These challenges limit the clinical utility of ECVs for these organisms and support the removal of ECVs from the CLSI M100 standards document.The Burkholderia cepacia complex is a group of bacterial species that cause difficult-to-treat opportunistic infections. Recently, clinical breakpoints, which are used to determine whether organisms are susceptible to certain antimicrobials, were removed from Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute (CLSI) standards for these organisms due to problems with antimicrobial susceptibility testing performance. Clinicians are now faced with the challenge of how to treat these complex infections without clinical breakpoints. Here, we determine epidemiological cut-off values (ECVs) for relevant antimicrobials for the B. cepacia complex. While we established ECVs for ceftazidime, levofloxacin, meropenem, and minocycline, we were unable to determine a reliable ECV for trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. Additionally, we encountered significant challenges in our analyses, including data limitations for these organisms and high ECVs that are not clinically useful. These challenges limit the practical use of these ECVs in helping guide treatment and support the removal of ECVs from the CLSI M100 standards document.

llm_summary: Researchers examined a group of bacteria called Burkholderia cepacia complex that causes serious infections and is difficult to treat because standard testing methods do not work well for identifying which antibiotics will work against it. The team analyzed data from nearly 1,900 bacterial samples collected from previous studies and independent laboratories to establish epidemiological cut-off values, which are measurements that help doctors determine if a bacteria strain is normal or unusual in its response to antibiotics. They successfully established cut-off values for four antibiotics but could not reliably determine one for trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole because the data was too inconsistent and spread out across a wide range. The researchers found that the cut-off values they did establish were too high to be practically useful for doctors trying to decide which antibiotics to prescribe for patients with these infections. These findings support the decision to remove these cut-off values from official clinical standards because the challenges with the data and the impractical results mean they cannot reliably guide treatment decisions for patients.

title: A Global Perspective on Migraine Attack Triggers: Understanding Differences Across Lifestyles, Religions, and Regions.
abstract: This review aims to summarize migraine attack triggers and understand variance across lifestyles, religions, and regions.Experts from 11 countries collaborated to suggest a definition of migraine attack triggers. After investigating the geographical distribution of various triggers, referring to an earlier review written by the International Headache Academy (iHEAD) of the International Headache Society, we collected literature and summarized findings on both globally observed triggers and region- or culture-specific triggers. The most common triggers included stress, menstruation, and sleep disturbances. Several triggers were observed only in certain cultural contexts, such as fasting during Ramadan or Yom Kippur, or in specific regions, including barometric pressure in Eastern Asia, Lodos winds in Türkiye, midnight sun in the Arctic region, and watermelon consumption in Brazil. We summarized migraine attack triggers reported universally and specifically in different settings. In addition to using conventional methodology, future studies should address the mechanisms and causality of these triggers.© 2026. llm_summary: Migraine headaches affect millions of people worldwide, but the things that trigger these painful attacks can vary greatly depending on where someone lives and their cultural background. Experts from eleven different countries worked together to review scientific studies and create a clear definition of migraine triggers, which are the things that cause these headaches to start. The researchers found that stress, menstrual cycles, and poor sleep were the most common triggers reported by people everywhere, but they also discovered that certain triggers only happened in specific regions or cultures, such as fasting during religious holidays like Ramadan, changes in air pressure in Eastern Asia, or even eating watermelon in Brazil. These findings show that doctors and patients need to understand both the universal triggers that affect most people and the unique triggers that matter in different parts of the world. Future research should focus on understanding exactly how and why these triggers cause migraines rather than just listing what they are.

title: Communication Difficulties and Management: The Lived Experience of Individuals With Frontotemporal Lobar Degeneration Spectrum Disorders.
abstract: Frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD) is the neuropathology that underlies a collection of progressive clinical syndromes typically classified by the initial/primary symptom. For example, individuals with loss of word meaning as a first manifestation are often diagnosed with the semantic variant of primary progressive aphasia. Growing evidence suggests that language and communication can be impacted in all clinical syndromes across the FTLD spectrum, but the functional relevance of these symptoms has yet to be explored.The Frontotemporal Degeneration (FTD) Insights Survey is the largest community survey of individuals affected by FTLD. It was administered online and included questions related to demographics, symptoms, life participation, quality of life, and experiences with and hopes for treatment. Self-reported diagnoses of respondents included the nonfluent/agrammatic, semantic, and unspecified variants of primary progressive aphasia, semantic dementia, corticobasal syndrome, progressive supranuclear palsy, and behavioral variant FTD. Here, we grouped respondents according to whether they had a language-predominant (n = 43), motor-predominant (n = 43), or behavior-predominant (n = 90) variant of FTLD and used descriptive statistics to explore how they perceive their own communication difficulties and gauge their motivation for management.Over 65% of respondents in each group identified changes to communication as a symptom; subsequent analyses focused on the responses of this cohort. Across groups, word finding and speaking were two of the most frequently endorsed difficulties. Over 50% of each group identified improved communication as a treatment priority, reflecting the impact that these symptoms have on their day-to-day life. Speech-language therapy is an important approach to manage these changes and minimize their impact. Whereas 76% of the language and motor groups had attended speech-language therapy, this was true for only 16% of the behavior group.Individuals across the FTLD spectrum experience changes to communication that impact their social engagement and quality of life. Management needs to be tailored to the needs of each individual, but recommendations are provided based on the insights and group-level preferences reported here. Future research is needed to identify current referral practices and how to increase engagement in skilled communication interventions, especially for individuals with the behavioral variant of FTD.https://doi.org/10.23641/asha.33940597.

llm_summary: Frontotemporal lobar degeneration is a progressive brain disease that affects different people in different ways, with some experiencing language problems first, others having movement difficulties, and still others showing behavior changes. Researchers surveyed over 175 people living with this disease through an online questionnaire to understand how communication problems affected their daily lives and what treatments they wanted most. More than sixty-five percent of people in all three groups reported experiencing changes in communication, with word-finding and speaking difficulties being the most common complaints, and over half of each group said improving communication was their top priority for treatment. The study revealed a significant gap in care, as seventy-six percent of people with language or movement problems had received speech therapy, but only sixteen percent of people with behavior-focused symptoms had received this help. Future research needs to explore why fewer people with behavioral variants receive speech therapy and how to better connect all patients with communication specialists who can help them maintain their quality of life and social connections.

title: Evaluation of Modern Hematology-Oncology Home-Call: Optimizing Patient Care, Physician Wellbeing, and Trainee Education.
abstract: Traditional home-call managing after-hours pager communications remains a common component of hematology-oncology fellowship and modern practice. Little is known about these patient-related interactions and implications. This project aimed to characterize after-hours pager volumes and evaluate perceived impacts on care, physician wellbeing, and trainee education. We performed a mixed-methods study at a tertiary academic center, analyzing after-hours pager activity from 2020-2024 across Hematology Consult (HCP), Hematology Outpatient (HOP), and Medical Oncology (MOP) pagers. A survey of hematology-oncology fellows evaluated perceptions and attitudes toward the home-call experience using free-text responses and a 5-point Likert scale. After-hours pager burden was substantial and sustained. The MOP received >3,000 pages annually, with medians of 5-6 per weekday and 15-15.5 per weekend day. The HOP volume nearly doubled over the study period (960 to 1,721 annually) with median pager volumes of 1-3 per weekday and 2-7 per weekend day. The HCP volume ranged from 594-768 pages annually. Survey response rate was 58% (19/33). Only 16% of fellows endorsed educational value from patient calls on MOP or HOP, and ≤5% agreed that call tasks required physician-level expertise. Respondents reported that the pager resulted in fatigue, anxiety, and social disruptions. Free text responses revealed themes of low educational value, high non-urgent call volume, and system inefficiencies. Contemporary home-call had substantial pager burdens with limited actionability, adverse effects on wellbeing, and low educational value. Systems engineering, including triage processes and augmented patient education, could help optimize patient care, physician wellbeing, and trainee education.Copyright © 2026 American Society of Hematology.

llm_summary: Doctors who work in blood disorders and cancer care often have to respond to patient calls and messages after regular work hours, but little research has examined how this affects their wellbeing or training. Researchers at a major medical center studied after-hours pager activity over four years and surveyed doctors-in-training about their experiences with these nighttime and weekend calls. They found that doctors received thousands of pages each year, with particularly high volumes on weekends, yet only a small percentage of fellows felt these calls taught them anything valuable or required a doctor's expertise. The survey also revealed that constant paging caused fatigue, anxiety, and disrupted doctors' personal lives, while many calls involved routine issues that could have been handled differently. The researchers suggest that hospitals could improve this situation by creating better systems to sort urgent from non-urgent calls and by educating patients more thoroughly, which would ultimately benefit patient care, reduce doctor burnout, and improve training for future physicians.

title: Real-world effects of a sepsis early detection model integrated into clinical workflow: a quasi-experimental study.
abstract: Sepsis is a life-threatening condition in which delayed recognition and treatment are associated with increased mortality. While predictive models such as Epic's Early Detection of Sepsis Model (ESM) were developed to support early intervention, their real-world effects after integration into clinical workflows remain difficult to evaluate.To evaluate the real-world effects of ESM integrated into clinical workflow on clinical outcomes, antibiotic use, and harm-benefit tradeoffs.We conducted a quasi-experimental study in a single healthcare system using encounter-level data from inpatient settings. Inpatient mortality, prolonged hospitalization, antibiotic use, and sepsis prevalence (defined by EHR) were compared between the pre-acquisition period (3 June 2023 to 24 June 2024) and the online period (21 August 2024 to 26 December 2024) when the model became visible to clinicians. We also applied a counterfactual framework using models trained on pre-acquisition data to estimate expected outcomes without ESM and to quantify harms related to overtreatment and delayed treatment.Among 89,469 encounters, 75,215 occurred during the pre-acquisition period and 14,254 during the online period. In unadjusted analyses, inpatient mortality, prolonged hospitalization, antibiotic use, and EHR-defined sepsis proportion all decreased during the online period (all p≤0.006). In the counterfactual analyses, observed outcomes were lower than expected without ESM for mortality (1.21% vs 1.94%; p<0.001), prolonged hospitalization (5.56% vs 8.14%; p<0.001), and antibiotic use (43.52% vs 47.74%; p<0.001). False positive harm (37.72% vs 42.31%; p<0.001) was also lower than expected.Integration of ESM into clinical workflow was associated with improved patient outcomes, reduced antibiotic use, and decreased harm from overtreatment, without evidence of increased harm from delayed treatment, supporting a positive net clinical benefit and the safety and effectiveness of ESM under Software as a Medical Device principles.Thieme. llm_summary: Sepsis is a serious blood infection that can be deadly if doctors do not recognize and treat it quickly, which is why researchers developed computer prediction tools to alert doctors when patients might be developing this condition. Researchers studied what happened when one of these prediction tools, called the Early Detection of Sepsis Model, was added to a hospital's electronic health records system so doctors could see the alerts while caring for patients. After the tool became available to doctors, the hospital saw improvements in several important measures, including lower death rates, fewer patients staying in the hospital longer than expected, and less unnecessary antibiotic use compared to what would have been expected without the tool. The results suggest that using this prediction tool in real clinical settings helped patients by catching sepsis earlier and reducing overtreatment, without causing harm from delayed treatment of actual infections. These findings support the safety and effectiveness of using computer prediction models like this one to help doctors make better decisions about sepsis care in hospitals.

title: Global burden of liver disease: 2026 update.
abstract: Chronic liver disease (CLD) remains a major global health challenge, affecting more than 1.5 billion people worldwide and contributing to morbidity, mortality, and healthcare costs. Cirrhosis is the 12th leading cause of death globally and together with primary liver cancer accounts for nearly 2.4 million deaths annually, disproportionately affecting low- and middle-income countries. The principal etiologies driving the burden of liver disease include alcohol-associated liver disease, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), and chronic viral hepatitis (HBV and HCV). Demographic changes, rising obesity, and increasing alcohol consumption are expected to escalate the burden of ALD and MASLD, while improved access to vaccination and antiviral therapy continues to reshape the epidemiology of viral hepatitis. Acute liver failure, though rare, results in significant clinical and economic consequences and highlights striking regional disparities in etiology and outcomes. Cirrhosis carries elevated risk of progression to hepatic decompensation, acute-on-chronic liver failure, and hepatocellular carcinoma. These complications are associated with limited access to advanced therapies in resource-restricted regions. Importantly, Africa now bears the highest age-standardized mortality rates from cirrhosis and liver cancer, driven largely by viral hepatitis, aflatoxin exposure, and constrained access to care. Liver transplantation remains lifesaving but is accessible to a minority of patients globally. The escalating burden of MASLD, the growing interplay of metabolic disease and alcohol use, and persistent gaps in viral hepatitis diagnosis and treatment underscore the urgent need for integrated prevention, early detection, and equitable access to evidence-based liver care. This review provides an updated global assessment of the burden of liver disease, highlighting widening regional disparities, and outlining priorities and strategies for reducing its worldwide impact.Copyright © 2026. The main causes of liver disease are alcohol use, obesity-related fatty liver disease, and viral infections like hepatitis B and C, with these problems expected to worsen as obesity increases and drinking habits change around the world. Africa currently has the highest death rates from cirrhosis, which is severe scarring of the liver, and liver cancer, largely because of viral hepatitis infections, food contamination with aflatoxins, and limited access to medical treatment.

title: Transcatheter Valve-in-Valve versus Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement for Failed Bioprostheses: AI-ECG Age as a Marker of Mortality.
abstract: To analyze outcomes of patients with failed stented bioprostheses undergoing redo surgical aortic valve replacement (redo SAVR) versus valve-in-valve transcatheter AVR (ViV TAVR) and evaluate the impact of preoperative artificial-intelligence electrocardiogram (AI-ECG) age on all-cause mortality.Between 2010 and 2025, 1558 patients underwent repeat AVR for a failed bioprosthesis. To obtain a more homogenous cohort, patients with concomitant procedures were excluded, leaving 244 redo SAVR and 369 ViV TAVR cases. Propensity score matching (1:1) was then applied, yielding 167 balanced pairs. Preoperative ECGs were analyzed using a convolutional neural network to estimate AI-ECG age. The age gap was defined as AI-ECG age minus chronological age, with positive values indicating a physiologically older age.The matched cohort had a mean chronological age of 72±11 years and AI-ECG age of 68±10 years. Mean age gap was -3.6 ± 9 years (range, -22 to +15). Compared to redo SAVR, ViV TAVR was associated with higher median predismissal gradients (13 [9-19] vs 9 [7-13] mm Hg, P<0.001), and more frequent severe prosthesis-patient mismatch (PPM) (25% vs 11%, P<0.001). Operative mortality was 2.4% for redo-SAVR and 0.6% for ViV (P=0.37). A positive age gap was an independent predictor of all-cause mortality (HR: 1.20; 95% CI: 1.16-1.24; P<0.001). No significant interaction between treatment modality and age gap was observed (HR: 1.02, 95% CI 0.96-1.07; P=0.571). An increasing age gap was associated with measures of postoperative outcomes, including atrial fibrillation, blood product transfusion, prolonged ICU stay, and prolonged hospitalization.AI-ECG age gap is independently associated with mortality following repeat aortic valve replacement and provides prognostic information beyond chronological age. Increasing age gap is also associated with several markers of postoperative outcomes, supporting its role as a noninvasive measure of physiologic reserve.Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Inc.

llm_summary: Researchers examined patients who needed a second aortic valve replacement, which is surgery to replace a heart valve that had previously been replaced with a biological valve made from animal tissue. The study compared two treatment approaches: traditional open-heart surgery versus a less invasive catheter-based procedure where doctors thread a new valve through blood vessels to replace the failed one. They used artificial intelligence to analyze heart electrical patterns from patient electrocardiograms and created an "age gap" score by comparing the AI-estimated biological age of the heart to each patient's actual age, with positive scores indicating a heart that appeared older than it should be. The key finding was that patients with a larger positive age gap, meaning their hearts appeared significantly older than their chronological age, had worse survival outcomes after either type of valve replacement procedure. This research suggests that measuring the physiological age of the heart through artificial intelligence provides valuable information about which patients are at higher risk for complications and death, going beyond what doctors can learn from a patient's actual age alone.

title: Grade 3 Lung Carcinoids/NETs: The IASLC Pathology Committee Study with Proposal of a New Diagnostic Category.
abstract: Lung carcinoids are well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors (NETs), designated in the current thoracic WHO classification as typical carcinoids (grade 1) and atypical carcinoids (grade 2), whereas rare tumors with carcinoid/NET morphology and >10 mitoses/2mm2 are designated as large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (LCNEC). This approach, however, has been a matter of growing debate.Lung resections of tumors with carcinoid/NET morphology and >10 mitoses/2 mm2 were contributed by the members of IASLC Pathology Committee. Digitized slides and detailed clinicopathologic, immunohistochemical, and molecular data were collected and analyzed.In total, 28 cases meeting the study criteria were collected from 9 institutions in 6 countries. Tumors exhibited mean mitotic counts of 15/2mm2 (range, 11-30/2mm2) and mean hot-spot Ki-67 rate of 32% (range 13-54%). In all cases, Ki-67 was heterogeneous, containing cold-spot zones with Ki-67 of <1%-15%. In all cases, Rb and p53 showed wild-type pattern by immunohistochemistry. Next-generation sequencing (n=9) revealed wild-type RB1 and TP53, low TMB (1.3-3.3 mutations/Mb), and genomic alterations characteristic of lung carcinoids. The study cohort exhibited significantly worse OS and RFS than control groups of 117 typical and 52 atypical carcinoids (P<0.0001 for all comparisons).In this international multi-institutional study, we address a major unresolved issue for WHO classification. By assembling the largest cohort to-date of the study cases, we propose that they should be classified as grade 3 carcinoids/NETs rather than LCNEC to enable clinical management more aligned with their biology. The concurrent IASLC proposal to include Ki-67 as additional criterion for grade 3 carcinoids should further enhance this approach.Copyright © 2026 International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer. llm_summary: Lung carcinoids are slow-growing tumors of the lung that doctors have traditionally divided into two grades based on how fast the cancer cells are dividing, but some rare tumors with carcinoid features that divide very quickly have created confusion about how to classify them. Researchers from nine institutions across six countries collected 28 cases of these confusing tumors and studied their characteristics, including how many dividing cells they contained, genetic information, and how well patients survived after treatment. The tumors showed high numbers of dividing cells and genetic patterns that were actually more similar to slow-growing carcinoids than to the aggressive large cell neuroendocrine carcinomas they were previously labeled as, and patients with these tumors had much worse outcomes than those with typical slow-growing carcinoids. The researchers propose that these tumors should be reclassified as a new grade three category of carcinoids rather than being called large cell neuroendocrine carcinomas, which would better match how the tumors actually behave and help doctors treat patients more appropriately. This new classification system, especially when combined with measuring a marker called Ki-67 to assess how many cells are actively dividing.

title: Contrast-Associated Acute Kidney Injury: Comprehensive Review of Risk Factors, Pathophysiology, Definition and Management.
abstract: Contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CA-AKI) remains an important clinical concern, especially as percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI) are being increasingly performed. This review provides a comprehensive, evidence-based synthesis of CA-AKI, acknowledging a shift in terminology from "contrast-induced" to "contrast-associated" to reflect the interplay of co-existing non-contrast factors and patient comorbidities. A comprehensive literature search was performed in PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from inception through June 2025 using terms related to contrast-associated acute kidney injury, risk factors, pathophysiology, prevention, and management; studies were selected based on relevance, methodological quality, and clinical applicability. While the exact causal relationship between contrast exposure and AKI is debated, CA-AKI is associated with adverse outcomes, including prolonged hospitalization, increased healthcare costs, and higher morbidity and mortality, as well as procedural variables such as contrast volume. Pathophysiological mechanisms include afferent arteriolar dilatation, medullary ischemia, direct tubular epithelial injury, and mitochondrial dysfunction, which can lead to maladaptive repair and progression to CKD. Management focuses on preventive strategies- maintaining hemodynamic stability, optimizing volume status, minimizing contrast dose, and implementing nephrotoxin stewardship. Despite the use of validated risk scores and emerging biomarkers for earlier detection, management remains largely supportive. Future paradigms emphasize individualized clinical decision-making, digital health solutions, and the potential for targeted therapies to prevent the AKI-to-CKD transition.Copyright © 2026. llm_summary: Contrast-associated acute kidney injury, which is damage to the kidneys that can occur after patients receive contrast dye during heart procedures, remains a serious concern as more people undergo these medical interventions. Researchers conducted a comprehensive review of scientific literature to understand the risk factors, how this kidney damage happens in the body, how it is defined, and the best ways to manage it. The study found that while the exact relationship between contrast dye and kidney injury is still debated, this condition is linked to serious consequences including longer hospital stays, higher medical costs, and increased risk of death or long-term kidney disease. The researchers identified that kidney damage occurs through several mechanisms including reduced blood flow to kidney tissue, direct injury to kidney cells, and problems with how cells repair themselves, which can eventually lead to chronic kidney disease. Moving forward, doctors should focus on preventing kidney injury through personalized treatment decisions, using digital health tools to monitor patients, and developing new targeted treatments that could stop the progression from acute kidney injury to permanent kidney disease.

llm_summary: Background:  Pruritus, which is the medical term for itching, is a common symptom that can result from various underlying health conditions ranging from skin disorders to systemic diseases affecting the whole body. The combination of symptoms described—itching, weight gain, swelling in the lower legs, and skin damage from scratching—suggests a complex medical condition that requires careful investigation to identify the root cause.

title: Effectiveness of Medical-Behavioral Therapy in Patients with Fecal Incontinence.
abstract: Guidelines recommend individualized medical and behavioral therapy (MBT) for fecal incontinence (FI), yet its effectiveness remains poorly defined. We assessed the response to MBT in FI.In this 5-center U.S. trial, adults with FI received individualized MBT (dietary modifications, medications, and pelvic floor exercises) for up to 3 months. The primary outcome was a ≥75% reduction in FI frequency after 4 weeks of MBT. Secondary outcomes included 3-month FI, bowel habits, FI-related quality of life (QoL) and changes exceeding minimal clinically important differences (MCIDs).Among 260 participants, FI occurred approximately once daily on average, more than one-third of bowel movements were incontinent, and nearly 25% had undergone anorectal procedures and/or colon resection. Sixty (23%) participants responded at 1 month but only 39 (15%) had a sustained response at 3 months; 200 (77%) were non-responders. At 3 months, FI-QoL also improved in sustained responders (P≤.006). Greater reductions in FI frequency were associated with a higher likelihood of exceeding MCIDs for FI frequency (P<.006) and FI-QoL lifestyle and coping subscores (P≤.04). In multivariable analysis, a greater response was independently associated with higher baseline FI frequency and no external anal sphincter defects (P=.0002). For a given reduction in Bristol stool score, FI frequency declined more among participants with more frequent baseline FI (P=.002).Among patients with moderate-to-severe FI, 23% and 15% responded to MBT at 1 and 3 months. Responses at 3-months were clinically meaningful, associated with improved QoL, and more likely in patients with higher baseline FI frequency, and no visible external sphincter defects.Copyright © 2026. llm_summary: Fecal incontinence, which is the inability to control bowel movements, affects many people and causes significant problems with quality of life, yet doctors have not clearly understood how well standard treatments actually work. Researchers at five medical centers across the United States studied 260 adults with moderate to severe fecal incontinence who received individualized treatment combining dietary changes, medications, and pelvic floor exercises (exercises that strengthen the muscles controlling bowel movements) for up to three months. Only 23 percent of patients showed significant improvement after one month, and this number dropped to just 15 percent by three months, though those who did improve experienced meaningful gains in their quality of life and bowel control. Patients who benefited most from treatment were those who had more frequent incontinence episodes at the start and those who did not have damage to their external anal sphincter, which is the ring-shaped muscle that helps hold stool inside the body. These findings suggest that while medical and behavioral therapy helps only a minority of patients with severe fecal incontinence, the improvements that do occur are real and meaningful, and doctors may be able to predict which patients are most likely to benefit based on their.

title: IMPROVED SEVERITY AND QUALITY-OF-LIFE MEASURES FOR FECAL INCONTINENCE: DEVELOPMENT OF THE MINNESOTA (MiNi)-FISI AND MiNi-FI-QOL.
abstract: Among patients with fecal incontinence (FI), the 29-item quality-of-life (FI-QoL) instrument is widely used but lengthy and only modestly correlated with symptom severity. We devised and evaluated revised symptom severity and FI-QoL instruments.Among 822 individuals with FI from a multicenter FI-QoL cohort (n=118), community (n=170), pelvic floor clinic (n=423), and clinical trials (n=111), FI severity was assessed using the Fecal Incontinence Severity Index (FISI), the Fecal Incontinence Symptom Severity scale, and a derived combined instrument, the Minnesota FISI (MiNi-FISI). FI specific-QoL was assessed with the 29-item FI-QoL, a new Minnesota FI-QoL (MiNi-FI-QoL) and SF-36 instruments. Associations between FI severity and QoL and the validity of the MiNi-FI-QoL were examined; findings were validated in a separate trial (n=260).Among 1082 patients, FI symptoms and QoL impact were worse in clinic and trial patients than community participants (P<.001). FISI scores explained 26% of FI-QoL variance, increasing to 60% when staying near a toilet to prevent FI was included (P<.001). For a given FISI score, FI-QoL declined as time spent near a toilet increased. Iterative reduction yielded a new 11-item Minnesota (MiNi) FI-QoL score, which captured 97% of the variance in the 29-item FI-QoL and correlated with SF36 scores. A revised 7-item Minnesota FISI (MiNi-FISI) explained 46% of FI-QoL variance vs 36% for the original FISI.The MiNi-FISI and MiNi-FI-QoL are concise, psychometrically derived short forms with strong performance across diverse cohorts. Further validation, including direct patient input to confirm content validity, is warranted.Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Inc.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether they could create shorter and simpler tools to measure how severe fecal incontinence (loss of bowel control) is and how much it affects a person's quality of life, since the existing 29-question quality-of-life test was long and didn't always match up well with symptom severity. The study involved over 1,000 people with fecal incontinence from different settings including clinics, community groups, and clinical trials, and researchers tested various measurement tools to see which ones worked best at capturing both symptom severity and quality-of-life impact. The researchers discovered that the original severity scores only explained about 26 percent of the variation in quality-of-life scores, but when they added information about how much time people spent staying near a toilet to prevent accidents, this jumped to 60 percent. Through careful analysis, they created two new shorter tools: a 7-item severity scale and an 11-item quality-of-life scale that captured nearly all the information from the longer original tests while being much quicker and easier to use. These new shorter tools performed well across all the different groups studied, though the researchers note that more testing.

title: Multi-target blood test for hepatocellular carcinoma early detection: a cross-sectional analysis of the prospective ALTUS study.
abstract: Globally, 350 million people are at risk for HCC. Ultrasound screening is recommended but is limited by poor early-stage sensitivity and low adherence. This study evaluated whether the multi-target HCC blood test (mt-HBT) demonstrates non-inferior sensitivity for early-stage HCC compared with ultrasound and assessed its specificity.This prospective, multicenter study, conducted between July 2021 and June 2025 in the United States, evaluated the performance of the mt-HBT in a head-to-head comparison with standard-of-care ultrasound among adults with cirrhosis or chronic HBV infection who were eligible for routine HCC screening. All participants underwent computed tomography or magnetic resonance imaging as a reference standard. The co-primary outcomes were non-inferiority of mt-HBT to ultrasound for early-stage HCC sensitivity, with sequential testing of superiority, and mt-HBT specificity. A secondary outcome was overall (any-stage) mt-HBT sensitivity.Of 3089 participants, 2293 were evaluable with paired ultrasound and mt-HBT results. Thirty-seven HCCs were identified, with 27 classified as early stage by Milan criteria. Early-stage HCC sensitivities were 66.7% (95% CI, 47.8-81.4%) for mt-HBT and 22.2% (95% CI, 10.6-40.8%) for ultrasound, confirming mt-HBT non-inferiority within the prespecified 5% margin. The specificity for mt-HBT was 81.8% (95% CI, 80.1-83.4%), which did not meet the pre-specified co-primary outcome of 82%. Ultrasound specificity was 98.6% (95% CI, 98.0-99.0%). Any-stage HCC sensitivity was 73.0% (95% CI, 57.0-84.6%) for mt-HBT and 29.7% (95% CI, 17.5-45.8%) for ultrasound. No serious adverse events occurred during the blood collection process.The mt-HBT had higher observed sensitivity than ultrasound for early-stage HCC, with a paired absolute difference of 44.4% (95% CI, 20.2-63.8); however, specificity did not meet the prespecified target.The trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05064553) IMPACT AND IMPLICATIONS: HCC screening remains limited by the suboptimal sensitivity of ultrasound, particularly among patients with obesity and steatotic liver disease. In this prospective multicenter study, a multi-target HCC blood test demonstrated substantially higher sensitivity for early-stage HCC detection than ultrasound while maintaining favorable screening performance across diverse patient subgroups. These findings are important for clinicians, researchers, and patients because they support further evaluation of blood-based approaches to address known limitations of imaging-based screening.Copyright © 2026. llm_summary: Hundreds of millions of people worldwide are at risk for liver cancer, but current screening methods like ultrasound imaging miss many early cases and many patients skip these screenings altogether. Researchers tested a new blood test that looks for multiple markers of liver cancer against standard ultrasound screening in nearly 2,300 patients with cirrhosis or chronic hepatitis B infection, using CT or MRI scans as the gold standard to confirm which patients actually had cancer. The blood test detected early-stage liver cancer in about 67 percent of cases compared to only 22 percent for ultrasound, which is a major improvement, though the blood test's ability to correctly identify patients without cancer was slightly lower than hoped at 82 percent instead of the target of 82 percent or higher. These results suggest that blood-based screening could help catch liver cancer earlier than imaging alone, which is especially important for patients with obesity or fatty liver disease where ultrasound works poorly. The researchers say more work is needed to refine the blood test before it can replace ultrasound in routine screening, but the findings support developing blood tests as a better option for detecting early liver cancer.

title: Minimally Invasive Hemi-Hysterectomy for Symptomatic Uterine Didelphys: Surgical Technique and Fertility-Preserving Considerations.
abstract: To describe the step-by-step approach to hemi-hysterectomy in a patient with uterine didelphys to reduce pelvic pain while preserving fertility.Tertiary academic medical center.A 32-year-old G0 patient with uterine didelphys, Obstructed Hemivagina and Ipsilateral Renal Anomaly (OHVIRA) Syndrome, and chronic pelvic pain. She had previously undergone resection of an oblique vaginal septum for hematocolpos. She presented with persistent pelvic pain requiring multiple emergency room visits, copious white-yellow vaginal discharge and leukocytosis of unknown origin with white blood cell count of 14,000 µL. Exam revealed a hypoplastic left cervix which was thought to be obstructing menstrual flow resulting in chronic pelvic pain.Robotic-assisted laparoscopic left hemi-hysterectomy and salpingectomy were performed. The left vaginal cuff was closed with special consideration given to the contralateral right cervix, which remained in situ. A medial defect in the right uterus was closed in multiple layers with appropriate reapproximation. Final diagnostic hysteroscopy was performed and confirmed patency and integrity of the remaining uterine cavity. The surgery and postoperative course were uncomplicated. Her chronic pelvic pain, abnormal vaginal discharge, and leukocytosis of unknown origin resolved after treatment.Hemi-hysterectomy is not a standard treatment for uterine didelphys-associated pelvic pain but may be considered in highly selected patients with persistent symptoms attributable to one hemiuterus after treatment of associated obstructive anatomy and careful exclusion of alternative etiologies. When pursued, meticulous preoperative planning and surgical technique are essential to preserve the contralateral hemiuterus and its reproductive potential.Copyright © 2026. llm_summary: A 32-year-old woman with a rare condition called uterine didelphys, which means she had two separate uteruses instead of one, suffered from chronic pelvic pain that persisted even after previous surgery to remove a blockage in her vaginal canal. Doctors performed a minimally invasive robotic surgery to remove her left uterus and fallopian tube while carefully preserving her right uterus and its ability to become pregnant in the future. After the surgery, the woman's chronic pain, abnormal vaginal discharge, and elevated white blood cell count all resolved completely, and she recovered without complications. This case demonstrates that removing one half of a double uterus can be an effective treatment option for women with severe pain from this rare condition, but only when the pain clearly comes from one specific uterus and other possible causes have been ruled out. Doctors emphasize that this type of surgery requires very careful planning and precise surgical technique to protect the remaining uterus and preserve a woman's future ability to have children.

llm_summary: Background:  Hemorrhoidal embolization is a minimally invasive procedure where doctors block blood vessels feeding hemorrhoids, which are swollen veins in the rectal area that can cause pain and bleeding. Some patients experience ongoing pain in the anorectal region (the area around the anus and rectum) after this procedure, which may be related to pelvic floor dysfunction (weakness or tension in the muscles that support pelvic organs) and central pelvic sensitization (a condition where the nervous system becomes overly sensitive to pain signals in the pelvic area).

title: Cardiac Remodeling, Prognostic markers, and Cardiovascular Outcomes Across Heart Failure Phenotypes in Adults with Congenital Heart Disease.
abstract: Data comparing cardiac remodeling, prognostic markers, and cardiovascular outcomes across heart failure (HF) phenotypes in adults with congenital heart disease (CHD) are limited.In this study, adults with CHD and HF were classified based on left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF): HF with reduced EF (HFrEF; LVEF <40%), HF with mildly reduced EF (HFmrEF; LVEF 41%-49%), and HF with preserved EF (HFpEF; LVEF ≥50% with pulmonary artery wedge pressure ≥15 mmHg). Cardiac function (strain imaging), prognostic markers (NT-proBNP and peak oxygen consumption), and cardiovascular outcomes (HF hospitalization and cardiovascular death/heart transplantation) were compared across groups.Among 1,303 patients, 304 (23%) had HFrEF, 551 (42%) had HFmrEF, and 448 (34%) had HFpEF. There was a graded worsening of biatrial and right ventricular function from HFpEF to HFmrEF to HFrEF (all p<0.001). Despite less severe chamber dysfunction, HFpEF was characterized by higher NT-proBNP levels and lower peak oxygen consumption compared with HFmrEF. HFrEF was associated with the highest adjusted risk of HF hospitalization (hazard ratio, 1.52; p=0.005) and cardiovascular death/heart transplantation (hazard ratio, 1.74; p=0.002), compared to HFmrEF and HFpEF. HF therapy was associated with lower event rates overall, with the strongest association in HFrEF, a more modest association in HFmrEF, and no significant association in HFpEF.In adults with CHD and HF, LVEF-defined HF phenotypes identified distinct patterns of cardiac remodeling and prognosis, with worse cardiac remodeling and adverse outcomes observed in the HFrEF phenotype. These findings support use of EF phenotype-based approach to HF management in CHD.Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Inc.

llm_summary: Researchers examined how heart failure develops differently in adults born with heart defects, since previous studies have not thoroughly compared these different patterns. The study looked at 1,303 patients with congenital heart disease and heart failure, dividing them into three groups based on how well their hearts pumped blood: those with severely weakened pumping (23 percent), those with mildly weakened pumping (42 percent), and those with normal pumping but fluid buildup (34 percent). The results showed that patients with the most severely weakened hearts had the worst overall heart function and the highest risk of needing hospitalization or experiencing death or heart transplant, while those with normal pumping had better heart structure but surprisingly high levels of stress markers in their blood. Heart failure medications worked best for patients with the most severely weakened hearts, worked somewhat for those with mildly weakened hearts, and did not significantly help those with normal pumping but fluid buildup. These findings suggest that doctors should tailor heart failure treatment based on how well a patient's heart pumps, rather than using a one-size-fits-all approach for all adults with congenital heart disease.

title: Reframing the Gut-Brain Axis: The Gut Wall as a Neural Immune Interface in Multiple Sclerosis and Autoimmune Neurological Diseases.
abstract: Gut wall physiology in multiple sclerosis (MS) and autoimmune neurologic diseases remains underexplored. This review examines gut wall dysfunctions' contribution to MS and autoimmune neurological disorder pathogenesis and progression. We discuss 3 inter-related aspects of gut physiology: intestinal barrier, enteric nervous system (ENS), and mucosal immunity. We highlight the ENS as a putative target of immune injury in selected antibody-mediated and T cell-associated neurologic diseases. Finally, we propose a unifying framework in which the gut functions as a site of immune priming and target of autoimmune injury, bridging microbiome-driven mechanisms in MS with ENS-directed autoimmunity across neurologic diseases. llm_summary: Researchers examined how the gut wall, which is the lining of the digestive system, may play an important role in multiple sclerosis and other autoimmune neurological diseases where the body's immune system attacks the nervous system. This review looked at three connected parts of how the gut works: the intestinal barrier that controls what enters the bloodstream, the enteric nervous system which is a network of nerves in the gut, and the immune system in the gut lining. The authors found that the enteric nervous system may be a target where the immune system causes damage in certain neurological diseases, particularly those involving antibodies or specific immune cells. The research proposes a new way of thinking about these diseases by suggesting the gut serves as both a place where immune responses start and a place where autoimmune damage occurs, connecting gut bacteria-related mechanisms in multiple sclerosis with immune attacks on the gut's nervous system across different neurological conditions. This framework could help scientists and doctors better understand how gut health influences neurological diseases and may lead to new treatment approaches targeting the gut-brain connection.

title: Anti-Fungal and Toxicology Assessment of ISFP10, an Inhibitor of Fungal Phosphoglucomutase (PGM).
abstract: The novel small molecule ISFP10 inhibits fungal phosphoglucomutase (PGM) activity in Aspergillus fumigatus and Pneumocystis spp. With 50-fold selectivity over the human isoform, conferred by a conserved cysteine residue present in several pathogenic fungi, ISFP10 may represent a promising broad-spectrum antifungal. We evaluated its activity against Candida albicans and Candida glabrata, followed by toxicology assessment in mice.Minimum inhibitory concentration susceptibilities were performed on three strains of C. albicans and C. glabrata and compared with fluconazole. Growth inhibition was further assessed in an 8-h, concentration-dependent growth assay. For toxicology, C57BL6 mice received once-daily intraperitoneal injections of vehicle control (dimethyl sulfoxide) or ISFP10 (10 mg/kg) for 7 days. Body weight, complete blood count (CBC), blood chemistry, histopathology of major organs, and lung extracellular matrix (ECM) and cytokine levels (ELISA, qPCR) were analyzed.ISFP10 inhibited all tested Candida strains with significantly greater potency than fluconazole. It also showed concentration-dependent inhibition of growth in liquid culture. In mice, no significant differences in daily or final body weight, ECM transcript levels, or interleukin (IL)-6 expression were observed between groups. Tumor necrosis factor-α (TNFα) levels in lung tissue were significantly reduced in ISFP10-treated animals, suggesting a potential anti-inflammatory effect. Blood chemistry and CBC revealed minor abnormalities (increased neutrophils, decreased potassium), but these were not clinically significant. Histopathologic evaluation showed no evidence of organ toxicity.ISFP10 demonstrates potent antifungal properties against C. albicans and C. glabrata and a favorable safety profile in vivo, supporting its further development as a potential broad-spectrum antifungal agent.© 2026. llm_summary: Researchers examined a new experimental drug called ISFP10 that targets a specific enzyme found in fungal infections, which are serious health problems that current treatments like fluconazole sometimes cannot effectively fight. The team tested how well ISFP10 worked against common fungal infections called Candida in laboratory samples and then gave the drug to mice for a week to check if it caused any harmful side effects. The drug proved to be much more powerful than fluconazole at stopping the growth of Candida fungi, and it worked in a dose-dependent way, meaning higher amounts killed more fungal cells. In the mice that received ISFP10, researchers found no serious organ damage or dangerous blood changes, though the drug did reduce inflammation markers in the lungs, which could be beneficial for patients. These promising results suggest that ISFP10 deserves further testing and development as a potential new treatment for fungal infections, though more research in larger animal studies and eventually human patients will be needed before it can be used in medical practice.

title: NCCN Risk Groups Do Not Predict Adverse Pathology or Oncologic Outcomes Among Patients With Grade Group 1 Prostate Cancer in the MRI Era.
abstract: Prior studies in the pre-MRI era suggest that patients with NCCN Intermediate and High Risk Grade Group 1 prostate cancer (GG1 PCa) on biopsy have increased risk for adverse oncologic outcomes. However, prostate MRI has altered patient selection for biopsy and improved prostate sampling. Herein, we examined factors associated with adverse pathologic features (APF) at radical prostatectomy (RP) and biochemical recurrence (BCR) among patients with GG1 in the MRI era.A prospectively maintained institutional prostate cancer registry identified patients with GG1 PCa on biopsy who underwent RP from 2000 to 2023, stratified by MRI use. Among 302 patients with GG1 and pre-operative MRI, NCCN risk group was associated with neither APF nor BCR. Age (OR 1.07, 95% CI 1.01-1.14, p = 0.01), PIRADS (p = 0.01), and % core positivity (OR 1.02, 95% CI 1.00-1.03, p = 0.04) were associated with APF. Age (HR 1.07, 95% CI 1.01-1.13, p = 0.03), APF (HR 4.36, 95% CI 2.14-8.86, p < 0.001), and positive margins (HR 4.88, 95% CI 2.39-9.98, p < 0.001) were associated with BCR.Prior to prostate MRI, NCCN risk groups offered meaningful prognostication among patients with GG1 PCa. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether a standard risk classification system called NCCN risk groups could predict which patients with early-stage prostate cancer would have worse outcomes after surgery. They compared patients who had prostate MRI scans (a detailed imaging test) before surgery to older patients who did not have MRI scans, tracking whether cancer returned or spread in both groups. Among patients without MRI scans, the NCCN risk groups did help predict worse outcomes, but surprisingly, among patients who had MRI scans before surgery, the NCCN risk groups were not useful for predicting problems. Instead, factors like patient age, MRI findings, and how much of the biopsy samples contained cancer cells were better at predicting which patients would have worse outcomes. The study suggests that doctors should stop relying on the traditional NCCN risk groups for early-stage prostate cancer patients and instead focus on newer information from MRI scans and biopsy characteristics to better predict which patients need more aggressive treatment.

title: Impella purge solutions in patients receiving extracorporeal membrane oxygenation.
abstract: The optimal Impella purge solution in patients receiving concomitant ECMO and Impella (ECPELLA) support remains to be elucidated. We aimed to assess Impella device function in patients supported by ECPELLA receiving heparin-containing or anticoagulant-free (5% dextrose or sodium bicarbonate) purge solutions. Of 25 included patients, 14 received anticoagulant-free and 11 received heparin-containing purge solutions, with a median of five days of ECPELLA support. The only episode of Impella device malfunction occurred in the heparin-containing group. Given the low event rate and apparent maintenance of acceptable device longevity, use of anticoagulant-free purge solutions alongside systemic anticoagulation in ECPELLA patients may be reasonable but requires validation in an appropriately powered study.© 2026. llm_summary: Researchers examined the best way to keep a heart-pumping device called an Impella working properly when patients also receive a machine that does the work of both the heart and lungs, a combination treatment known as ECPELLA support. The study included 25 patients who received ECPELLA treatment for about five days on average, with some patients getting a purge solution containing blood thinner and others getting a purge solution without blood thinner. The results showed that only one device problem occurred, and it happened in the group that received the blood thinner purge solution, while the group without blood thinner in the purge solution had no device problems. These findings suggest that using a purge solution without blood thinner may be safe and effective for ECPELLA patients since the heart-pumping device continued to work well in both groups. However, the researchers noted that because so few problems occurred, larger and more carefully designed studies are needed to confirm whether anticoagulant-free purge solutions are truly the better choice for these critically ill patients.

title: Geographic Variation in Diagnostic Codes Associated With Mild Cognitive Impairment, Alzheimer Disease, and Related Dementias.
abstract: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI), Alzheimer disease (AD), and AD-related dementias (ADRD) are growing public health concerns. Regional, demographic, and clinical differences in these diagnoses and associated comorbid conditions may inform strategies to improve prevention, care, and outcomes. To assess the demographic and geographic distribution of patients in the United States with coded MCI or AD/ADRD, the prevalence of common comorbidities, and the frequency and timing of progression to complicated MCI or AD/ADRD within 180 days, using data from the American Academy of Neurology's former Axon Registry.This observational study included adults aged 50-89 years with at least 1 outpatient encounter between 2017 and 2023 in 201 participating US neurology practices. Registry data were linked to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's 2019 Social Determinants of Health data set to assign patients to geographic regions. ICD-10 codes were used to identify MCI and AD/ADRD diagnoses, define comorbid conditions, and classify "complicated" MCI or AD/ADRD (e.g., with behavioral disturbances). The primary outcomes were odds of coded MCI/AD/ADRD, prevalence of top comorbidities, and proportion of patients progressing to complicated MCI/AD/ADRD within 180 days of initial diagnosis, stratified by region.Of 1,144,081 individuals with at least 1 documented outpatient encounter, 146,273 (12.8%) had MCI or AD/ADRD ICD codes. Of those, 65,088 (44.5%) were in the South, 35,027 (23.9%) in the Midwest, 30,008 (20.5%) in the Northeast, and 16,134 (11.0%) in the West. Unadjusted odds of MCI/AD/ADRD codes were 0.170 (Northeast), 0.155 (South), 0.134 (West), and 0.125 (Midwest). Among those with uncomplicated MCI or AD/ADRD at first encounter, the highest proportion of progression to complicated codes within 180 days was in the Northeast (2.04%), followed by the West (1.91%), South (1.24%), and Midwest (1.06%). Common comorbidities included hypertension, depression or mood disorders, and gait abnormalities.These findings highlight geographic and demographic variations in coded MCI/AD/ADRD prevalence and progression. Future studies should address underlying factors and the impact of comorbidities on outcomes, ultimately guiding more targeted approaches to dementia prevention and management. Future studies that phenotype AD/ADRD beyond the use of ICD codes can further validate the results.

title: From Hippocrates to Biologics, The Evolving History of Pericarditis: A Review.
abstract: Pericarditis remains a common and clinically relevant cardiovascular condition whose diagnosis and management have evolved substantially over time. Understanding this historical progression provides important context for contemporary practice and emerging therapeutic strategies. Early descriptions, dating back to Hippocrates, framed pericarditis as a clinical observation, with more precise diagnostic characterization emerging in the 19th century through the work of Laennec and later refined by clinicians such as Spodick and Hatle. Initial treatment approaches were largely symptomatic or surgical, including pericardiectomy for advanced constrictive disease. The mid-twentieth century marked a shift toward medical therapy with the introduction of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and corticosteroids, which improved symptom control but were limited by high recurrence rates. The advent of echocardiography transformed pericardial disease evaluation by enabling noninvasive diagnosis, hemodynamic assessment, and safer pericardiocentesis. More recently, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging has further advanced care by allowing detailed tissue characterization and improved risk stratification. Randomized trials established colchicine as a cornerstone therapy for both acute and recurrent pericarditis. A major paradigm shift has occurred with the recognition of autoinflammatory mechanisms underlying recurrent disease and the introduction of targeted interleukin-1 inhibition, including anakinra and rilonacept, particularly for refractory cases. Together, these advances reflect a transition from empirical management toward mechanism-based, personalized care. Ongoing progress in imaging, biomarker integration, and targeted immunomodulation is expected to further refine diagnosis, treatment, and long-term outcomes for patients with pericardial disease.

title: Genetic and cellular architecture of breast cancer risk across ancestries.
abstract: Breast cancer genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified more than 200 susceptibility loci, but most studies are dominated by European and East Asian populations.We analyzed breast cancer GWAS summary statistics from African (AFR), East Asian (EAS), European (EUR), and Hispanic/Latina (H/L) samples (159,297 cases and 212,102 controls). We estimated logit-scale SNP-based heritability, polygenicity, and cross-ancestry genetic correlation, partitioned heritability across functional annotations, and integrated GWAS results with the Tabula Sapiens single-cell atlas using scDRS+.The logit-scale heritability of breast cancer ranged from h2=0.47 (SE = 0.07) in EAS to AFR h2=0.61 (SE = 0.10), with no significant differences across ancestries (p = 0.63). The model-implied number of non-null susceptibility SNPs in the sparse normal-mixture effect-size model also varied from 4,446 (SE = 3,100) in EAS to 8,308 (SE = 2,751) in AFR, but differences were not significant across ancestries (p = 0.55). Cross-sample genetic correlations varied, with the strongest correlation between EUR and EAS (ρ=0.79, SE = 0.08) and weakest between AFR and H/L (ρ=0.26, SE = 0.24). Regulatory annotations were enriched for breast cancer heritability across samples. Integration with single-cell expression profiles implicated ancestry-shared associations with innate immune, secretory epithelial, and stromal cell types.These results indicate substantial cross-ancestry sharing of breast cancer polygenic architecture, highlight a consistent contribution of regulatory variation, and identify convergent cellular contexts that motivate functional follow-up and inform expectations for the transferability and attainable performance of common-variant risk prediction across populations.Published by Oxford University Press 2026.

title: Association of Postoperative Complication with Subsequent Mental Health Disorders: A Population-Based Study.
abstract: Postoperative complication is associated with lower health-related quality of life, but its association with subsequent mental health disorders is less well understood. We examined whether 30-day postoperative complication was associated with new or worsening mental health disorders.This population-based retrospective study included adults ≥18 years of age undergoing 1 of 25 common operations in Ontario, Canada, from January 2007 through December 2019. The primary outcome was new or worsening mental health disorders within 1 year, stratified by 30-day postoperative complication. Multivariable regression using generalized estimating equations adjusted for patient, provider, and procedural factors.Among 1,165,711 patients (median age 60 years; 61.9% female), 5.0% developed new or worsening mental health disorders within 1 year. The rate was higher among patients with a complication (6.2% vs 4.9%; p < 0.001). Complication was associated with higher adjusted odds (aOR) of mental health disorders at 1 year (aOR 1.28; 95% CI 1.24 to 1.32), with the strongest association at 30 days (1.77; 1.65 to 1.90). At 1 year, the association was present among patients without prior mental health history (1.31; 1.17-1.46), but not among those with pre-existing history. Patients with complication also had more new psychiatrist consultations (3.2% vs 1.5%; 2.02; 1.69 to 2.42) and a higher rate of new psychotropic prescriptions. Findings were generally consistent across other time points.Postoperative complication was associated with subsequent mental health disorders, specifically among patients without prior mental health history. abstract: Focal critical demyelinating lesions anatomically associated with progressive motor impairment are described in multiple sclerosis (MS) and restricted demyelinating diseases, typically within the spinal cord lateral column and ventral cervicomedullary junction (CMJ). This study describes such lesions within the intracerebral corticospinal tracts.We retrospectively reviewed people seen at Mayo MS Clinic (2002-2025) with progressive central nervous system demyelinating disease and progressive (≥ 1 year) upper motor neuron weakness anatomically associated with a presumed demyelinating lesion of the cerebral white matter, internal capsule, or upper brainstem, excluding alternative spinal cord or CMJ lesions. Demographics, disease course, Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS), MS disease-modifying therapy use, brain and spinal cord magnetic resonance imaging, cerebrospinal fluid studies and neuropathology findings were reviewed.Seventeen people had an intracerebral critical demyelinating lesion: cerebral white matter in 12 (70%), internal capsule in 3 (18%) and upper brainstem in 2 (12%). Ten were female, and all were white. Progression from onset course was 13 (76%) and from relapse onset was 4 (24%). Median, interquartile range (IQR) for age at progressive motor impairment onset was 46 (IQR 38-52) years, and EDSS at last evaluation was 5.5 (IQR 4.0-5.5). Sixteen (94%) had progressive spastic hemiparesis and 1 (6%) monoparesis. Cognitive impairment occurred in 6/12 (50%) and seizures in 3/12 (25%) with cerebral white matter critical lesions. Abnormal intrathecal production of immunoglobulin G markers was consistent with MS in 10/15 (66%). Neuropathology confirmed demyelination in 4/6 biopsies.Intracerebral critical demyelinating lesions associated with progressive motor impairment can rarely occur along the corticospinal tracts of the brain.© 2026. title: MRI Characteristics of Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody-Associated Disease: A Review.
abstract: Myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) is a demyelinating disease distinct from multiple sclerosis (MS) and aquaporin-4 antibody-positive neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (AQP4+NMOSD). Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is central to confirming attacks, defining lesion distribution, and excluding alternative diagnoses and is a key component of the 2023 MOGAD diagnostic criteria. However, its imaging spectrum and lesion evolution remain underrecognized in practice, and variability in imaging parameters can contribute to delayed diagnosis and suboptimal treatment.This article summarizes the hallmark MRI features of optic nerve, brain, and spinal cord involvement in MOGAD, including key findings from the 2023 diagnostic criteria, supported by illustrative figures and detailed tables. The characteristic evolution of MRI abnormalities in MOGAD is highlighted, including radiologic lag, lesion dynamics during acute attacks, and frequent T2-lesion resolution, contrasting with the persistent lesions typical of MS. A recommended MRI protocol for acute attacks is proposed, and the timing and utility of rebaselining MRI (ie, repeating the MRI to establish a new baseline) after onset are reviewed. The clinical course of MOGAD is of attack-related neuroinflammation evident clinically and radiologically, and asymptomatic radiological activity is rare, suggesting that surveillance MRI has less clinical utility than in MS and less value as a surrogate biomarker in clinical trials. MRI features that differentiate MOGAD from MS and AQP4+NMOSD are summarized and imaging red flags suggestive of alternative diagnoses are highlighted. Finally, emerging advanced imaging, artificial intelligence in MOGAD imaging, and the link between imaging and immunopathogenesis are reviewed.MRI is central to MOGAD evaluation, and recognition of the characteristic imaging features and lesion dynamics outlined in this review can aid diagnosis. Application of the standardized MRI protocol summarized here can optimize use in clinical practice and promote harmonization across research studies. Future imaging and artificial intelligence applications may improve diagnosis, disease monitoring, and understanding of MOGAD pathogenesis.

title: Evaluating a shared decision engagement system in the NCI community oncology research program: a multi-level RCT.
abstract: Improving patient-centered care and communication in breast cancer remains challenging in the complex and evolving landscape of breast cancer care delivery.The SharES (Alliance A231901CD) trial was carried out in collaboration with the NCI Community Oncology Research Program Alliance Research Base to evaluate a multi-level intervention in a crossed design: 1) a patient-level randomized intervention of the evidence-based iCanDecide online tool with added emotional support enhancements (iCanDecide-ESE), intended to promote better information uptake by supporting management of distress associated with a new diagnosis vs. the standard version (iCanDecide-S); and 2) a clinic-level stepped-wedge randomized Clinician Dashboard intervention. Patient-reported outcomes assessed 5-weeks after registration were knowledge about breast cancer locoregional treatment (primary outcome), cancer worry and breast cancer self-efficacy (key secondary outcomes). We evaluated outcomes using linear mixed models considering the nesting of individuals within clinic across time periods.We enrolled 542 (403 evaluable) patients and 54 clinicians across 25 surgical clinics. The confidence intervals for all outcomes included zero but excluded pre-specified clinically important differences in the knowledge score. We found good fidelity to the intervention components and considerable variation in the primary outcome across sites.The addition of emotional support components to a patient support tool previously found effective is unlikely to result in clinically important improvements in knowledge, cancer worry, or breast cancer self-efficacy. The strong engagement of NCORP sites, clinicians and patients with the study and intervention components suggests future cancer care delivery studies could leverage implementation strategies to promote multi-level patient-centered communication interventions.ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04549571. title: FDG PET characteristics of intraneural perineurioma: patient series.
abstract: Intraneural perineuriomas (INPs) are rare benign peripheral nerve sheath tumors with characteristic clinical and MRI features. Their 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) positron emission tomography (PET) appearance has not been characterized in a patient series. The authors evaluated FDG uptake patterns in INP.The authors retrospectively reviewed that data of patients with confirmed INP who had MRI and FDG PET studies that included the affected nerve. Eight patients were included (5 male and 3 female; mean age 30.8 years, range 16-61 years). All lesions showed mildly increased FDG uptake relative to the contralateral nerve (lesion maximum standardized uptake value [SUVmax]: mean 1.5, median 1.2, range 1.1-3.5; contralateral nerve SUVmax: mean 0.9, median 0.9, range 0.8-1.0) and skeletal muscle background (SUVmean: mean 0.8, range 0.5-0.9). Six patients had denervation edema and/or fatty atrophy, without appreciably increased FDG uptake in the affected musculature. No additional abnormal hypermetabolic foci were identified.INPs generally demonstrate low-level FDG uptake. PET is best regarded as a complementary test when already available or when metabolic characterization may refine the differential diagnosis; unexpectedly high uptake should prompt reconsideration of the diagnosis or additional evaluation. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26698.

llm_summary: The 2024 to 2025 General Surgery residency application cycle introduced an increase in program signals from 5 to 15, prompting researchers to evaluate how this change affected the matching process between applicants and programs. Using data from the AAMC ERAS application system, Thalamus interview platform, and NRMP ranking and matching records, the study analyzed whether signaling a program—a mechanism allowing applicants to indicate interest—influenced interview invitations, placement on rank order lists, and final match outcomes. Applicants who signaled interest at a program were significantly more likely to receive an interview invitation and be placed on that program's rank order list compared to programs they did not signal, and signaling was associated with improved median match rates for candidates. The findings suggest that both applicants and programs are using the expanded signaling system as intended to facilitate better matching, and the increase in available signals appeared to reduce the average number of applications per applicant without harming interview or match outcomes. The authors note that continued research is necessary to fully understand the long-term impacts of program signaling on residency selection and to identify any potential unintended negative consequences of this policy change.

The authors note that these observational findings suggest signals facilitate better matching between applicants and programs, though ongoing research is needed to identify any unintended negative consequences of the expanded signaling system.

title: Potently neutralizing and protective human monoclonal antibodies against the measles fusion protein trimer.
abstract: Measles remains a significant source of morbidity and mortality globally. There are currently no licensed treatments for patients at high risk of severe disease. There is limited knowledge about the human antibody response to a measles infection or vaccination or the structural determinants of antibody-mediated neutralization on the measles virus surface hemagglutinin (H) and fusion (F) glycoproteins. Here, we describe a panel of human monoclonal antibodies isolated from individuals who had been naturally infected with the measles virus. Several antibodies that recognized a prefusion-stabilized F protein potently neutralized the virus in vitro. We determined the structural basis of molecular recognition and virus neutralization using cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) for two antibodies that recognize distinct sites of the F protein, MeV-15 and MeV-104. These antibodies also strongly inhibited viral replication in vivo when administered prophylactically in a murine transgenic model and when administered therapeutically in a cotton rat model of established infection.Copyright © 2026 The Author(s). llm_summary: Measles continues to cause significant illness and death worldwide, yet no approved treatments exist for patients at high risk of severe disease. Researchers isolated human monoclonal antibodies from individuals naturally infected with measles virus and identified several antibodies that bound to the prefusion form of the viral fusion protein and potently neutralized the virus in laboratory tests. Using cryo-electron microscopy, the team determined the three-dimensional structures showing how two antibodies, MeV-15 and MeV-104, recognized different sites on the fusion protein and achieved virus neutralization. When given before infection in mice or after infection was established in cotton rats, both antibodies strongly reduced viral replication in living animals. These results suggest that monoclonal antibodies targeting the measles fusion protein may represent a potential therapeutic approach for high-risk patients, though further development and clinical testing would be needed to establish safety and efficacy in humans.
