title: The 2026 World Health Organization Classification of Tumors of Soft Tissue and Bone: 6th Edition.
abstract: The 6th edition of the World Health Organization Classification of Soft Tissue and Bone Tumors (STB6) integrates the latest scientific and molecular discoveries with decades of pathological expertise to establish a globally accepted common language for diagnosis and clinical behavior. In this volume, the "essential" and "desirable" diagnostic criteria have been refined, considering different resource settings, ensuring accuracy while maintaining flexibility. A tumor type (entity) is a tumor in which multiple parameters (eg, clinical, histopathological, and/or genetic features) differ from those of other tumor types. In total, 19 new entities met these criteria and were added. A subtype is different in at least one dimension from the main tumor type (clinical, histopathological, or genetic), preferably resulting in a different treatment or outcome. A morphological pattern (no longer "variant") is important for pathologists to be aware of to facilitate recognition but is not associated with different clinical behavior. The classification was drafted by 203 editors and authors from 27 countries, representing genetics, medical oncology, surgical oncology, orthopedic surgery, and radiology, in addition to pathology. STB6 includes soft tissue tumors (n=116), bone tumors (n=46), vascular tumors of soft tissue and bone (n=18), undifferentiated spindle and round cell sarcomas (n=4), hematopoietic and dendritic cell neoplasms (n=6), and genetic syndromes (n=6). In total, 62 sarcomas are included. A consensus was reached among the expert editorial board. In this review, we highlight changes in tumor classification in STB6, including recently described tumor types, novel diagnostic markers, recent discoveries in molecular genetics, and improvements in prognostication.Copyright © 2026 The Author(s). title: Progression of intermittent exotropia in surgical and non-surgical patients: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Intermittent exotropia (IXT) is a common form of childhood strabismus, and greater exodeviation or poorer control at presentation are known factors influencing the decision to pursue surgery. However, existing studies have not tracked pre-operative progression longitudinally or directly compared these changes between patients who undergo surgery and nonsurgical controls. This study aimed to compare the clinical features and pre-operative progression of IXT between surgically and nonsurgically managed children matched by duration of follow-up.The medical records of patients < 19 years diagnosed with IXT from 1 January 2002, through 31 August 2023 at a single institution were retrospectively reviewed. Patients with premature birth, neurologic disease, developmental delay, or other forms of exotropia were excluded. All patients who underwent surgery were observed from diagnosis until strabismus surgery was recommended and matched one-to-one with non-surgically-managed controls based on a similar observation duration. Control was assessed at distance and near using a standardized office-based severity scale ranging from 0 to 5.Eighty-one surgical patients diagnosed with IXT were matched with 81 non-surgical patients with IXT. Surgical patients (49 female, median age 3.7 years) were followed for a median of 23 months compared to 27 months for non-surgical patients (48 female, median age 4.0 years). Surgical patients had worse initial median distance control (2.3 vs 2.0; p = .004) and near horizontal exodeviation (25.0 prism diopters [PD] vs 20.0 PD; p = .035) compared to controls. After the pre-operative observation period, surgical patients demonstrated worse control and horizontal exodeviation at both distance (4.0 vs 2.0; 30.0 PD vs 25.0 PD; p < .001) and near (2.0 vs 1.0; 28.9 PD vs 21.6 PD; p < .001).Children who ultimately underwent surgery for intermittent exotropia not only presented with more severe disease but also demonstrated objectively greater deterioration in control and exodeviation during observation than matched nonsurgical peers. These findings underscore the progressive nature of clinically significant IXT and highlight the utility of serial, office-based control assessments in identifying patients likely to require surgery.

title: Using multi-trait polygenic scores to predict lithium responsiveness in patients with bipolar disorder.
abstract: The predictive power of polygenic scores (PGSs) for lithium treatment response in bipolar disorder remains limited.To enhance the prediction of lithium responsiveness by developing a multi-trait PGS (mt-PGS) combining genetic information from multiple phenotypes implicated in lithium response and/or bipolar disorder aetiology.We analysed data collected from bipolar disorder patients who had received lithium treatment for at least 6 months and participated in the International Consortium on Lithium Genetics study (N = 2367). The Alda scale was used to assess lithium responsiveness, and treatment outcome was defined as continuous total Alda score (0-10) and categorical outcome (favourable ≥7 versus unfavourable response). PGSs were calculated for 60 phenotypes grouped into 5 clinical-biological clusters: psychiatric and behavioural (#23 phenotypes), cardiometabolic (#17), autoimmune/inflammatory (#5), neurocognitive (#8) and renal function (#7). We applied cross-validated machine learning regression approaches in both outcomes within each cluster, with the selected features from each cluster subsequently combined to construct the final mt-PGS models. Model performance was assessed using explained variance (R2) for the continuous outcome, and both McFadden's pseudo-R2 and standard classification model parameters for the categorical outcome.mt-PGS explained between 5.70% (continuous outcome) and 9.11% (categorical outcome) of the interindividual variability in lithium responsiveness. Classification accuracy (area under the curve) for the categorical outcome was 68.24% (95% CI: 64.98-71.66), with a Brier score of 0.257. Of the 5 clusters, the PGSs for psychiatric and behavioural phenotypes were most strongly associated with lithium responsiveness, accounting for 3.67-6.52% of its variability.By integrating PGSs for multiple relevant phenotypes, predictive accuracy for lithium response improved substantially compared with single-trait methods. Future research incorporating larger, more diverse populations and combining genetic scores with clinical data holds promise for further enhancing prediction and advancing clinical implementation.

The multi-trait polygenic score approach integrated genetic information from 60 phenotypes organized into five clusters—psychiatric and behavioral, cardiometabolic, autoimmune/inflammatory, neurocognitive, and renal function—using machine learning to identify the most predictive genetic variants within each cluster. title: Intrathecal Hydromorphone Dosing for Adolescent Spinal Fusion: A Prospective Dose-Escalation Study.
abstract: Intrathecal opioids are widely used for postoperative analgesia in pediatric spine surgery, but optimal dosing remains undefined. We evaluated the relationship between intrathecal hydromorphone (ITH) dose, analgesia, and adverse effects in adolescents undergoing posterior spinal fusion (PSF).In this single-center, prospective, blinded dose-escalation study using a biased-coin up-down sequential allocation design, patients aged 10-17 years undergoing PSF received ITH starting at 3.5 mcg kg-1, with dose adjustments based on analgesic response (range 2.0 to 7 mcg kg-1 with a maximum of 400 mcg). The primary outcome was maximum postoperative pain within 18 h. Secondary outcomes included pain burden (area under the curve), 24-h systemic opioid consumption (oral morphine equivalents [OME], excluding ITH), adverse effects, supplemental diazepam use, and rescue opioid use. Associations between dose and outcomes were assessed using Spearman correlation and logistic regression.Twenty-seven patients completed the study. The median ITH dose received was 5.5 mcg kg-1 (IQR, 3.5-7.0), with a median absolute dose of 370 mcg (IQR, 180-400). No significant association was observed between ITH dose and maximum pain (r = 0.16, p = 0.41), pain burden (r = 0.32, p = 0.10), or 24-h OME (r = 0.13, p = 0.52). ITH dose was not significantly associated with the time to rescue opioid (HR = 1.24; 95% CI 0.68-2.25; p = 0.485) or diazepam (HR = 1.10; 95% CI 0.72-1.71; p = 0.655). Adverse respiratory events occurred at doses > 5 mcg kg-1 without improved analgesia.Increasing ITH dose was not associated with improved analgesia or change in supplemental opioid or diazepam use. Doses > 5 mcg kg-1 were associated with adverse respiratory effects. These findings support conservative dosing strategies and underscore the need to define the minimum effective dose in pediatric populations.© 2026 John Wiley & Sons Ltd.

In this prospective dose-escalation study of 27 patients aged 10-17 years, participants received intrathecal hydromorphone starting at 3.5 micrograms per kilogram and adjusted based on pain response, with doses ranging from 2.0 to 7 micrograms per kilogram (maximum 400 micrograms). Higher intrathecal hydromorphone doses showed no significant association with reduced maximum pain (r = 0.16, p = 0.41), lower pain burden (r = 0.32, p = 0.10), or decreased 24-hour systemic opioid consumption (r = 0.13, p = 0.52). Doses exceeding 5 micrograms per kilogram were associated with adverse respiratory events without providing improved pain relief, suggesting that higher doses do not offer additional analgesic benefit. These findings support using conservative dosing strategies for intrathecal.

title: An international multicenter analysis of the outcome of pediatric first variceal hemorrhage.
abstract: Management of portal hypertension in children including primary prophylaxis of variceal bleeding is controversial due to limited understanding of mortality risk after first variceal hemorrhage (1VH). This international multicenter study was designed to advance understanding of outcomes after pediatric 1VH.Center-specific characteristics and approaches to portal hypertension were determined at 44 international sites. K-means clustered the centers based upon volume and complexity of approaches [cluster 1 high (n=5), cluster 2 low (n=21), cluster 3 intermediate (n=18]). Clinical features and outcomes after 1VH were available from 345 subjects. Factors associated with overall survival (OS) and survival with native liver (SNL) were estimated by Kaplan-Meier survival curves, log rank tests, univariable and multivariable Cox regression models. OS and SNL were high in portal vein thrombosis and noncirrhotic diseases and significantly higher than biliary atresia and cirrhotic diseases (p<.001). Diminished SNL was observed in decompensated disease [diuretics (i.e. ascites) or hospitalization at 1VH], biliary atresia with poor bile flow, cirrhotic disease, after sclerotherapy or no endoscopic intervention. Diminished OS was noted in those with cirrhosis or requiring sclerotherapy. 6-week mortality was determined and compared among clusters using average treatment effect under the Rubin causal model. Overall 6-week mortality was 4.1%, 1.4% in nonhospitalized subjects and was significantly higher in cluster 2 versus 1 centers (P=.010).Immediate mortality after 1VH in children is low compared to adults. Outcomes after 1VH are diagnosis-specific and worse in decompensated disease and after sclerotherapy. The study analyzed clinical features and survival data from 345 children, categorizing centers by their volume and complexity of care and comparing outcomes across different underlying diagnoses and disease severity levels. abstract: BackgroundAfrican American adults experience a disproportionate burden of dementia, shaped by structural and clinical factors that remain unclear.ObjectiveTo quantify associations between multimorbidity, polypharmacy, and cognition in the context of neighborhood disadvantage.MethodsThis study is a cross-sectional analysis of 348 African American adults aged 45-92 years (mean 64.3 years; 73.6% female) from the Aging Research Characterizing Health Exposome via Social drivers (ARCHES) cohort. Comorbidity burden was assessed using a modified Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI), polypharmacy as ≥5 medications, and neighborhood disadvantage using the Area Deprivation Index (ADI). Linear regression estimated associations with a Preclinical Alzheimer's Cognitive Composite (PACC). The polypharmacy model included modified CCI as a covariate, and effect modification by ADI was assessed using an interaction term between polypharmacy and ADI.ResultsHigher modified CCI was associated with lower cognitive performance (B = -0.071; 95% CI: -0.130, -0.012). Polypharmacy was not independently associated with cognition after modified CCI adjustment (B = -0.081; β = -0.057; p = 0.257). No significant ADI interaction was found (p = 0.064).

title: Left Atrial Appendage Closure Versus Oral Anticoagulation in Atrial Fibrillation: An Updated Meta-Analysis of RCTs Using Reconstructed Individual Patient Data.
abstract: Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) is a reasonable alternative to oral anticoagulation (OAC) in selected patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). We conducted an updated meta-analysis of RCTs comparing LAAC vs. OAC in patients with AF. The primary efficacy endpoint was a composite of all stroke, systemic embolism, or cardiovascular/all-cause death. The primary safety endpoint was major bleeding. Secondary endpoints included net adverse clinical events, all-cause death, non-procedure related bleeding, and ischemic stroke. Reconstructed IPD meta-analysis using a two-stage approach and study-level meta-analysis using random-effects models were performed. Six trials enrolling 7,004 patients randomized to LAAC (n=3,681) or OAC (n=3,323) were included. There were no significant differences between LAAC vs. OAC for the primary efficacy endpoint (∆RMST -0.006 years; 95% CI -0.027 to 0.015 years, p=0.56) or primary safety endpoint (∆RMST 0.004 years; 95% CI -0.025 to 0.034 years; p=0.77) at 3 years. Non-procedure related bleeding was significantly lower with LAAC vs. OAC (∆RMST 0.162 years; 95% CI 0.104 to 0.220 years, p<0.001) with no difference in all-cause death (∆RMST 0.029 years, 95% CI -0.031 to 0.089 years, p=0.34). In a study-level meta-analysis, ischemic stroke was not significantly different with LAAC vs. OAC (RR 1.32; 95% CI 0.94 to 1.86; p=0.09). In conclusion, the trade-off between a statistically significant lower risk of non-procedure related bleeding and a numerically, but not statistically, higher risk of ischemic stroke with LAAC vs. OAC necessitates individualized risk assessment and shared decision making for patients with AF at elevated risk of stroke.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: There Were No Differences in Total Knee Arthroplasty Function Following High Tibial Osteotomy or Unicompartmental Knee Arthroplasty: More Than 10 Years of Follow-Up.
abstract: In the United States (U.S.), unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA) is more widely adopted than high tibial osteotomy (HTO) as treatment for medial knee osteoarthritis. Both procedures may ultimately require conversion to total knee arthroplasty (TKA). However, outcomes of TKA following prior HTO or UKA remain incompletely characterized in the U.S.Therefore, this study evaluated revision-free survivorship and clinical outcomes of TKA following prior ipsilateral HTO or UKA in a U.S.We prospectively followed 216 patients who underwent TKA after ipsilateral HTO (n = 134) or UKA (n = 82) between 2000 and 2023 at a single U.S. center, who had a mean follow-up of 11.5 years (range, zero to 24.0) after TKA. Data included demographics, comorbidities, implant characteristics, revision surgery, all-cause reoperations, Knee Society Scores (KSS; minimal clinically important difference six points), and range of motion. Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards analyses were used to compare revision-free survival, infection rate, and reoperation rate between cohorts.Revision, infection, and all-cause reoperation rates after TKA were similar in both cohorts (revision: 4 versus 6%, P = 0.91; infection: 4 versus 2%, P = 0.27; all-cause reoperation, P = 0.34). The UKA-TKA procedures more frequently employed stemmed tibial (71 versus 15%, P < 0.001) and femoral components (21 versus 5%, P < 0.001) than the HTO-TKA cohort, although HTO-TKA procedures had a significantly longer surgery time (133.5 versus 102.0 minutes, P < 0.001). The HTO-TKA patients had significantly higher KSS functional scores at two years (median difference 15 points, P < 0.001) and five years (median difference 10 points, P = 0.04) compared to UKA-TKA.In this U.S. cohort, TKAs following prior HTO or UKA showed no statistically significant differences in revision rates, infection, or all-cause reoperation. Operative time was significantly longer for TKA after HTO, whereas TKA after UKA more frequently required stemmed components. Overall, these findings suggest no statistically significant differences in outcomes or survivorship between prior HTO and the widely adopted UKA, supporting HTO as a viable joint-preserving option in appropriately selected patients.Copyright © 2026 The Author(s). title: Assessing the Impact of Increased Pull-Up Requirements on Upper Extremity Musculoskeletal Injuries Among Males in the U.S. Marine Corps: An Interrupted Time Series Analysis.
abstract: In 2017, the United States Marine Corps (USMC) increased the pull-up requirements of the Physical Fitness Test (PFT) to improve combat readiness, raising concerns regarding potential increases in upper extremity (UE) musculoskeletal injuries (MSKIs). This study assesses the impact of this policy change on UE MSKI incidence among active-duty male Marines.Linear regressions estimated with ordinary least squares were used to perform interrupted time series analyses of UE MSKI rates among male Marines from the Military Health System Data Repository between 2014 and 2023. Upper extremity MSKI rate trends were evaluated pre- (2014-2016) and post-intervention (2017-2023), stratified by age, race/ethnicity, body mass index (BMI), and rank. Newey-West SEs were used in linear regression analyses to adjust for violations from autocorrelation and heteroskedasticity.The study population included 231,323 Marines in the pre-intervention period (2014-2016) and 313,537 in the post-intervention period (2017-2023). Cumulative UE MSKI proportions increased (9.0%-9.4%). Pre-policy, UE MSKI rates trended downward (b1 = -5.09, P < .001). Post-policy, this trend significantly reversed (b3 = 5.11, P < .001) but not immediately (b2 = -4.00, P = .431). Subgroup analysis revealed sustained increasing rates among Marines <20 years (b1 + b3 = 0.88, P < .001). Conversely, decreasing rates occurred in Marines with obesity (b1 + b3 = -1.09, P = .006), ages 40-49 (b1 + b3 = -1.21, P = .046), and senior enlisted (b1 + b3 = -1.10, P = .012). Warrant officers experienced a significant decrease in UE MSKI rates (b2 = -34.22, P = .007) as well as subsequent trend stabilization (b3 = 6.23, P < .001).The 2017 standards were temporally associated with a plateau in previously declining UE MSKI rates. While no immediate population-level spike occurred, the heterogeneity of subgroup responses highlights specific risks for younger personnel. Future policy modifications should balance fitness objectives with targeted injury prevention strategies to optimize readiness.Published by Oxford University Press on behalf of the Association of Military Surgeons of the United States 2026.

title: A Multicenter 13-Week Evaluation of the twiist Automated Insulin Delivery in Insulin-Treated Type 2 Diabetes: The twiist-T2D Pivotal Trial.
abstract: To evaluate the efficacy, safety, and user satisfaction of the twiist automated insulin delivery (AID) system in adults with type 2 diabetes.In a single-arm, multicenter trial, 307 adults with insulin-treated type 2 diabetes, 19-85 years old, initiated use of the twiist AID system for 13 weeks after collection of baseline continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) data. The primary outcome was change in HbA1c from baseline to 13 weeks.Mean HbA1c decreased by 0.7% (95% CI -0.9 to -0.6) from 8.1% ± 1.5% at baseline to 7.4% ± 0.9% after using twiist for 13 weeks (P < 0.001 for both noninferiority and superiority). The treatment effect was greatest in participants with baseline HbA1c ≥9.0%. A substantial HbA1c reduction was observed when AID was added to prestudy use of a glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonist or sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor drug, which was continued during the trial. Mean CGM-measured time-in-range 70-180 mg/dL increased from 57% ± 26% to 73% ± 17% (mean change 16% [95% CI 14-18]; P < 0.001). All other multiplicity-controlled CGM outcomes reflective of hyperglycemia showed significant improvement from baseline. The frequency of CGM-measured hypoglycemia was low at baseline and remained low during follow-up. Diabetic ketoacidosis occurred in one participant; no severe hypoglycemia events occurred. Using twiist, participant satisfaction was higher than with their prestudy insulin delivery method (P < 0.001) and sleep quality improved (P < 0.001).In this single-arm, 13-week trial in adults with insulin-treated type 2 diabetes, AID with the twiist system was safe and associated with substantially improved glycemia.© 2026 by the American Diabetes Association.

title: Top Ten Tips Palliative Care Clinicians Should Know About Caring for People Receiving Critical Care for Cardiovascular Disease.
abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of death worldwide and is a major driver of critical illness, resulting in admission to cardiac intensive care units (CICUs). Patients with acute, life-threatening CVD often experience episodes of acute decompensation characterized by high symptom burden that may portend progressive loss of function, significantly impair quality of life (QOL), and involve high-intensity, technologically advanced therapies to sustain life. Despite these advances, up to 30% of patients die during CICU hospitalizations, and those who survive may subsequently face persistent functional impairment and psychosocial distress. During critical CVD (CCVD), patients often endure prognostic uncertainty and face complex decisions regarding life-sustaining therapies alongside refractory symptoms. Thus, care that focuses exclusively on disease-directed or life-prolonging therapies is often insufficient to address the full spectrum of patient and caregiver needs. When integrated alongside intensive cardiovascular care, palliative care (PC) offers a complementary and essential approach to the management of CCVD to inform therapeutic decisions, improve QOL, and address psychosocial and spiritual well-being. In this article, a multidisciplinary team featuring PC clinicians (physicians, nurse practitioners, social worker, psychologist, and chaplain), cardiologists, cardiac surgeons, cardiothoracic anesthesiologists, and intensivists present evidence-based guidance in a "Top Ten Tips" format to support PC clinicians caring for CICU patients and their caregivers.

llm_summary: Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of death worldwide and drives critical illness requiring intensive care, yet up to 30% of patients die during cardiac intensive care unit hospitalizations while survivors often face functional impairment and psychological distress. A multidisciplinary team of palliative care clinicians, cardiologists, cardiac surgeons, and intensivists developed evidence-based guidance to support palliative care providers caring for critically ill cardiovascular patients and their families. The authors recognized that patients with acute, life-threatening cardiovascular disease experience high symptom burden, prognostic uncertainty, and complex decisions about life-sustaining therapies that disease-directed treatment alone cannot adequately address. The guidance presented in a "Top Ten Tips" format emphasizes that palliative care integrated alongside intensive cardiovascular care offers a complementary approach to improve quality of life and address psychosocial and spiritual needs alongside medical decision-making. This collaborative framework aims to help palliative care clinicians better support both patients and caregivers navigating the physical, emotional, and existential challenges of critical cardiovascular illness.
llm_summary_expert: A multidisciplinary team of palliative care clinicians, cardiologists, cardiac surgeons, cardiothoracic anesthesiologists, and intensivists developed evidence-based guidance for integrating palliative care into critical cardiovascular disease management in cardiac intensive care units. The authors identified that cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of death worldwide and drives critical illness, with up to 30% of cardiac intensive care unit patients dying during hospitalization and survivors experiencing persistent functional impairment and psychosocial distress. The guidance addresses the high symptom burden, prognostic uncertainty, and complex therapeutic decisions that characterize acute, life-threatening cardiovascular disease requiring life-sustaining technologies. The authors presented ten evidence-based tips to support palliative care clinicians in addressing the full spectrum of patient and caregiver needs alongside intensive cardiovascular care. This multidisciplinary consensus approach emphasizes that palliative care integrated with disease-directed therapies improves quality of life and addresses psychosocial and spiritual well-being in critically ill cardiovascular patients.

title: Legionella Pneumonia in the Modern Era: Clinical Features and Predictors of Mortality.
abstract: Legionella pneumonia is an important cause of severe pneumonia, yet contemporary data describing its clinical phenotype, diagnostic patterns, and outcomes in the modern era are limited.We conducted a retrospective multicenter cohort study of adults with laboratory-confirmed Legionella pneumonia across an integrated health system between January 2019 and September 2025. The primary outcome was 30-day mortality. Severe disease was defined as having a requirement for high-flow nasal cannula, noninvasive ventilation, mechanical ventilation, or extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). Univariate and multivariable logistic regression were used to identify predictors of mortality and severe disease.There were 344 patients with laboratory-confirmed Legionella pneumonia during the study period. The median age was 66.6 years, and 45.1% were immunocompromised. Most patients required hospital admission (94.2%), with 36.1% admitted to the intensive care unit; 22.7% required mechanical ventilation and 1.5% ECMO. Thirty- and 90-day mortality were 11.9% and 16.6%, respectively. In multivariable analysis, cirrhosis (OR 10.2, 95% CI 2.15-48.3, P = .003), immunocompromised status (odds ratio [OR] 2.24, 95% CI 1.05-4.77, P = .036), age (OR 1.03, 95% CI 1.00-1.06, P = .031), and lymphopenia at presentation (OR 2.09, 95% CI 1.02-4.24, P = .043) were independently associated with increased 30-day mortality. Among patients who were polymerase chain reaction (PCR) or culture positive, urinary antigen testing was positive in only 25.6%.Legionella pneumonia was associated with substantial short-term mortality. Cirrhosis, age, immunocompromised status, and lymphopenia at presentation emerged as independent predictors of 30-day mortality, underscoring the importance of host vulnerability in determining outcomes.© The Author(s) 2026. title: Utilizing EHR Automation to Improve Safety of Newly Admitted Patients With Tracheostomy.
abstract: The project aimed to improve the safety of hospitalized tracheostomy and laryngectomy adults by reducing the time to initial respiratory therapist assessment and the delivery of emergency equipment to the bedside.Tracheostomy and laryngectomy patients are classified as a low-volume, high-risk patient population. The specialized care and equipment needed for them are essential, especially in an acute care setting like a hospital. The ability to ensure safety equipment compliance at the time of admission is a challenge as it relies heavily on communication, which can be subject to human error. Three months of retrospective data were analyzed, which led the team to identify a gap in the notification process. The project team created an automated pager notification of new patients needing assessment and delivery of emergency equipment, triggered by an EHR notification when the patient's status changed to admitted.A Kruskal-Wallis test compared time to assessment between the 2 groups and established that the difference was not statistically significant (P=0.121). However, the lower mean and median times to assessment in the postintervention group are clinically significant for this population.Automated notifications were effective in reducing delays in care and delivery of emergency equipment for this vulnerable population. ​.Copyright © 2026 Wolters Kluwer Health, LLC. llm_summary: Tracheostomy and laryngectomy patients require specialized emergency equipment and rapid assessment upon hospital admission, but delays in care delivery can occur due to communication failures in manual notification processes. Researchers implemented an automated electronic health record system that triggered pager notifications to respiratory therapists when these high-risk patients were admitted to the hospital. Analysis of retrospective data from three months before and after the intervention showed that the postintervention group had lower mean and median times to respiratory therapist assessment, though a Kruskal-Wallis test indicated this difference was not statistically significant (P=0.121). Despite the lack of statistical significance, the reduction in assessment delays observed after automation implementation may have clinical importance for this vulnerable patient population. The findings suggest that automated EHR notifications can help reduce delays in emergency equipment delivery, though further research with larger sample sizes may be needed to establish statistical significance.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers examined hospitalized adults with tracheostomy or laryngectomy, a low-volume high-risk population requiring specialized equipment and rapid assessment, by implementing an automated EHR-triggered pager notification system to alert respiratory therapists of newly admitted patients. The intervention was evaluated using retrospective data from a three-month baseline period compared to a postintervention period, with time to initial respiratory therapist assessment as the primary endpoint. A Kruskal-Wallis test comparing time to assessment between groups yielded a p-value of 0.121, indicating no statistically significant difference; however, the postintervention group demonstrated lower mean and median assessment times. Automated notifications were associated with reduced delays in care delivery and emergency equipment provision for this vulnerable population. The clinical significance of the observed time reductions requires consideration given the lack of statistical significance and the observational study design.

title: Astrocytic and Axonal Injury Biomarkers in AQP4 Antibody-Positive NMOSD: Insights From PREVENT and CHAMPION-NMOSD.
abstract: Glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) and neurofilament light chain (NfL) are biomarkers of astrocytic and axonal injury, respectively, in aquaporin-4 antibody-positive neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (AQP4-Ab+ NMOSD). We evaluated serum GFAP and NfL levels during treatment with complement component 5 inhibitors eculizumab or ravulizumab and examined associations between pretreatment biomarker levels, clinical characteristics, and on-trial relapse risk using samples from the PREVENT (eculizumab) and CHAMPION-NMOSD (ravulizumab) phase 3 trials.Serum GFAP and NfL levels were analyzed retrospectively in PREVENT and prospectively in CHAMPION-NMOSD and compared with levels in demographically matched external healthy donors. Associations between baseline clinical characteristics and high biomarker levels (≥2 SDs above the healthy donor mean) were evaluated using logistic regression with a test-and-validate strategy. Changes throughout treatment were assessed relative to pretreatment baseline. Biomarker changes associated with adjudicated on-trial relapses were examined. Associations between baseline biomarker levels and time to first adjudicated on-trial relapse were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analyses.Samples were available from 41 PREVENT and 55 CHAMPION-NMOSD patients. Pretreatment baseline GFAP and NfL levels were elevated in patients compared with healthy donors. High baseline GFAP levels were associated with older age at initial presentation, less time since last relapse, and higher baseline Hauser Ambulation Index (HAI) score. High baseline NfL levels were associated with older age and higher baseline HAI score. High baseline GFAP and NfL levels using age-adjusted Z-scores were evaluated and would not have materially changed the conclusions. The median GFAP levels declined rapidly (within 4-6 weeks) and were sustained with both eculizumab and ravulizumab. The median NfL levels declined significantly with ravulizumab but not eculizumab. In PREVENT, adjudicated on-trial relapses were associated with increased GFAP levels in placebo-treated patients, while GFAP increases were attenuated in eculizumab-treated patients.Serum GFAP and NfL levels are elevated in patients with NMOSD and are associated with clinical features of disability. Complement component 5 blockade biologically suppresses astrocytic injury in NMOSD, validating GFAP as a pharmacodynamic biomarker and mechanistic readout of target engagement in randomized phase 3 trials. This aligns with earlier findings across different compounds in separate phase 3 trials.

title: Building Anatomical Knowledge Competency for PGY-1 Readiness: Design, Implementation and Learner's Perception of A Year 4 Clinical Anatomy Elective.
abstract: Persistent gaps in anatomical knowledge among incoming residents have raised concerns about clinical preparedness, especially in surgical and interventional disciplines. Conventional anatomy instruction and limited cadaveric exposure and learning opportunities in medical curricula have prompted calls for innovative, clinically focused anatomical curricular integration in clinical training. This article describes the development, implementation, and impact of a tailored Year 4 Clinical Anatomy Elective in the Department of Clinical Anatomy at Mayo Clinic, designed to reinforce competency in clinically relevant anatomical understanding and support learners' perceived preparedness during transitions to residency. A 4-week elective was designed for fourth-year medical students interested in pursuing a specific residency program. The course was personalized for students' clinical interests and incorporated fresh tissue dissection, simulation, procedural skills training, and imaging using an immersive learning platform. The elective was structured within the experiential learning model using a guided, self-directed format within a multicapability laboratory and instructional environment, grounded in constructivist theory. A 5-year review of elective records and informal thematic analysis of student feedback were conducted. Most participants pursued surgically related specialties, with orthopedic surgery being the most common. Exploratory thematic analysis identified six core themes: Professional Identity Formation, Educational Benefits, Learning Challenges, Connection to Clinical Practice, Patient Care Implications, and Future Preparation and Transferability. These students perceived gains in areas aligned with ACGME milestones: increased confidence, greater preparedness for residency, and improvement in their ability to apply anatomical knowledge in clinical settings. This perception may be indicative of lifelong learning and early educator identity formation. A specialty-specific, clinically integrated anatomy elective may support learners' perceived preparedness for residency, reinforce clinically relevant anatomical understanding, and support the development of educational and professional competencies. Such targeted interventions may help address perceived gaps in anatomical preparedness during the transition to residency and contribute to postgraduate training within a competency-based medical education framework.© 2026 American Association of Clinical Anatomists and British Association of Clinical Anatomists.

title: Multi-ancestry genome-wide association meta-analysis of hepatocellular carcinoma identifies 15 risk loci including MAP3K9, DHRS1, MTTP, and 8q24.21.
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the third leading cause of cancer death globally, often arising on a background of cirrhosis. Here, we aimed to establish genetic drivers of all-cause HCC across ancestries in a large meta-analysis. We included 15 cohorts comprising 17,697 HCC affected individuals and 2,715,683 control subjects in this meta-analysis. We found 15 genome-wide significant (p < 5 × 10-8) germline loci, including in/near GCKR, MTTP, ADH5, 8q24.21 (nearest gene MYC), MAP3K9, and GABPB2, and a further two loci found on transcriptome- and regulome-wide association analyses. MAP3K9, TERT, and GABPB2 variants act independently of cirrhosis on both colocalization analysis and sensitivity analyses. There was significant ancestral heterogeneity in six loci including variants in the HLA locus that had divergent effects on HCC risk between East Asian and European ancestries. Fine mapping identified 11 potentially causal coding variants, including p.Leu446Pro (c.1337T>C) in GCKR and p.Asp423Glu (c.1269C>T) in MEN1. MEN1, 8q24.21 (nearest gene MYC), and TERT are all involved in the β-catenin pathway transactivation complex. Transcriptome-wide analysis identified enrichment of germline-encoded DHRS1 in HCC. Regulome-wide analysis replicated the germline signal for EPHA2 and found a chromatin-accessible region containing genes ZNF367 and HABP4. Finally, we demonstrated that population-level genetic architecture for HCC overlaps with steatotic and viral liver disease, and individuals with genetic risk for lower body mass index have higher risk of HCC. Genetic risk for HCC is determined by germline susceptibility to β-catenin pathway activation and cirrhosis. title: Nivolumab with doxorubicin, vinblastine, and dacarbazine in older adults with classic Hodgkin lymphoma: do S1826 results hold up in the real world?
abstract: Older adults (OA, ≥60 years) with classic Hodgkin lymphoma (cHL) have historically experienced inferior outcomes compared to younger patients. Nivolumab in combination with doxorubicin, vinblastine, and dacarbazine (NAVD) has demonstrated high efficacy in clinical trials, but real-world data in OA are limited. We conducted a multicenter retrospective study across 20 centers in patients with newly diagnosed advanced stage cHL treated with NAVD and analyzed outcomes in OA across the aging spectrum. Among 327 total patients, 81 (25%) were ≥60 years, with most OA presenting with stage IV disease (58%) and B symptoms (57%). Anygrade and ≥grade 3 AEs occurred in 88% and 67% of OA, respectively. Prophylactic growth factors were used in most OA (82%) which led to low rates of febrile neutropenia (12%) and infection (12%) despite 52% ≥grade 3 neutropenia. Immune-related AEs occurred in 29% (12% ≥grade 3) and treatment was discontinued due to toxicity in 10% of OA. Interim overall (ORR) and complete response rates (CRR) were 100% and 81.6%, end-of-treatment rates were 88% and 82.6%, respectively. At a median follow-up of 12.6 months, 1-year progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) in OA were 91.5% and 98.6%, respectively. OS was inferior in OA compared with patients.

title: Nicotine replacement therapy sampling for cigarette cessation in dental care: A National Dental Practice-Based Research Network cluster randomized clinical trial.
abstract: Cigarette smoking is detrimental to oral health. Oral health professionals rarely prescribe smoking cessation medications. Nicotine replacement therapy sampling (NRTS), providing brief starter courses of NRT, could improve provision of NRT and promote cessation. The aim of the Free Samples for Health (FreSH) study was to test the effectiveness of NRTS compared with enhanced usual care on long-term abstinence from combustible tobacco.Two-group, pragmatic, cluster (dental practice) randomized clinical trial.The study was conducted in the Midwest and Northeast nodes of the United States' National Dental Practice-Based Research Network in 59 dental practices. Practices were randomized to intervention condition.Participants (recruited June 2023-June 2025) were adult patients of network practices who smoke cigarettes daily [n = 1196; NRTS n = 486, comparison group (ET) n = 710; 59% female; 71% White].All participants received Ask-Advise-Refer: oral health practitioners asked smoking status, advised quitting and referred to state tobacco quitlines. Participants in the NRTS group were given a 2-week supply of 14 mg nicotine patches and 4 mg nicotine lozenges; participants in the ET group were given an electric toothbrush.Participants were surveyed after their visit and at 1, 3 and 6 months post enrollment. The primary outcome was 7-day point-prevalence abstinence measured 6 months post enrollment confirmed via expired breath carbon monoxide (CO) < 6 p.p.m. Secondary outcomes included quit attempts, short-term abstinence, NRT and quitline use. Covariates included stage of change, confidence, readiness and cigarettes per day.While there was no condition effect on CO-confirmed abstinence at 6 months post intervention [NRTS: 8.4%, ET: 8.0%; adjusted odds ratio (aOR) = 1.04, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 0.65-2.09], the NRTS intervention statistically significantly increased NRT use across all timepoints (NRTS: 50%, ET: 13%; aOR = 7.39, 95% CI = 5.29-10.31) and quit attempts at all timepoints (NRTS: 58%, ET: 49%; aOR = 1.46, 95% CI = 1.06-2.02). There was a statistically significant effect of NRTS on self-reported 7-day point-prevalence abstinence at 1 month post enrollment (NRTS: 12.8%, ET: 9.0%; aOR = 1.72, 95% CI = 1.03-2.88). There was no difference in quitline use. Practices assigned to the NRTS condition recruited notably fewer participants (t = 2.11, P = 0.04).Free nicotine replacement therapy (NRT) samples are not sufficient to improve long-term smoking abstinence in dental patients; however, NRT samples increase engagement with quitting behaviors and may serve as a starting point toward quitting. title: Metacarpophalangeal Arthroplasty: A 14-Year Nationwide Analysis of Trends and Acute Perioperative Outcomes in Rheumatoid Arthritis and Osteoarthritis.
abstract: Metacarpophalangeal (MCP) arthroplasty is an established surgical option for end-stage MCP arthritis. We analyzed trends in case volumes and 30-day perioperative outcomes after MCP arthroplasty performed for rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and osteoarthritis (OA).We used the National Surgical Quality Improvement Program database to identify all MCP arthroplasties performed for RA (n = 216) or OA (n = 452) between 2010 and 2023. Bivariate analysis was used to compare patient demographics, operative characteristics, and 30-day outcomes. We analyzed temporal trends in case volumes using Poisson regression models and trends in patient characteristics using linear regression.Patients with RA were more likely to be female (85% vs 54%) and have a history of smoking (22% vs 10%) and chronic steroid use (58% vs 4%). Patients with OA had more prevalent comorbidities including obesity, diabetes, and hypertension. Patients with RA more frequently required multi-joint replacement, concomitant soft tissue balancing procedures, plastic surgery involvement, and inpatient admission. The annual case volume for OA increased at +5.9% per year (P < .001), whereas the volume for RA remained steady. The outpatient case volume grew at a rate of +4.6% per year (P < .001). Both groups had similarly low rates of 30-day complications (0.9% RA, 1.8% OA), readmission (0.5% RA, 1.5% OA), and reoperation (0% RA, 0.9% OA).Despite distinct patient profiles and operative complexity, both OA and RA patients experience low rates of perioperative adverse events after MCP arthroplasty. Osteoarthritis is a growing indication for this procedure, which is increasingly being performed in the outpatient setting.

title: Pregnancy Outcomes, Placenta Histopathology and Immunohistochemistry in Patients with a History of Recurrent Pregnancy Loss or Implantation Failure Undergoing In Vitro Fertilization.
abstract: To evaluate pregnancy outcomes, placental histopathology, and placental immune markers in pregnancies after in vitro fertilization (IVF) with a history of recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL) or recurrent implantation failure (RIF).Retrospective cohort study.Single academic center.Patients who underwent IVF with a history of RPL or RIF and age- and body mass index (BMI)-matched spontaneous pregnancies and IVF patients without a history of RPL or RIF between 2018 and 2023.IVF with a history of RPL or RIF.Placental histopathology, placental immunohistochemical markers.Among 2,215 IVF cycles, 407 resulted in live births within our hospital system. We analyzed 325 IVF patients (52 with RPL, 30 with RIF and 243 without RPL/RIF) and 197 patients with spontaneous pregnancies as a reference group. Placental histopathology was available for 283 patients and immunohistochemistry (IHC) was conducted on 133 samples. After adjusting for maternal age and BMI, and correcting for multiple comparisons, pregnancies in the IVF-no RPL/RIF group had statistically increased incidence of postpartum hemorrhage, and a trend towards preeclampsia was observed in the IVF-RPL group. In placental histopathology, increased incidence of fetal vascular malperfusion, inflammatory lesions such as chronic villitis, and intervillous thrombi was noted in IVF pregnancies, especially in IVF-RPL group. IHC analysis showed significantly higher numbers of CD163+ and CD68+ placental macrophages in all IVF groups, and markedly high CD163+ cells in IVF-RIF group. IL-6 levels did not differ between groups.IVF pregnancies, especially in patients with a history of RPL or RIF, are associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes and distinct placental histopathology, and elevated placental macrophages. These findings highlight the importance of individualized counseling and prenatal/postnatal surveillance although additional work is needed in larger multicenter cohorts to fully establish the pathophysiological association.Copyright © 2026. title: Safety and Efficacy of Repeat Surgery for Recurrent Craniopharyngiomas: A RAPID Consortium Collaboration.
abstract: Craniopharyngiomas (CPs) recur in 20% to 50% of cases after initial management. To date, there are no large multi-institutional series investigating outcomes in patients receiving surgery for recurrent CP. Here, we leverage the Registry of Adenomas of the Pituitary and Related Disorders to analyze outcomes after surgical treatment of recurrent CP.Demographic, clinical, radiographic, surgical, and outcome variables were analyzed for 483 patients receiving surgery for primary or recurrent CP across 16 US-based academic skull-base centers comprising the Registry of Adenomas of the Pituitary and Related Disorders consortium from 2000 to 2024.Among the 483 patients, 360 (74.5%) had primary CP and 123 (25.5%) had recurrent CP. The recurrent cohort was younger at initial diagnosis (Padj < .01) and recurrence (Padj = .02). Adamantinomatous CPs were more common in the recurrent cohort but not significantly so, and 33.3% of cases had prior radiation therapy. Recurrent cases had more frequent preoperative endocrine dysfunction and hormone replacement (Padj < .01). Patients with recurrent CP had less frequent suprasellar tumor extension (Padj = .04) and more frequent preinfundibular/transinfundibular over retroinfundibular localization (Padj = .02). There were no differences in operative approach; endoscopic endonasal surgery was the most common, and procedures achieved similar distributions of gross and subtotal resection in both cohorts (Padj = .30) with similar low frequencies of unplanned reoperation and surgical complications. New postoperative arginine vasopressin deficiency (in patients without preoperative arginine vasopressin deficiency) was more common in the primary cohort (Padj = .04), but long-term follow-up demonstrated similar frequencies of endocrine dysfunction in both cohorts and comparably low rates (<25%) of future recurrence within an average follow-up period of 1.57 years (Padj= .17).This study provides the largest comparative evaluation of patients undergoing surgery for recurrent vs primary CP. Despite prior treatment, patients with recurrent CP achieved comparable resection outcomes with similar rates of neuroendocrine dysfunction. These findings indicate surgical resection remains a safe and efficacious option for recurrent CP, especially as emerging targeted therapies become available.Copyright © Congress of Neurological Surgeons 2026. title: Diabetes Severity in Cornea Donors and 1-Year Outcomes in Recipients in the Diabetes Endothelial Keratoplasty Study: A Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Clinical Trial.
abstract: The effect of cornea donor diabetes severity on graft success, endothelial cell density (ECD), and morphometry after Descemet membrane endothelial keratoplasty (DMEK) is not known.To determine whether graft success, corneal endothelial cell loss (ECL), and morphometric changes 1 year after DMEK are associated with cornea donor diabetes severity measured by severity score, donor's postmortem level of hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c), and postmortem advanced glycation end products (AGEs) or advanced oxidation end products (AOPs).This was a secondary analysis of a multicenter, double-masked, randomized clinical trial at 28 clinical sites (46 surgeons) and 13 eye banks in the US among individuals undergoing low- to moderate-risk DMEK. AGE and AOP measurements were collected from a subset of donors. Data analysis was conducted from September 1, 2025, through April 30, 2026.DMEK performed with a cornea from a donor without or with diabetes, assigned using a minimization procedure (comparable to randomization) to achieve an approximate 2:1 distribution, respectively.Graft success, ECL, coefficient of variation (CV) of cell area, and percentage of hexagonal cells (HEX) at 1 year from eye bank and postoperative specular central endothelial images.A total of 1097 individuals (1421 study eyes; median [IQR] age, 71 [66-76] years; 631 [57.5%] female) undergoing low- to moderate-risk DMEK (1044 [95.2%] for Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy) were included. AGE and AOP measurements were collected from a subset of 472 donors (542 study donor corneas). Among 968 eyes with a postmortem donor HbA1c level lower than 6.5%, the 1-year graft success rate was 97.1% (95% CI, 95.4%-98.4%), compared with 97.4% (95% CI, 93.9%-100.0%), 93.0% (95% CI, 83.3%-98.8%), and 95.8% (95% CI, 87.3%-100.0%) among eyes with a donor HbA1c level of 6.5% to less than 7.5% (n = 194), 7.5% to less than 9.0% (n = 86), and 9.0% or higher (n = 48), respectively (P = .72). There was no significant difference in mean ECD across donor HbA1c groups. Donor diabetes severity measured with severity score, donor HbA1c level, and AGE and AOP metrics was not associated with 1-year graft failure, ECD, CV in cell area, or HEX percentage.This secondary analysis of a randomized clinical trial found that ECL and morphometry 1 year after DMEK were not affected by cornea donor diabetes severity. Comparable 1-year graft success, ECL, and cell morphometrics with tissue from donors with and without diabetes, regardless of the diabetes severity biomarker values observed, support the use of corneas from donors with diabetes for endothelial keratoplasty procedures without additional preoperative testing or risk stratification based on the diabetes status of the cornea donor.ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05134480.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether corneas from donors with diabetes would perform differently after transplantation compared to those from donors without diabetes, since diabetes can damage cells over time through processes like glycation. In this secondary analysis of a randomized trial involving 1,097 patients receiving corneal transplants (DMEK procedure) at 28 clinical sites, corneas were assigned from donors with varying levels of diabetes severity, measured by blood sugar control markers and chemical damage indicators. One year after transplant, graft success rates were similar across all donor diabetes severity groups, ranging from 93.0% to 97.4%, with no significant differences in endothelial cell loss or cell shape changes (P = . 72). These findings suggest that corneal tissue from donors with diabetes, regardless of how severe their diabetes was, performed comparably to tissue from donors without diabetes in supporting transplant success.
llm_summary_expert: This secondary analysis of a multicenter randomized clinical trial examined 1097 individuals (1421 eyes) undergoing low- to moderate-risk Descemet membrane endothelial keratoplasty (DMEK), comparing outcomes between corneas from donors with and without diabetes. Graft success, endothelial cell density (ECD), endothelial cell loss (ECL), coefficient of variation in cell area, and percentage of hexagonal cells were assessed at 1 year using specular microscopy. One-year graft success rates were 97.1% (95% CI, 95.4%-98.4%) for donor postmortem hemoglobin A1c levels lower than 6.5% and 93.0% (95% CI, 83.3%-98.8%) for levels of 7.5% to less than 9.0%, with no significant difference across groups (P = . 72). Donor diabetes severity measured by severity score, postmortem HbA1c level, and advanced glycation end products or advanced oxidation end products was not associated with 1-year graft failure.

title: Certainty may remain the best term for GRADE evidence ratings despite conceptual limitations: a commentary.
abstract: The Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach initially described its ratings as confidence in an effect estimate. Current applications retain this focus while specifying the inference of interest, such as whether the true effect lies above or below a decision-relevant threshold. The terminology later changed from "quality of evidence" to "certainty of evidence."GRADE reports four ordered levels-high, moderate, low, and very low-of support for an outcome- and inference-specific conclusion. Ordinary English may give certainty an all-or-none state, but technical attributes permit gradation. We compare certainty, quality, confidence, strength, and trustworthiness through their strengths and limitations. None resolves the tension without adding another concern.In the absence of a superior alternative, certainty may remain the most practical term because it is established in guidance, teaching, software, and practice. It should be defined as an ordered judgment about support for a specified inference, not as proof.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.

llm_summary: The GRADE approach uses standardized terminology to communicate how confident researchers and clinicians should be in evidence supporting clinical recommendations, with ratings ranging from high to very low certainty. The authors examined five candidate terms—certainty, quality, confidence, strength, and trustworthiness—to evaluate which best describes GRADE's four-level rating system for evidence supporting outcome-specific conclusions. Each term carries both strengths and limitations, and no single alternative fully resolves the conceptual tensions inherent in communicating gradations of evidence support. The authors conclude that "certainty" remains the most practical term despite its conceptual limitations, primarily because it is already established in GRADE guidance, educational materials, software tools, and clinical practice. The term should be understood as an ordered judgment about the degree of support for a specified inference rather than as absolute proof.
llm_summary_expert: The GRADE approach uses an ordered four-level rating system—high, moderate, low, and very low—to assess certainty of evidence for outcome- and inference-specific conclusions. The authors compared five candidate terms (certainty, quality, confidence, strength, and trustworthiness) to evaluate their conceptual strengths and limitations for describing these evidence ratings. Each alternative term presented distinct advantages and disadvantages without fully resolving the inherent tension between technical gradation and ordinary language interpretation. The authors concluded that certainty remains the most practical term despite its conceptual limitations, primarily because it is already established in GRADE guidance, teaching materials, software, and clinical practice. Certainty should be defined as an ordered judgment about support for a specified inference rather than as proof.

title: Technology-Supported Solutions to Improve Guideline-Informed Care for Kidney Disease: Conclusions from a Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) Controversies Conference.
abstract: Implementation of guideline-informed care for the prevention, detection, and management of kidney disease remains suboptimal throughout the world. In November 2025, Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) held a Controversies Conference on the role of technology-supported solutions to improve guideline-informed care for people with or at risk for kidney disease and to identify priorities for research. There have been rapid advances in various technologies for earlier identification of people with kidney disease; risk stratification for adverse kidney, cardiovascular, and other clinical and patient-centered outcomes; and promotion of guideline-informed therapies, monitoring, and patient self-management. Still, there remain important considerations for how to optimize the use of such technologies for achieving care that is integrated, personalized, safe, and guideline-informed. The conference identified a range of lived experience, clinician, health care system, health policy, and technology-level factors that can influence the effectiveness of technology-supported solutions in improving guideline-informed care. Research priorities included developing and maintaining living guidelines; harmonizing and integrating guideline recommendations into clinical decision support solutions; generating evidence on the effectiveness and safety of technology-supported solutions that reduce disparities and preserve trust; developing and evaluating efforts that promote interoperability, feasibility and scalability of technologies across health care systems; developing more effective public-private partnerships and systematic use of validated health technology assessments; and clarifying the incremental value of emerging technologies involving sensor-derived biomarkers and integrated multimodal data. Strategies to optimize digital health technologies for promoting guideline-informed care were also delineated.Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Inc.

llm_summary: A KDIGO Controversies Conference in November 2025 examined how technology-supported solutions could improve the implementation of kidney disease guidelines, which remain suboptimal globally despite established clinical recommendations. The conference brought together experts to identify rapid advances in technologies for early detection of kidney disease, risk stratification for adverse outcomes, and promotion of guideline-informed treatments and patient self-management. Participants recognized that multiple factors—including patient experiences, clinician perspectives, health system infrastructure, policy considerations, and technology design—influence whether technology-supported solutions effectively improve guideline-informed care. The conference established research priorities including the development of living guidelines, integration of guideline recommendations into clinical decision support systems, generation of evidence on technology effectiveness and safety that reduces health disparities, and clarification of the added value of emerging technologies such as sensor-derived biomarkers. Future work should focus on optimizing digital health technologies to promote guideline-informed care while addressing interoperability, feasibility, and scalability across diverse health care systems.

title: Predictive Accuracy and Procedural Benefits of Software-Enhanced Flow-Diverter Planning: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Flow-diverting (FD) stents play a critical role in the management of complex intracranial aneurysms. Successful FD stent deployment requires precise planning to minimize peri- and postprocedural complications. This traditionally relied on physician expertise for precise planning; however, software simulations now offer estimative modeling.This systematic review and meta-analysis compares physician and software simulations for predicting stent deployment and assesses the clinical impact of software integration on procedural metrics.We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus (articles through July 18, 2025) using Nested Knowledge Autolit. The search combined Medical Subject Headings (MeSH) terms and keywords and followed updated Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. A manual review of the reference lists was performed to identify gray literature.Fourteen studies were included. All studies that involved comparative data, a physician, and software/simulation tool regarding intracranial aneurysms with outcomes relating to accuracy metrics, interobserver agreement or apposition, or procedural metrics were included.All data were analyzed using R, Version 4.5.2, and the "meta" package. Risk of bias (RoB) assessment was completed using the ROBINS-I tool for procedural metric-related studies and the COSMIN-based checklist for accuracy/agreement-related studies.The pooled analysis found software-predicted stent length to be shorter than the physicians' predicted length (mean difference [MD], 2.88 mm; 95% CI, 1.25-4.51), without a statistically significant difference in diameter (MD, 0.00 mm; 95% CI, -0.09 to 0.09); software-chosen dimensions were accurate to the postimplantation length (MD, -1.40 mm; 95% CI, -3.56 to 0.76) and diameter (MD, 0.17 mm; 95% CI, -0.63 to 0.97); software-assisted cases were associated with shorter procedure duration (MD, 9.91 min; 95% CI, 1.23-18.58), lower radiation dose (MD 305.52 mGy [172.14, 438.90]), and fewer corrective interventions (OR 3.44 [1.78, 6.64]); and there was no significant difference in hemorrhagic complications (OR 1.67 [0.65, 4.28]) and postoperative aneurysm occlusion (OR 0.52 [0.07, 3.78]).Given the retrospective nature and bias limitations of current literature, further prospective, randomized studies are warranted to better assess the clinical impact of simulation software in the endovascular treatment of intracranial aneurysms.The findings in this paper provide preliminary evidence to support integration of virtual simulation software in the preprocedural FD treatment planning.© 2026 by American Journal of Neuroradiology.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether computer software simulations could improve the planning and outcomes of flow-diverter stent placement for complex brain aneurysms by comparing software predictions to physician estimates across fourteen studies. The meta-analysis found that software predicted shorter stent lengths than physicians by an average of 2.88 mm, though software-selected dimensions ultimately matched the actual implanted stent size accurately and showed no significant difference in diameter predictions. Software-assisted procedures were associated with shorter operative times (9.91 minutes faster), lower radiation exposure (305.52 mGy reduction), and fewer corrective interventions needed during the procedure (3.44 times lower odds), with no significant differences in bleeding complications or aneurysm closure rates. These findings suggest that integrating virtual simulation software into preprocedural planning may offer practical procedural benefits, though the current evidence comes primarily from retrospective studies with inherent bias limitations. The authors recommend conducting prospective, randomized controlled trials to more rigorously establish whether software-assisted planning truly improves clinical outcomes in endovascular aneurysm treatment.

title: Volumetric changes in articulating interpositional spacers for two-stage temporomandibular joint arthroplasty. A pilot study.
abstract: Two-stage temporomandibular joint (TMJ) arthroplasty may involve the placement of a spacer until a final prosthesis is placed. In cases where a patient is not immobilized via intermaxillary fixation (IMF), the spacer is considered to be articulating, and the patient can open their mouth and function more normally during this interval. This study was designed to retrospectively assess the volumetric changes of the spacer within the temporomandibular joint following the use of an articulating bone cement spacer in a two-stage reconstruction. Fourteen patients (thirteen females, one male with mean ± SD age of 58.1 ± 13.0 years underwent two-stage TMJ reconstruction with an articulating spacer. The mean duration of the spacer retention was 142.1 ± 58.4 days. The median volume change of the temporomandibular joint spacer was quantified. Longer retention of the spacer was significantly associated with greater volume change (P = 0.011). There was no impact on prosthesis fit or occlusion at the time of surgery, and prosthesis outcomes were good. This study indicates that the duration of retention of the articulating bone cement spacer in the TMJ influences the amount of spacer volumetric changes, although the amount of change does not appear to be clinically significant.Copyright © 2026 International Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons. llm_summary: Two-stage temporomandibular joint arthroplasty sometimes requires placement of a temporary spacer between surgical stages, and articulating spacers allow patients to function normally without jaw immobilization during this interval. Researchers retrospectively examined volumetric changes in bone cement spacers placed in the temporomandibular joints of fourteen patients (thirteen female, one male; mean age 58.1 years) who underwent two-stage TMJ reconstruction, with spacers retained for a mean duration of 142.1 days. The study found that longer retention of the spacer was significantly associated with greater volumetric change (P = 0.011), indicating that spacers gradually decreased in volume over time. Despite these measurable volumetric changes, the spacer degradation did not negatively impact the fit of the final prosthesis, occlusion, or surgical outcomes, which were rated as good. Although duration of spacer retention influences the amount of volumetric change observed, the clinical significance of these changes appears minimal based on the prosthesis outcomes reported in this pilot study.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers examined volumetric changes in articulating bone cement spacers placed during two-stage temporomandibular joint arthroplasty in 14 patients (13 female, 1 male; mean age 58.1 years) who were not immobilized via intermaxillary fixation. Prosthesis fit, occlusion, and surgical outcomes were unaffected by spacer volume changes. Although spacer retention duration correlated with volumetric changes, the magnitude of change did not appear clinically significant.

title: Prognostic and Predictive Effect of Age in Molecularly Defined Lower-Grade Gliomas.
abstract: Age ≥40 years is regarded as a high-risk feature and an indication for adjuvant chemoradiotherapy for patients with lower-grade glioma in clinical practice guidelines. It is unclear whether age remains a relevant prognostic factor for contemporary definitions of lower-grade gliomas in the molecular era.The Prospective Gliomas Research (PROGRES) database contains individual patient-level data from 11 prospective clinical trials or observational registries of histologically defined lower-grade 2-3 oligodendroglioma or astrocytoma. We determined the association of age (18-39 years v ≥40 years) with progression-free survival (PFS) stratified by isocitrate dehydrogenase 1 or 2 (IDH1/2) status, using log-rank tests and Cox regression models. We validated our findings in a separate multi-institutional retrospective cohort (Retrospective Glioma Research [REGRES] database).We identified 1,619 and 1,292 eligible patients in the PROGRES and REGRES cohorts, respectively. IDH-wildtype tumors were more common in patients 40 years and older (38% v 5%, odds ratio: 11.3 [95% CI, 6.5 to 19.7]). Age was associated with PFS in IDH-wildtype (5-year PFS for ≥40 v 18-39 years: 6% v 24%, hazard ratio [HR], 1.74 [95% CI, 1.21 to 2.50]) but not in IDH-mutant glioma (60% v 59%, HR, 0.89 [95% CI, 0.76 to 1.05], Pinteraction < .001). In IDH-wildtype tumors, older age predicted aggressive molecular features, including TERT promoter mutation (65% v 28%), EGFR amplification (41% v 15%), and chromosome +7/-10 alteration (57% v 25%). In a pooled analysis of four clinical trials, age was not predictive of a benefit from chemoradiotherapy versus radiotherapy alone for IDH-mutant glioma.In the absence of additional clinical or molecular risk factors, age alone should not be considered an indication for administration or deferral of adjuvant treatment. Practice guidelines should be revised to reflect contemporary prognostic factors in the molecular era.

llm_summary: Age 40 years and older has traditionally been considered a high-risk feature warranting aggressive treatment for lower-grade gliomas, but it remains unclear whether this classification holds true with modern molecular tumor classification. title: Addition of Metastasis-Directed Therapy to Standard of Care for Oligometastatic Disease: Primary Aggregated Analysis of All Baskets from the Phase II Randomized EXTEND Trial.
abstract: We tested the hypothesis that adding metastasis-directed therapy (MDT) to standard-of-care (SOC) systemic therapy improves progression-free survival (PFS) among patients with oligometastatic disease.EXTEND was a multicenter randomized phase II trial. Patients with 1-5 metastases were randomly assigned to MDT + SOC versus SOC in one of the six baskets (breast, pancreas, kidney, two prostate baskets, and an other basket) with basket-specific stratification and powering. PFS, the primary end point, was prespecified in the per-protocol set within each basket, across all baskets, and across all baskets excluding the prostate baskets. Exploratory end points included circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) and immune profiling.From 2018 through 2023, 521 patients were screened, 350 were randomly assigned, and 334 were analyzed per protocol (MDT + SOC, n = 166; SOC, n = 168). Radiotherapy was used as MDT for 98% of metastases (370/379). Overall, after a median follow-up of 53 months, PFS was improved with MDT + SOC (hazard ratio [HR], 0.54 [95% CI, 0.41 to 0.72], P < .001). Similarly, PFS was improved when excluding the prostate baskets (HR, 0.60 [95% CI, 0.40 to 0.89]). Within each basket, PFS superiority was identified for the pancreas, prostate, and other baskets, whereas the breast and kidney baskets were inconclusive. At enrollment, detectable ctDNA correlated with shorter PFS and survival; by contrast, ctDNA clearance 3 months postenrollment correlated with improved survival. MDT + SOC-induced systemic immune activation was most pronounced among baskets demonstrating PFS superiority.The phase II EXTEND trial supports the addition of MDT to SOC for oligometastatic disease. Histology-specific efficacy signals were identified for phase III testing. Translational insights suggest the potential for optimizing the definition of oligometastasis using ctDNA and point to systemic immune responses as a possible mechanism of benefit from MDT.

llm_summary: The EXTEND trial investigated whether adding metastasis-directed therapy (MDT), primarily radiotherapy, to standard systemic treatment could improve progression-free survival in patients with oligometastatic disease, defined as 1-5 metastases across six cancer types. Among 334 patients analyzed per protocol (166 receiving MDT plus standard care versus 168 receiving standard care alone), the combination approach significantly improved progression-free survival with a hazard ratio of 0.54 (95% CI, 0.41 to 0.72; P < . 001) after a median follow-up of 53 months. Benefit was observed in pancreatic, prostate, and other cancer types, while results were inconclusive for breast and kidney cancers, suggesting that treatment efficacy may depend on cancer histology. Circulating tumor DNA clearance at three months post-enrollment correlated with improved survival, and patients receiving MDT plus standard care showed enhanced systemic immune activation, pointing to immune mechanisms as a potential source of benefit.
llm_summary_expert: The EXTEND trial randomized 334 patients with 1-5 metastases across six disease baskets to receive metastasis-directed therapy plus standard-of-care systemic therapy (MDT + SOC, n = 166) or SOC alone (n = 168), with progression-free survival as the primary endpoint assessed per protocol within and across baskets. Radiotherapy comprised 98% of metastasis-directed interventions, and median follow-up was 53 months. Overall, MDT + SOC improved PFS compared with SOC (hazard ratio 0.54, 95% CI 0.41–0.72, P < . 001), with similar benefit excluding prostate baskets (HR 0.60, 95% CI 0.40–0.89). PFS superiority was identified in pancreas, prostate, and other baskets, whereas breast and kidney baskets showed inconclusive results.

title: Omitting Bone Marrow Sampling in FDG-Avid Rhabdomyosarcoma With 2-[18F]FDG PET-Negative Marrow: Results From an International Retrospective Study.
abstract: Detection of bone marrow disease has been a major component of rhabdomyosarcoma (RMS) staging with bilateral bone marrow aspirates/biopsies (BMAB) from the iliac crests considered the diagnostic gold standard. This study's goal was to determine if 2-18F-labeled fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography ([18F]FDG PET/CT) or PET/magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) may replace BMAB in RMS staging.Patients were recruited in Europe and North America. Medical records, FDG PET/CT or FDG PET/MRI (PET), and BMAB reports were collected retrospectively. Images were re-reviewed by nuclear medicine physicians at the patients' home institutions if PET reports indicated increased FDG uptake at bone/bone marrow sites or if tumor cells were detected in bone marrow samples.PET imaging and BMAB were performed before chemotherapy and tumor resection in 301 patients with FDG-avid RMS. Bone marrow metastases were detected by PET and BMAB in 54, by PET only in 24, and by BMAB only in one of 301 patients with FDG-avid primary tumors. Absence of bone marrow metastases was confirmed by PET and BMAB in 222 of 301 patients. These observations translated into 98% sensitivity and 90% specificity for PET in detecting bone marrow metastases when BMAB was considered as gold standard. FDG-avid marrow disease was patchy (1-5 foci) in one third of cases. Patients with marrow disease indicated by PET and BMAB had more FDG-avid bone marrow foci, more metastatic sites, and lower survival than those with marrow disease indicated by PET only, suggesting more advanced disease stages.Bone marrow sampling may be omitted in patients without evidence of FDG-avid bone marrow disease by PET. If there are FDG-avid bone marrow lesions, further investigation by MRI and/or biopsy should be considered.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether PET imaging could replace bone marrow biopsies in staging rhabdomyosarcoma, a childhood cancer, by retrospectively collecting imaging and biopsy data from 301 patients across Europe and North America who had FDG-avid primary tumors. PET imaging detected bone marrow metastases in 54 patients confirmed by biopsy and in 24 additional patients where biopsy showed no disease, while biopsy alone detected metastases in only one patient, yielding 98% sensitivity and 90% specificity for PET compared to biopsy as the reference standard. Patients with bone marrow disease confirmed by both PET and biopsy had more extensive disease with multiple metastatic sites and lower survival rates than those with disease detected by PET alone, suggesting these groups represented different disease stages. The findings suggest that bone marrow sampling may be safely omitted in patients without evidence of FDG-avid bone marrow disease on PET imaging, though further investigation with MRI and biopsy should be considered when FDG-avid bone marrow lesions are present. This retrospective study provides evidence.
