PET imaging and BMAB were performed before chemotherapy and tumor resection, with images re-reviewed by nuclear medicine physicians when indicated. Bone marrow metastases were detected by both modalities in 54 patients, by PET only in 24 patients, and by BMAB only in 1 patient, with 222 patients showing absence of marrow disease on both tests, yielding 98% sensitivity and 90% specificity for PET when BMAB was considered the gold standard. FDG-avid marrow disease was patchy with 1-5 foci in one-third of cases, and patients with disease detected by both PET and BMAB had more FDG-avid bone marrow foci and lower survival.

title: Phase I/II Study of Bavdegalutamide, a Proteolysis-Targeting Chimera Androgen Receptor Degrader, in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer.
abstract: This phase I/II study (which, to our knowledge, is the first such study in humans) evaluated the safety and efficacy of bavdegalutamide (ARV-110), a proteolysis-targeting chimera (PROTAC) androgen receptor (AR) degrader, in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC).Eligible patients were adult (18 years and older) males with mCRPC previously treated with an AR pathway inhibitor (ARPI). In phase I, patients received escalating doses of oral bavdegalutamide to determine the recommended phase II dose (RP2D). In phase II, patients received bavdegalutamide at the RP2D in 28-day cycles. Antitumor activity, including prostate-specific antigen (PSA) response rate (≥50% [PSA50] or ≥30% [PSA30] decline from baseline) and radiographic progression-free survival (rPFS), was assessed in three AR molecular profile-defined subgroups and a less-pretreated (one prior ARPI without prior chemotherapy) subgroup.In phase I (N = 95), bavdegalutamide 420 mg once daily was the RP2D. In phase II, PSA50 and PSA30 rates, respectively, were 60.0% and 70.0% among patients with tumors harboring AR T878 and/or H875 mutations (n = 20), 4.3% and 6.5% among those with wild-type AR or other AR alterations (n = 46), and 3.1% and 6.3% among those with AR L702H mutations or AR splice variant 7 expression (n = 32); the median rPFS was 11.1, 4.2, and 5.1 months in the respective subgroups. Among less-pretreated patients (n = 42), the PSA50 rate was 21.4%, the PSA30 rate was 23.8%, and the median rPFS was 11.1 months. Among phase II patients (n = 144), 72.3% experienced grade 1/2 treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) and 17.4% experienced grade 3 TRAEs; no grade ≥4 TRAEs occurred. TRAEs led to dose reduction and discontinuation in 11.8% and 11.1% of patients, respectively.Bavdegalutamide had a manageable safety profile and showed promising clinical activity in patients with mCRPC, particularly those with tumors harboring AR T878/H875 mutations.

title: VAV1 targeting for cancer therapeutics: mechanistic understanding and preclinical promise.
abstract: Vav1, although mainly expressed in hematopoietic cells where it participates in the regulation of signaling pathways downstream of numerous cell surface receptors, has been found mutated and ectopically expressed in many human cancers where it drives tumor proliferation. Thus, mechanisms aimed at targeting Vav1 could have therapeutic benefit in cancers where it is aberrantly expressed in either a wild type or mutant form.This review describes and summarizes the expanding cellular and molecular mechanisms by which Vav1 contributes to tumor development, proliferation and survival in human cancers within and outside the hematopoietic lineages. We will discuss the emerging role of Vav1 as an oncogenic driver in many human tumors and the current studies aimed at identifying various therapeutics to target this protein and the pathways it regulates.Targeting Vav1 comes with several challenges due to its role in regulating signaling in immune cells, so any small molecule or other approaches need to balance targeting this molecule in cancer and sparing effects on the immune system where it might be participating in a positive role in anti-tumor immunity. Furthermore, the role of the other Vav family members in Vav1-expressing or mutated cancer needs to be addressed.

llm_summary: Vav1, a protein normally expressed in immune cells where it regulates signaling from cell surface receptors, has been found mutated and abnormally expressed in many human cancers where it promotes tumor growth. This review examines the cellular and molecular mechanisms by which Vav1 contributes to tumor development, proliferation, and survival across both hematopoietic and non-hematopoietic cancers, and discusses its emerging role as an oncogenic driver in human tumors. The authors summarize current therapeutic approaches aimed at targeting Vav1 and the signaling pathways it regulates as potential cancer treatments. A significant challenge in developing Vav1-targeting therapies is balancing the need to inhibit the protein in cancer cells while preserving its positive role in immune cells that fight tumors. Future research must also clarify how other members of the Vav protein family contribute to cancers where Vav1 is expressed or mutated.
llm_summary_expert: Vav1, a guanine nucleotide exchange factor predominantly expressed in hematopoietic cells, has been identified as mutated and ectopically expressed in multiple human cancers where it functions as an oncogenic driver promoting tumor proliferation and survival. This review synthesizes cellular and molecular mechanisms by which Vav1 contributes to tumor development across hematopoietic and non-hematopoietic lineages and examines emerging therapeutic strategies targeting this protein and its regulated signaling pathways. Therapeutic targeting of Vav1 presents a critical challenge: interventions must selectively inhibit Vav1 in cancer cells while preserving its physiological role in immune cells, where it may contribute to anti-tumor immunity. The therapeutic approach must also account for potential compensatory functions of other Vav family members in cancers expressing wild-type or mutant Vav1. These considerations necessitate careful preclinical and clinical evaluation to balance efficacy against immunological toxicity.

title: Use of Anticoagulation Among Patients With Atrial Fibrillation or Atrial Flutter in the United States.
abstract: Oral anticoagulation (OAC) remains underused in patients with atrial fibrillation or flutter at high risk of ischemic stroke. We aimed to characterize documented OAC prescribing at diagnosis and during 1-year follow-up and identify factors associated with baseline OAC prescribing.Using electronic health records from 7 US health systems participating in the National Patient-Centered Clinical Research Network between 2015 and 2019, we identified patients with newly diagnosed atrial fibrillation at high risk of ischemic stroke (CHA2DS2-VASc score ≥2 for men or ≥3 for women). The primary outcomes were documented OAC prescription at baseline and during 1-year follow-up. Exposures included demographic, clinical, and health-system characteristics. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with baseline OAC prescribing and loss of documented OAC prescribing during follow-up.Among 161 295 patients (median age, 76 years [interquartile range, 68-82]; 70 327 [43.6%] women), 92 518 (57.4%) had a documented OAC prescription at baseline, increasing from 56.6% in 2015 to 62.6% in 2019. Among those with a documented baseline OAC prescription, 45.6% had no documented OAC prescription during 1-year follow-up. Among 68 777 patients without a documented baseline OAC prescription, 12.5% had an OAC prescription documented during follow-up. Dementia (odds ratio, 0.58 [95% CI, 0.56-0.61]), prior major bleeding (odds ratio, 0.69 [95% CI, 0.63-0.75]), and renal disease (odds ratio, 0.84 [95% CI, 0.81-0.88]) were associated with lower odds of baseline OAC prescribing, whereas heart failure was associated with higher odds (odds ratio, 1.40 [95% CI, 1.37-1.43]).Among patients with newly diagnosed atrial fibrillation at high risk for ischemic stroke, OAC prescribing at diagnosis was suboptimal, and loss of documented OAC prescribing was common during the first year. title: Association Between Early Postoperative Limb Symmetry Index Scores and 2-Year Patient-Reported Outcomes After Quadriceps Tendon Autograft ACL Reconstruction.
abstract: The limb symmetry index (LSI) is a measure comparing strength and functional movement between the surgical and nonsurgical limbs, used after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) to guide rehabilitation and assess return-to-sport readiness. With increasing use of the quadriceps tendon autograft (QT-ACLR), limited data exist on whether the LSI score correlates with patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs).To evaluate the predictive value of postoperative strength and functional LSI tests at 3, 6, and 9 months for short-term PROMs, determine Patient Acceptable Symptom State (PASS) thresholds, and assess differences based on PASS achievement. It was hypothesized that quadriceps strength LSI score would more strongly predict 2-year PROMs than hamstring strength LSI score, and that higher 9-month isokinetic quadriceps LSI scores would be associated with higher International Knee Documentation Committee (IKDC) and Lysholm scores.Case series; Level of evidence, 4.Patients undergoing primary QT-ACLR from 2021 to 2024 with LSI testing during rehabilitation (isometric and isokinetic lower extremity strength, Y-Balance, hop testing) and no revision or additional knee surgery were included. The LSI score was assessed at 3, 6, and 9 months, and PROMs, including Lysholm and IKDC scores, were collected at a mean follow-up of 2.0 ± 0.7 years. Multivariable linear regression was used to evaluate associations between LSI measures and PROMs after adjusting for age, sex, and body mass index (BMI). Receiver operating characteristic analysis was used to determine PASS thresholds.A total of 100 knees in 100 patients (mean age, 25.3 ± 11.2 years; BMI, 25.9 ± 6.5 kg/m2; 52% male) were included. Quadriceps and hamstring strength and functional performance progressively improved from 3 to 9 months, with the LSI score reaching 77% to 81% for quadriceps strength and 98% to 100% for hamstring strength by 9 months postoperatively. At a mean follow-up of 2.0 ± 0.7 years, the mean satisfaction score was 8.4 of 10, the Lysholm score was 90.7, and the IKDC score was 77.8. Linear regression, adjusted for age, sex, and BMI, demonstrated that 3-month isometric quadriceps LSI score had a strong effect on IKDC score, explaining substantial variance (β = 3.9; adjusted R2 [AdjR2] = 0.36; P < .03); 6-month isokinetic quadriceps and hamstrings showed moderate but significant effects (β = 2.9-3.7; AdjR2 = 0.13-0.17; P < .05) on IKDC score; and 9-month fast quadriceps had a strong effect explaining substantial variance in Lysholm and IKDC scores (β = 3.9-4.7; AdjR2 = 0.34-0.35; P ≤ .003). Lysholm and IKDC scores correlated with satisfaction and accurately discriminated PASS thresholds (area under the curve, 0.927-0.937; P < .001). Patients achieving the IKDC PASS demonstrated higher LSI scores across time points and all PROMs.After QT-ACLR, strength-associated LSIs were independently associated with PROMs at a mean 2-year follow-up, after adjusting for age, sex, and BMI. Early isometric quadriceps strength at 3 months predicted higher 2-year IKDC scores, with PASS achievers generally attaining a 60% to 70% LSI score by 3 months. Isokinetic quadriceps strength at 9 months predicted both IKDC and Lysholm scores. These findings highlight the importance of early quadriceps strength recovery and the value of LSI measures in predicting PROMs and informing early rehabilitation.

title: The Neoadjuvant Window: Serial Assessment of Sarcopenia During Treatment for Pancreatic Cancer.
abstract: BackgroundSarcopenia is associated with worse outcomes in pancreatic cancer patients, but longitudinal body composition changes during neoadjuvant therapy remain poorly understood.MethodsA retrospective review identified patients who underwent pancreatectomy, either upfront or after neoadjuvant therapy, for pancreatic adenocarcinoma between 2011 and 2021. Skeletal muscle area, index, and mean attenuation were calculated from CT images throughout the treatment course to assess sarcopenia. Multivariable generalized linear and logistic regression models were used to assess associations between sarcopenia, neoadjuvant therapy, and postoperative outcomes.ResultsA total of 72 patients were included: 32 who underwent neoadjuvant therapy and 40 who underwent upfront surgery. Forty-one (57%) patients had sarcopenia at diagnosis (65% upfront surgery vs 47% neoadjuvant, P = 0.154). Post-neoadjuvant therapy, 15.6% developed and 18.8% resolved sarcopenia. Median skeletal muscle mean attenuation increased by 2.4 HU after neoadjuvant therapy (P = 0.02). Patients receiving neoadjuvant therapy were more likely to undergo nutrition consultation prior to surgery (61% vs 7%, P = 0.003). Neoadjuvant therapy was also associated with higher postoperative albumin levels (β = 0.244; 95% CI 0.041-0.446). Baseline sarcopenia diagnosed by skeletal muscle area was associated with increased postoperative complications (OR 13.696; 95% CI 2.537-73.921), while neoadjuvant therapy did not significantly impact complications (OR 0.384; 95% CI 0.12-1.226).ConclusionsPatients who completed neoadjuvant therapy and underwent resection did not have increased rates of sarcopenia and were more likely to receive preoperative nutrition consultation and have higher postoperative albumin levels. The neoadjuvant period may represent an opportunity for sarcopenia assessment, nutritional optimization, and multimodal prehabilitation prior to pancreatectomy.

title: Epistemological Anatomy: A Conceptual Framework for Understanding Anatomical Knowledge.
abstract: Anatomy is often regarded as settled knowledge. Yet anatomical propositions differ enormously in their evidentiary foundations, while textbooks and atlases frequently present them with similar certainty. How, then, does an anatomical observation become anatomical knowledge? We introduce epistemological anatomy as a framework for the systematic study of how anatomical knowledge is generated, validated, transmitted, challenged, and revised. The framework treats the anatomical proposition as a unit of analysis and distinguishes among evidence, scientific confidence, and authority. It also introduces epistemic calibration, defined as the correspondence between the strength of evidence supporting a proposition and the confidence assigned to it. Because no generation can independently re-examine the entire human body, anatomy necessarily depends on scientific inheritance and trust. Historical examples such as the human rete mirabile and meningeal lymphatic vessels illustrate how authority, technology, transmission, and re-examination can alter the standing of anatomical propositions. Epistemological anatomy is proposed not as a replacement for traditional anatomy, but as a new field and complementary research program to make the evidentiary histories of anatomical claims more visible and to identify propositions that merit renewed investigation.© 2026 The Author(s). title: Intravenous immunoglobulin as an adjunct to phototherapy in neonatal haemolytic disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Phototherapy remains the first-line treatment of haemolytic disease of the newborn (HDN), a potentially life-threatening condition caused by maternal alloimmunisation. Intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) has been proposed as an adjunct to reduce the need for exchange transfusion (ET), a procedure associated with significant risks. This meta-analysis aims to evaluate the safety and efficacy of IVIG combined with phototherapy versus phototherapy alone in neonates with HDN. A comprehensive search of MEDLINE, EMBASE, CINAHL and the Cochrane Library was conducted up to 24 April 2025. Eligible studies included randomised controlled trials and observational cohorts evaluating IVIG in HDN. Data were pooled using random-effects models. This study was prospectively registered in Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD420251025766). Nineteen studies involving 3673 neonates met the inclusion criteria. IVIG reduced the need for ET (odd ratio [OR] = 0.34; confidence interval [CI]: 0.2-0.8; I2 = 88%) when used as an adjunct to phototherapy compared to phototherapy alone. Subgroup analysis suggested that the reduction in ET was more consistent in Rh-mediated HDN (OR = 0.2; CI: 0.1-0.8; I2 = 81%) than in ABO-mediated HDN (OR = 0.76; CI: 0.1-4.1; I2 = 89%). There were no differences in the length of hospital stay (mean difference [MD] = -0.1 days; CI: -0.8 to 0.6; I2 = 98%), duration of phototherapy (MD = -5.1 h; CI: -15.7 to 5.4; I2 = 98%) or incidence of adverse events (OR = 1.32; CI: 0.2-10.5; I2 = 91%) between groups. Despite reducing ET requirements, adjunctive IVIG with phototherapy may not provide additional clinical benefits compared with phototherapy alone. title: Endocrine Therapy Omission in Estrogen Receptor-Low (1-10%) Early Stage Breast Cancer: An Updated Analysis of the NCDB Database.
abstract: Endocrine therapy (ET) is recommended for estrogen receptor (ER)-positive breast cancer (BC), though its benefit in ER-low (1-10%) disease remains uncertain. Using the National Cancer Database (NCDB) from 2018 to 2020, we previously found that ET omission was associated with worse survival among 7018 patients with ER-low BC treated with (neo)adjuvant chemotherapy, with 586 deaths observed (Choong et al.). Herein, we evaluate ET omission and survival in an expanded NCDB cohort.Female patients with stage I-III ER-low BC diagnosed between 2018 and 2023 and treated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) and/or adjuvant chemotherapy were identified. Trends in ET use were assessed from 2018 to 2023, and overall survival (OS) was analyzed for patients diagnosed from 2018 to 2022. Kaplan-Meier methods estimated OS, and multivariable Cox regression evaluated associations between ET omission and mortality.Among 12,983 patients, 8658 received NAC (53% achieved pathologic complete response [pCR]) and 4325 received adjuvant chemotherapy alone. title: Achieving "ideal" sagittal alignment does not influence HRQoL outcomes 5 years following PSF for lenke 1 AIS.
abstract: Previous studies have emphasized the importance of thoracic kyphosis (TK) restoration and sagittal alignment for long-term outcomes following posterior spinal fusion (PSF) for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS). Although various equations have been introduced to predict the ideal regional alignment of the thoracic or lumbar spine, no study has validated these equations or investigated the influence of achieving these patient-specific ideal regional parameters on patient-reported health-related quality of life (HRQoL) outcomes following PSF for AIS.A retrospective cohort study of a multicenter AIS database identifying patients with PSF with 5-year follow-up was performed. Patients with Lenke 1 curves with complete radiographic records, focusing on sagittal alignment parameters for lumbar lordosis (LL), TK (T2-12), sagittal vertical alignment (SVA), and patient-reported outcomes scores (SRS-22) at preoperative and 5-year follow-up timepoints were included for analysis. "Ideal" TK was calculated using pelvic incidence (PI) and "ideal" lumbar alignment was defined using two criteria. Patients were then subdivided based on whether ideal regional alignment was achieved at 5 years follow-up. SRS-22 total scores were subdivided into quintiles with the lowest 40% of patients (score ≤ 4.3) used to define less optimal outcome (LOO).A total of 991 patients were identified, with 192 patients meeting inclusion criteria (mean 14.5 ± 2.1 years, 88.5% female). The mean "ideal" TK was calculated at 37.6 ± 5.7° (range 23.9°-51.8°) with a mean measured preoperative TK of 27.0 ± 11.8°). Following surgery, there was a significant increase in TK (P < 0.001) with 62 patients (32.3%) achieving "ideal" TK (Table 1). Nonetheless, achieving ideal TK demonstrated no significant impact on SRS-22 domain scores. Additionally, there was no association between achieving ideal TK and the development of LOO (33.9 vs 42.3%; P = 0.16), nor were other sagittal radiographic parameters. Preoperative SRS-22 scores primarily impacted 5-year SRS domain scores and change in score from preoperative values.In a cohort of patients undergoing PSF for Lenke 1 AIS, the pursuit of ideal region-specific alignment parameters did not influence patient-reported outcome measures 5 years following surgery. While this may indicate that younger patients are unaffected by less than "ideal" sagittal alignment, it is also possible that the current definition of "ideal" needs reconsideration. This may indicate the need for an updated sagittal plane assessment in AIS, searching beyond regional measures of sagittal curvature magnitude to better understand the sagittal plane distribution and shape as it relates to longer term outcomes.© 2026. Although thoracic kyphosis significantly increased after surgery and 32.3% of patients achieved the calculated "ideal" thoracic kyphosis value, achieving this ideal alignment showed no significant association with quality-of-life scores or with worse outcomes at 5-year follow-up. Preoperative quality-of-life scores were the primary predictor of 5-year outcomes, not whether ideal sagittal alignment parameters were achieved. These findings suggest that current definitions of "ideal" sagittal alignment may need reconsideration, and future research.

title: A phase 2 study of tipifarnib in children and young adults with tumors harboring HRAS genomic alterations: NCI-COG Pediatric MATCH trial (APEC1621M).
abstract: APEC1621 arm M, a subprotocol of the NCI-COG Pediatric MATCH clinical trial, is a phase 2 study evaluating tipifarnib, a farnesyl transferase inhibitor, in patients with relapsed or refractory solid tumors harboring HRAS mutations at codons G12, G13, Q61, or A146 (NCT04284774).Patients identified by the MATCH screening protocol and enrolled to the arm M subprotocol received tipifarnib at 350 mg/m2/dose (maximum 600 mg/dose) orally twice daily on an intermittent dosing schedule (days 1 to 7 and 15 to 21, every 28 days) until disease progression or intolerable toxicity. The primary aim was to determine the objective response rate (ORR) and secondary objectives included estimating progression-free survival (PFS) and assessing the tolerability of tipifarnib on the intermittent dosing schedule in children.Seven patients matched to the tipifarnib subprotocol and five patients (71%) enrolled. Two matched patients were ineligible for treatment. Diagnoses for the enrolled patients were rhabdomyosarcoma (n = 4) and angiosarcoma (n = 1). HRAS mutations identified in those tumors included G13R (n = 2) and G12S, G12C, and Q61L (n = 1 each). Treatment was associated with grade 1/2 adverse events (AE) consistent with those expected from prior studies. Grade 3 or higher AEs on treatment were disease progression, dyspnea, and pleural effusion, not related to protocol therapy. One patient had stable disease (SD) at the end of cycle two and remained on protocol therapy for four cycles. There were no objective responses (OR).This U.S. cooperative group study was successful at identifying pediatric patients with tumors that harbored oncogenic mutations in HRAS. The frequency of the mutations identified and patients enrolled was lower than anticipated and the study closed before accrual was complete. The adverse effect profile of tipifarnib in pediatric patients on the intermittent dosing schedule was acceptable. Limited single-agent efficacy of tipifarnib was observed in this biomarker-selected cohort of refractory pediatric tumors.© The Author(s) 2026. Published by Oxford University Press.

title: Enhancing Culturally Sensitive Care for Critically Ill Native American Patients and Families: An Educational Initiative and Resource Guide for Nursing and Medical Teams.
abstract: BackgroundNative American (NA) patients experience persistent inequities in advance care planning (ACP) and often present to tertiary centers with critical illness; culturally respectful serious-illness communication is therefore essential in emergency and intensive care settings.InterventionWe developed and implemented a nursing-led, multidisciplinary educational initiative at a large academic medical center serving patients from >50 tribal nations. Informed by a literature review, local practice needs, and expert input from a Native American Patient Experience Ambassador, we created (1) an "Honoring Your Choices" (HYC) communication card with culturally sensitive prompts for serious illness conversations and (2) a quick reference guide (QRG) outlining key cultural considerations and unit-specific resources. Tools were disseminated to seven intensive care units and the emergency department through nurse leader engagement, unit rounding, and staff education, and the initiative was presented at departmental Grand Rounds/didactics with pre/post surveys to assess impact.ResultsTwenty-seven pre-session and twenty-four post-session surveys were collected from clinicians and trainees. Prior to the session, >80% of respondents reported being not or only slightly confident discussing end-of-life issues with NA patients/families; post-session surveys demonstrated increased self-reported confidence in recognizing when cultural beliefs may influence care and in conducting end-of-life discussions.ConclusionsThis initiative demonstrates how culturally congruent approaches to serious illness conversations may support more meaningful engagement with NA patients and families. Our experience suggests that developing and evaluating a brief, point-of-care communication tool like Honoring Your Choices may be accomplished with existing interdisciplinary partnerships, offering a practical model that other institutions can readily mirror.

llm_summary: Native American patients in critical care settings often lack adequate advance care planning and experience health inequities, making culturally respectful communication essential for emergency and intensive care teams. Researchers at a large academic medical center developed and implemented a nursing-led educational initiative that included an "Honoring Your Choices" communication card with culturally sensitive prompts and a quick reference guide outlining key cultural considerations, which were distributed to seven intensive care units and the emergency department through staff education and unit engagement. title: To Lengthen or Revise: Reevaluating Anterior Acetabular Overhang Thresholds in Iliopsoas Impingement After Total Hip Arthroplasty.
abstract: Iliopsoas impingement (IPI) is a known cause of persistent anterior hip pain following total hip arthroplasty (THA). Management of IPI has often relied on an 8-mm anterior acetabular overhang threshold to guide operative treatment, favoring acetabular revision for greater overhang and iliopsoas tenotomy for lesser overhang. These thresholds were initially established on the basis of the outcomes of open tenotomy, and now, with an improved understanding of IPI and the advent of arthroscopic iliopsoas fractional lengthening (IPFL), a review of the 8-mm threshold is warranted.A retrospective review was performed to identify patients who underwent arthroscopic IPFL following primary THA between 2017 and 2024, with a minimum follow-up of 1 year. Acetabular overhang was measured for all patients using cross-table lateral radiographs, and patients were stratified into <8-mm and ≥8-mm cohorts. Patient-reported outcome measures, reoperations, revisions, and complications were collected and analyzed on the basis of both the classic 8-mm threshold and continuous statistical methods.We evaluated 86 hips undergoing IPFL. There were 83 patients (30 men and 53 women), with a mean age of 63.0 ± 11.2 years; with regard to race, 80 patients were White, 1 patient was Black or African American, and 2 patients listed other race or chose not to disclose. The acetabular overhang was <8 mm for 67 hips and ≥8 mm for 19 hips. The mean follow-up was 2.5 ± 1.6 years (range, 1 to 7.5 years). When comparing patients with <8-mm and ≥8-mm acetabular overhang, we observed no significant differences (p > 0.06) in the preoperative and postoperative visual analog scale (VAS) pain scores, modified Harris hip score, Single Assessment Numeric Evaluation (SANE) score, Tegner activity level, subjective groin pain improvement, subjective hip flexion strength improvement, and overall satisfaction. Reoperation (2.9% compared with 10.5%; p = 0.210) and acetabular revision rates (1.5% compared with 5%; p = 0.387) were not significantly different between the <8-mm and ≥8-mm overhang groups.Arthroscopic IPFL provided satisfactory outcomes for patients with IPI, independent of the magnitude of acetabular overhang. IPFL should be considered for first-line surgical management of IPI refractory to nonoperative management, even in the setting of substantial acetabular overhang, given positive outcomes and low rates of subsequent acetabular revision.Therapeutic Level IV. llm_summary: Iliopsoas impingement, a source of persistent anterior hip pain after hip replacement surgery, has traditionally been managed using an 8-millimeter acetabular overhang threshold to decide between revision surgery and tendon lengthening procedures. Researchers retrospectively reviewed 86 hip replacements in 83 patients (mean age 63 years) who underwent arthroscopic iliopsoas fractional lengthening between 2017 and 2024, measuring acetabular overhang on radiographs and comparing outcomes between patients with less than 8 millimeters of overhang (67 hips) and those with 8 millimeters or greater (19 hips). Pain scores, functional measures, and patient satisfaction showed no significant differences between the two groups (all p > 0.06), and reoperation rates were similarly low at 2.9% for the smaller overhang group versus 10.5% for the larger overhang group (p = 0.210). These findings suggest that arthroscopic lengthening may be effective regardless of overhang magnitude, potentially challenging the traditional 8-millimeter threshold that previously guided.

title: Anti-HDGFL2 cryptic protein antibodies provide a sensitive readout of TDP-43 pathology and clinical disease features.
abstract: TAR DNA-binding protein (TDP-43) cytoplasmic aggregates and nuclear depletion contribute to TDP-43 dysfunction in frontotemporal lobar degeneration with TDP-43 pathology (FTLD-TDP) and forms of motor neuron disease (MND), particularly amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). TDP-43 regulates alternative splicing, but its dysfunction can engender the inclusion of cryptic exons (CEs) during splicing. Transcripts harboring an in-frame CE can generate de novo proteins. One example is the CE variant of hepatoma-derived growth factor-like protein 2 (HDGFL2-CE). To understand HDGFL2-CE as a readout of TDP-43 dysfunction, and its spatial relationship with TDP-43 pathology, we generate anti-HDGFL2-CE polyclonal and monoclonal antibodies and develop sensitive HDGFL2-CE immunoassays. With these tools, we observe that HDGFL2-CE accumulates in neurons with TDP-43 pathology, and that higher frontal cortex HDGFL2-CE in FTLD-TDP and FTLD-TDP/MND associates with greater pathological TDP-43, earlier age of onset, and shorter survival, supporting HDGFL2-CE as a marker tightly linked to TDP-43 dysfunction and clinical disease features.Copyright © 2026 The Author(s). llm_summary: Researchers examined whether a cryptic protein called HDGFL2-CE, which is generated when TDP-43 dysfunction causes abnormal gene splicing, could serve as a marker for TDP-43 pathology in neurodegenerative diseases like frontotemporal lobar degeneration and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. They developed antibodies and sensitive tests to detect HDGFL2-CE and found that this protein accumulated in neurons showing TDP-43 pathology in patient brain tissue. Higher levels of HDGFL2-CE in the frontal cortex were associated with greater amounts of pathological TDP-43, earlier disease onset, and shorter survival in patients with frontotemporal lobar degeneration. These findings suggest that HDGFL2-CE accumulation correlates with TDP-43 dysfunction and clinical disease severity. The study establishes HDGFL2-CE as a potential biomarker for monitoring TDP-43-related neurodegeneration, though further research would be needed to determine its utility in clinical settings.

title: Magnetically guided microrobot via minimally invasive percutaneous cisternal access: a first preclinical evaluation.
abstract: Magnetically guided microrobots could enable minimally invasive intracranial interventions by navigating CSF spaces without traversing brain parenchyma. However, clinical translation requires in vivo validation of delivery, control, retrieval, and short-term safety under realistic workflow conditions. The aim of this study was to assess the feasibility and initial safety of percutaneous cisterna magna access, microrobot navigation, and retrieval using an image-integrated electromagnetic coil platform in a large-animal model, targeting future application to Dandy-Walker malformation cyst fenestration.In this Good Laboratory Practice-compliant ovine study, 7 male sheep were allocated to an MRI-only control group (n = 1), flexion control group (n = 1), and treatment group (n = 3; percutaneous cisternal access, deployment of a 3.5 × 7-mm Parylene-C-coated bladed microrobot with a neodymium core, magnetic navigation, scripted dwell, and retrieval), with 2 animals designated as alternates. Preoperative MRI was used for planning, with intraoperative cone-beam CT fusion and biplanar fluoroscopy. The follow-up period was 28 days and included daily observation, weekly neurological examination, and analysis of hematology/chemistry, intraoperative CSF, and terminal necropsy with histopathology. Outcomes were descriptive.The full workflow was completed in all 3 treated animals without conversion or rescue. Cannulation succeeded on the first attempt; continuous fluoroscopic visibility and stable magnetic control were maintained; and retrieval succeeded in a single maneuver. Postoperative recovery was uneventful, with weight gain and no neurological deficits over 28 days of follow-up. Laboratory values were within reference ranges except for 1 case of transient leukocytosis (day 0) that resolved. CSF was acellular/normal. Necropsy showed localized procedure-site changes only (dural fibrosis, thin adhesions in 2 of 3 treated animals). Histology revealed focal superficial vermian gliosis ≤ 2 mm in 2 of 3 treated animals without hemorrhage, necrosis, or off-target injury, and controls were within normal limits (1 case of minimal incidental axonal change in the flexion control).Percutaneous cisternal delivery and retrieval of an untethered microrobot were feasible and tolerated in sheep, with localized tissue responses at 28 days. These findings support further studies focused on longer follow-up, workflow optimization, and disease-specific efficacy.

llm_summary: Minimally invasive delivery of small magnetic devices through cerebrospinal fluid spaces could enable brain treatments without cutting through brain tissue, but this approach requires testing in living animals before human use. Researchers implanted a small bladed microrobot with a magnetic core into the fluid-filled spaces around the brains of three sheep, guided it using magnetic fields and imaging, and then retrieved it, while monitoring the animals for 28 days with neurological exams, blood tests, and tissue analysis. All three treated animals completed the full procedure without complications, maintained stable recovery with normal weight gain and no neurological deficits over the follow-up period, and showed only localized tissue changes at the procedure site on final examination. The findings indicate that percutaneous delivery and retrieval of untethered microrobots in cerebrospinal fluid spaces is technically feasible and produces minimal tissue injury in this large-animal model. Further studies with longer observation periods and testing in disease-specific applications are needed to determine whether this approach can be safely translated to human patients.

title: Critical Role for Living-Donor Liver Transplantation in a Changing Organ Landscape: Insights on National Trends from the NALLDIG Consortium.
abstract: Despite offering excellent outcomes and improved transplant access, living-donor liver transplantation (LDLT) has persistently represented a small minority of total liver transplant volume in the United States. Conversely, the use of advanced preservation (AP) technology and expansion of donation after circulatory death has been explosive. The impact of these trends on the future of LDLT practice in the US remains uncertain. Prior assessments have varied from considering LDLT and AP complimentary avenues to LT, to suggesting that increased deceased donor availability may render LDLT diminishingly relevant. In this viewpoint, the members of the North American Living Liver Donor Innovation Group, a consortium representing 37 LDLT-performing transplant centers, review key trends and contextualize heterogenous changes in LDLT practice. The authors argue that LDLT will continue to maintain relevance in the face of AP-driven increased deceased donor availability and argue that LDLT availability and expertise be preserved and expanded in the post-AP era.Copyright © 2026. llm_summary: Living-donor liver transplantation (LDLT) has traditionally represented a small portion of total liver transplants in the United States, but the field faces uncertainty as advanced preservation technology and donation after circulatory death have expanded deceased donor availability. The North American Living Liver Donor Innovation Group, a consortium of 37 LDLT-performing transplant centers, reviewed national trends in LDLT practice to assess how these competing approaches are reshaping the transplant landscape. The consortium's analysis revealed heterogeneous changes across LDLT programs, suggesting that the relationship between LDLT and advanced preservation technology is more complex than previous assessments that characterized them as either complementary or competitive approaches. The authors argue that LDLT will remain relevant and valuable even as increased deceased donor availability becomes possible through advanced preservation methods. The consortium recommends that LDLT availability and expertise be preserved and expanded in the coming era to maintain this important transplant option for patients.
llm_summary_expert: The North American Living Liver Donor Innovation Group, a consortium representing 37 living-donor liver transplantation (LDLT)-performing centers, reviewed national trends in LDLT practice in the context of expanding advanced preservation technology and donation after circulatory death utilization. While LDLT has historically represented a small minority of total liver transplant volume in the United States despite offering excellent outcomes and improved access, advanced preservation technology and expanded deceased donor availability have increased substantially. The consortium argues that LDLT will maintain clinical relevance and complementary value alongside increased deceased donor availability in the post-advanced preservation era. This viewpoint assessment is limited by its reliance on consortium member perspectives rather than comprehensive national registry data with quantified outcome comparisons.

title: Predictors of Neurologic Recovery in Retroperitoneal Hematoma-Associated Femoral Neuropathy: A Systematic Review with Pooled Patient-Level Analysis.
abstract: Retroperitoneal hematoma (RPH) is a rare but significant condition that can lead to femoral neuropathy (FN). This study aimed to evaluate etiologies, management approaches, and predictors of neurologic recovery in RPH-associated FN.A systematic review was performed according to PRISMA guidelines.156 studies comprising 209 patients (211 limbs) were included. Etiologies were medication-related hemorrhage (50%), trauma (22%), spontaneous bleeding (11%), post-procedural (5.7%), and combined (10%). Management was conservative (52%), surgical evacuation (37%), percutaneous decompression (5.6%), embolization (1%), and combined (4%). Trauma (OR 12.67, 95% CI 3.28-48.99, p < 0.001) and spontaneous etiology (OR 7.26, 95% CI 1.88-28.04, p = 0.004) were independently associated with higher odds of motor recovery compared with post-medication cases. Percutaneous decompression was associated with lower odds of motor recovery (OR 0.10, 95%CI 0.02-0.63, p =0.014) compared to medical management. Post-procedural and combined etiologies, as well as other treatment modalities, were not significantly associated with motor recovery. Longer follow-up was associated with greater quadriceps strength improvement on the MRC scale (β = 0.05/month, p =0.012). No variables were significantly associated with sensory recovery in primary analysis. Sensitivity analysis of patients with follow-up of 12+ months showed trauma as the only variable with significantly higher odds of motor and sensory recovery. Hematoma size, location and time to presentation were not predictive of outcomes.FN due to RPH occurs predominantly in anticoagulated patients and is usually managed conservatively. Etiology appears to primarily influence motor recovery. These findings support individualized, largely nonoperative management.Copyright © 2026 The Author(s). Published by Elsevier Inc. llm_summary: Femoral neuropathy caused by retroperitoneal hematoma is a rare complication that can result from bleeding, trauma, or medication side effects, and understanding which patients recover nerve function is clinically important. Researchers systematically reviewed 156 studies involving 209 patients to identify factors associated with neurologic recovery, finding that medication-related hemorrhage was the most common cause (50%), followed by trauma (22%) and spontaneous bleeding (11%). Trauma and spontaneous bleeding were associated with significantly higher odds of motor recovery compared to medication-related cases (odds ratios of 12.67 and 7.26, respectively), while percutaneous decompression showed lower odds of motor recovery than conservative management. Longer follow-up duration was associated with greater improvement in quadriceps strength, and in patients followed for 12 or more months, trauma was the only variable significantly associated with both motor and sensory recovery. The findings suggest that hematoma etiology primarily influences motor recovery outcomes, supporting an individualized approach that favors conservative management in most cases rather than routine surgical intervention.

title: International consensuses and guidelines on etiology, diagnosis, and treatment of retinal vein occlusion (RVO) by the Academy of Asia-Pacific Professors of Ophthalmology (AAPPO), Asia-Pacific Vitreo-retina Society (APVRS) and Academia Retina Internationalis (ARI).
abstract: Retinal vein occlusion (RVO) is a prevalent potentially blinding retinal vascular disease, with secondary macular edema, retinal ischemia, and ocular neovascular complications posing substantial threats to visual function. Supported by members of the Academy of Asia-Pacific Professors of Ophthalmology (AAPPO), Asia-Pacific Vitreo-retina Society (APVRS) and Academia Retina Internationalis (ARI), a consensus and guideline is provided a comprehensive update on the etiology, diagnosis and management of RVO. An updated consensus was judged necessary following numerous recent results from epidemiology studies, evolution of advanced imaging technologies and novel pharmacotherapeutics from clinical trials, including an expanding portfolio of anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) agents, drug delivery systems, and emerging evidence on relevant artificial intelligence. The formulation of these consensus statements were based on the review and discussion of a systematic search for the latest evidence-based data and voting by an International Panel of Experts (IPE) in the following key areas: I) Diagnostic controversies around classification systems and imaging modalities; II) Treatment controversies regarding anti-VEGF therapy, corticosteroid treatments, laser therapy, and surgical interventions; III) Management paradigm between standardized protocols from clinical trials and individualized approaches and IV) Emerging controversies in novel therapeutics. The primary goal was to furnish ophthalmologists with standardized, yet individualized, management protocols to try to optimize treatment safety and efficacy, ensuring alignment with contemporary clinical practices in the Asia-Pacific region.Copyright © 2026. llm_summary: Retinal vein occlusion (RVO) is a common eye disease that can cause vision loss through complications including fluid accumulation in the macula, tissue damage from insufficient blood flow, and abnormal blood vessel growth. An international panel of experts from ophthalmology organizations in the Asia-Pacific region and beyond conducted a systematic review of recent evidence on RVO's causes, diagnosis, and treatment to develop updated clinical guidelines. The consensus addressed diagnostic challenges related to classification systems and imaging technologies, as well as treatment controversies involving anti-VEGF drugs, corticosteroids, laser therapy, and surgery, while also considering emerging therapies and artificial intelligence applications. The experts formulated standardized yet individualized management protocols designed to help ophthalmologists optimize treatment safety and effectiveness while aligning with current clinical practices in the Asia-Pacific region. These guidelines aim to provide clinicians with evidence-based recommendations that balance the structured approaches validated in clinical trials with the flexibility needed to tailor treatment to individual patient circumstances.
llm_summary_expert: An international panel of experts from the Academy of Asia-Pacific Professors of Ophthalmology, Asia-Pacific Vitreo-retina Society, and Academia Retina Internationalis developed consensus guidelines on retinal vein occlusion etiology, diagnosis, and management through systematic evidence review and expert voting. The consensus addressed four key areas: diagnostic controversies regarding classification systems and imaging modalities, treatment controversies involving anti-VEGF therapy, corticosteroids, laser therapy, and surgical interventions, management paradigms balancing standardized clinical trial protocols with individualized approaches, and emerging therapeutics including novel anti-VEGF agents and artificial intelligence applications. The guidelines synthesized recent epidemiological data, advanced imaging technologies, and pharmacotherapeutic evidence to provide standardized yet individualized management protocols for optimizing treatment safety and efficacy in retinal vein occlusion. The recommendations aimed to align contemporary clinical practices across the Asia-Pacific region while addressing secondary complications including macular edema, retinal ischemia, and ocular neovascular disease.

title: Bleeding and Hemostasis Optimization in Primary and Revision Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Structured Expert-Opinion Survey.
abstract: Disruptive bleeding following total knee arthroplasty (TKA) continues to affect postoperative recovery despite advances in perioperative blood management, with wound drainage and dressing-related findings common clinical concerns. Conventional definitions based on estimated blood loss or hemoglobin decline may not capture bleeding events that alter clinical management. This study sought to establish agreement on disruptive bleeding in TKA and identify clinically relevant factors guiding monitoring, escalation, and hemostatic decision-making.A survey-based study was conducted among 14 fellowship-trained arthroplasty surgeons who had experience in primary and revision TKA. Domains included risk factors, definitions of disruptive bleeding, intraoperative bleeding patterns, postoperative drainage assessment, escalation criteria, and the use of topical hemostatic agents. Responses included Likert-scale ratings, categorical selections, and free-text data. High agreement for items was defined a priori as ≥ 70% agreement.Respondents supported defining disruptive bleeding as a composite of clinically meaningful outcomes rather than isolated quantitative measures. There was unanimous agreement to include operational indicators (symptomatic hemoglobin decline greater than three g/dL and persistent wound drainage) and downstream events (transfusion, reoperation, embolization, and readmission). Thrombocytopenia and anticoagulant use were important risk factors (n = 14 of 14), followed by coagulopathy and liver disease (n = 12 of 14). Escalation triggers included suspected arterial bleeding (n = 14 of 14), expanding hematoma (n = 13 of 14), hemodynamic instability (n = 13 of 14), neurovascular compromise (n = 13 of 14), and drainage beyond postoperative day five (n = 12 of 14). Routine prophylactic use of topical hemostatic agents was not supported in primary TKA (n = 2 of 14), but was selectively favored in revision cases (n = 7 of 14). Variability remained regarding drainage thresholds and timing of intervention.Disruptive bleeding in TKA was viewed as a composite construct defined by events that alter care rather than isolated numeric blood-loss measures. These findings represent an exploratory, hypothesis-generating framework requiring multidisciplinary and data-driven validation.Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Inc.

llm_summary: Postoperative bleeding after total knee replacement surgery remains a clinical challenge that can complicate recovery, prompting a need for clearer definitions and management strategies. Fourteen experienced knee replacement surgeons participated in a survey to establish consensus on what constitutes clinically significant bleeding and how to identify risk factors and escalation triggers. The experts unanimously agreed that disruptive bleeding should be defined by clinically meaningful outcomes such as symptomatic hemoglobin drops greater than three grams per deciliter, persistent wound drainage, transfusion requirements, reoperation, and readmission rather than by isolated blood loss measurements alone. Key risk factors identified with full agreement included thrombocytopenia and anticoagulant use, while escalation triggers warranting intervention included suspected arterial bleeding, expanding hematoma, hemodynamic instability, and drainage persisting beyond postoperative day five. The findings provide an exploratory framework for understanding disruptive bleeding in knee replacement surgery, though the authors note that multidisciplinary and data-driven validation is needed before these expert opinions can be fully implemented in clinical practice.
llm_summary_expert: A survey-based study among 14 fellowship-trained arthroplasty surgeons examined definitions and management of disruptive bleeding in primary and revision total knee arthroplasty through Likert-scale ratings and categorical selections across domains including risk factors, intraoperative patterns, postoperative drainage assessment, and hemostatic decision-making. Respondents achieved unanimous agreement (14 of 14) that disruptive bleeding should be defined as a composite of clinically meaningful outcomes including symptomatic hemoglobin decline greater than three g/dL, persistent wound drainage, transfusion, reoperation, embolization, and readmission rather than isolated quantitative measures. Thrombocytopenia and anticoagulant use were identified as important risk factors by all 14 respondents, with escalation triggers including suspected arterial bleeding (14 of 14), expanding hematoma (13 of 14), hemodynamic instability (13 of 14), and neurovascular compromise (13 of 14). Topical hemostatic agents were not routinely supported in primary TKA (2 of 14).

title: Outcomes and Complications of Elbow Arthrodesis.
abstract: Arthrodesis of the elbow is a rarely performed procedure sometimes considered when no other reliable surgical solutions exist. Most published reports are limited to single case reports or very small series. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the outcomes and complications of patients who underwent elbow arthrodesis and to determine whether this is a worthwhile salvage procedure for elbows not amendable to surgical reconstruction or arthroplasty.Between 2000 and 2024, a retrospective review was performed of 13 elbows (13 patients) that underwent elbow arthrodesis at a single tertiary academic institution. There were 11 males and 2 females with a mean age of 42 years at the time of arthrodesis. Most arthrodeses (92%) were performed for posttraumatic arthritis. Electronic medical records were reviewed to collect demographic and clinical data, details of the surgical procedure, clinical outcomes and complications. Additionally, patients were contacted at the time of this study to collect Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) for pain, Single Numeric Assessment Evaluation (SANE), Mayo Elbow Performance Score (MEPS), subjective satisfaction, and any additional reoperations or complications. Postoperative radiographs were evaluated to determine union and identify possible radiographic complications. The arthrodesis angle was also measured on lateral postoperative radiographs.The mean follow-up of this study was 7 years. The mean postoperative arthrodesis angle was in 75 degrees of flexion. Patient outcomes could be obtained at most recent follow up for 9 of 13 patients. At most recent follow-up, average VAS scores for pain were 2 at rest and 4 with activity. The mean MEPS and SANE were 49 and 46. The overall satisfaction score was 8/10 and 57% of patients reported to be better or much better than before surgery. Complications, including nonunion or periprosthetic fracture, occurred in 6 (46%) elbows, 5 (39%) of which led to revision surgery.Elbow arthrodesis demonstrated reasonable pain relief and subjective satisfaction for patients with severe destruction of the elbow joint despite poor functional outcomes. The combined rate of nonunion or postoperative fracture was greater than 40%. Elbow arthrodesis is a salvage procedure that should be only considered when no other reconstructive or arthroplasty options exist.Level IV, Case Series, Treatment Study.Copyright © 2026. llm_summary: Elbow arthrodesis, a procedure that fuses the elbow joint, is rarely performed and typically considered only when other surgical options are not viable, making it important to evaluate its effectiveness as a salvage treatment. Researchers conducted a retrospective review of 13 patients (11 male, 2 female, mean age 42 years) who underwent elbow arthrodesis between 2000 and 2024 at a single academic medical center, with most procedures performed for posttraumatic arthritis. At a mean follow-up of 7 years, patients who could be contacted (9 of 13) reported average pain scores of 2 at rest and 4 with activity, overall satisfaction of 8 out of 10, and 57% reported being better or much better than before surgery, though functional outcome scores were poor. Complications including nonunion or fracture occurred in 6 elbows (46%), with 5 of these requiring revision surgery, indicating a substantial complication rate. The authors conclude that elbow arthrodesis provides reasonable pain relief and patient satisfaction in severe cases but should only be considered as a last resort when reconstruction.
llm_summary_expert: This retrospective case series evaluated 13 patients (11 male, 2 female; mean age 42 years) who underwent elbow arthrodesis between 2000 and 2024 at a single tertiary institution, with 92% performed for posttraumatic arthritis and mean follow-up of 7 years. The primary endpoints included pain assessed by Visual Analogue Scale, functional outcomes measured by Mayo Elbow Performance Score (MEPS) and Single Numeric Assessment Evaluation (SANE), and radiographic union. At most recent follow-up (9 of 13 patients), mean VAS pain scores were 2 at rest and 4 with activity, mean MEPS was 49, mean SANE was 46, and overall satisfaction was 8/10, with 57% reporting improvement compared to preoperative status. Complications including nonunion or periprosthetic fracture occurred in 6 elbows (46%), with 5 (39%) requiring revision surgery. The authors conclude that elbow arthrodesis provides reasonable pain relief and subjective satisfaction despite poor functional outcomes, and should.

title: Long-term Safety and Efficacy of Once-Weekly Lonapegsomatropin in Adults With Growth Hormone Deficiency: Results From a 52-Week Open-Label Extension Trial.
abstract: To evaluate long-term safety and efficacy of once-weekly lonapegsomatropin in adults with growth hormone (GH) deficiency.This 52-week, multicenter, open-label extension trial enrolled adults with GH deficiency who completed the 38-week phase 3 foresiGHt trial, in which participants received lonapegsomatropin, placebo, or somatropin.1 In the extension, all participants received lonapegsomatropin. Safety assessment included adverse events (AEs), laboratory values, vital signs, immunogenicity, 12-lead electrocardiograms, and fundoscopy. Body composition (trunk percent fat, trunk fat mass, visceral adipose tissue, total body lean mass, trunk lean mass, and appendicular lean mass) was measured by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry, and patient-reported outcomes were evaluated.Following foresiGHt completion, 220 (88.7%) participants enrolled in the extension. Across foresiGHt and the extension, common lonapegsomatropin-associated AEs were nasopharyngitis, upper respiratory infection, and headache. Injection site reactions were infrequent (5.1%) and mild or moderate. After up to 90 weeks of treatment, body composition was maintained in participants continuing lonapegsomatropin, and improved relative to foresiGHt baseline in those initiating or switching to lonapegsomatropin. Clinically meaningful improvements in patient-reported outcomes from foresiGHt baseline were observed; 43.5%, 40.6%, and 35.8% of participants achieving a ≥10-point improvement in Treatment Related Impact Measure-Adult GH Deficiency (TRIM-AGHD) total score among those continuing, initiating, or switching to lonapegsomatropin, respectively.Once-weekly lonapegsomatropin was generally well tolerated and was associated with sustained improvements in body composition and patient-reported outcomes for up to 90 weeks. These findings extend prior evidence and support the long-term benefits of lonapegsomatropin in adults with GH deficiency, including those switching from somatropin.Copyright © 2026. llm_summary: A 52-week open-label extension trial evaluated the long-term safety and efficacy of lonapegsomatropin, a once-weekly growth hormone treatment, in 220 adults with growth hormone deficiency who had completed a prior 38-week phase 3 trial. Participants received lonapegsomatropin throughout the extension period, with researchers monitoring adverse events, body composition changes measured by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry, and patient-reported quality-of-life outcomes. Common side effects were mild respiratory infections and headaches, with injection site reactions occurring infrequently at 5.1% and remaining mild or moderate in severity. After up to 90 weeks of total treatment, body composition improvements were sustained in participants who continued lonapegsomatropin and improved relative to baseline in those newly starting or switching from another growth hormone therapy, with 35.8% to 43.5% of participants achieving clinically meaningful improvements in quality-of-life measures. These results support the long-term tolerability and effectiveness of once-weekly lonapegsomatropin for adults with growth hormone deficiency, including those transitioning from other growth hormone treatments.

abstract: Mild autonomous cortisol secretion (MACS) is a biochemical phenotype in adrenal incidentalomas associated with cardiometabolic risk. title: Safety and Efficacy of Combined Middle Meningeal Artery and CSF Venous Fistula Embolization in Treatment of Spontaneous Intracranial Hypotension with Concurrent Subdural Fluid Collection.
abstract: Fistulas forming between cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and spinal veins is a common cause of spontaneous intracranial hypotension (SIH) with subdural fluid collections(SDFC). CSF-venous fistulas embolization (CVFE) can be performed with a combined middle meningeal artery embolization (MMAE) to close the fistula and treat the SDFC.Assess the safety and efficacy of combined MMAE and CVFE treatment.We performed a retrospective cohort study of 40 patients who underwent combined MMAE and CVFE or CVFE alone with SIH and SDFC at a single institution. Patients deemed nonsurgical candidates were excluded. Their demographics, clinical outcomes, and complications were reviewed.18 patients who underwent combined embolization were compared to 22 patients who underwent CVFE alone. The median age at embolization was 69 years for the CVFE only group and 66 years for the combined group. 19/22 (86%) patients experienced complete or significant improvement in symptoms in the CVFE only group versus 15/18 (83%) in the combined group. One patient in the dual embolization group had repeat SDFC while three patients in the CVFE only group had repeat SDFC. One patient in both groups experienced no improvement or worse clinical outcomes after the procedure. No patients in either group experienced any procedural complications.Combined MMAE and CVFE was not found to have worse clinical outcomes or higher complication rates when compared to CVFE alone. In patients presenting with SDFC with CSF-venous fistula, combined embolization may be a potential therapy that can address all symptoms.© 2026 by American Journal of Neuroradiology.

title: Improvements in Return to Work Following Lumbar Discectomy With a Bone-Anchored Annular Closure Device.
abstract: Lumbar discectomy is the most frequently performed spinal surgery, and timely return to work is an important marker of functional recovery. Patients with large annular defects are at increased risk of reherniation and reoperation. Bone-anchored annular closure devices have been shown to reduce reherniation rates, but their effect on return to work has not been reported. This study investigates whether treatment with a bone-anchored annular closure device enables faster return to work in high-risk lumbar discectomy patients with large annular defects.In this prospective, multicenter, single-arm post-market study, 55 patients with large annular defects undergoing limited lumbar discectomy received a bone-anchored annular closure device. Employment status and return to work were assessed at 4 weeks, 3 months, and 12 months via questionnaires. Preoperative predictors of delayed return to work were analyzed using univariate logistic regression. Patients who were students, retirees, or stay-at-home parents were excluded from return-to-work analyses. Adverse events, reherniation, and reoperation were recorded.Among 46 employed patients (mean age, 41 years; 40% women), mean return to work was 3.4 weeks; 93% resumed work by 3 months and of those, 61% returned within 4 weeks and 100% by 9 weeks. Smoking was associated with delayed return to work (5.9 vs 3.2 weeks; P = 0.014). Two patients (3.6%) experienced symptomatic reherniation, 1 of whom required reoperation. No device-related adverse events were observed.Treatment with a bone-anchored annular closure device enabled rapid return to work in high-risk lumbar discectomy patients while maintaining low rates of reherniation and reoperation.These findings support the use of bone-anchored annular closure as an adjunct to lumbar discectomy in patients with large annular defects to accelerate return to work.This manuscript is generously published free of charge by ISASS, the International Society for the Advancement of Spine Surgery. title: N-of-1 investigational study of a novel antisense oligonucleotide drug in CHCHD10-related ALS shows early signs of efficacy.
abstract: Pathogenic CHCHD10 variants cause a rare, dominantly inherited form of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Six intrathecal doses were administered over 12 months (three 50-mg doses followed by three 75-mg doses). Prespecified primary outcomes were 12-month changes in functional, cognitive, quality-of-life, respiratory, neurofilament light (NfL), and survival measures; secondary outcomes assessed were safety and tolerability. Analyses were descriptive.No serious adverse events occurred. Post-dose headache and fatigue were mild to moderate, and cerebrospinal fluid safety results were unremarkable. Plasma NfL decreased by approximately 50% from a mildly elevated pretreatment baseline and entered the laboratory reference range. title: Retrieval-to-abstraction LLM-assisted literature synthesis: Case demonstrations in digital health technology-enabled randomized controlled trial outcome reporting.
abstract: Systematic reviews of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) support evidence-based clinical advancement. Clinical trial reporting guidelines, including CONSORT, establish common data elements that support systematic synthesis of published trial outcomes. However, the rapid rise of digital health technologies presents new challenges for reporting guidelines, and substantial real-world reporting heterogeneity has been observed. Therefore, machine-assisted evaluation of reporting adherence offers a pathway for more agile information management to accommodate the diverse and disruptive nature of digital health technology-enabled RCTs. Here, we propose an accelerated retrieval-to-abstraction literature synthesis framework to conduct article screening, text and table data preprocessing, and full-text review using an unmodified pretrained large language model. We apply this methodology in two digital health technology-enabled RCT case studies evaluating adherence to technology and digital health equity guideline reporting items. Large language model performance was on par with inter-annotator agreement F1 scores (≥0.9) in both screening and information-extraction tasks. These findings support the scalability and rigor of accelerated evidence synthesis and demonstrate the importance of common reporting elements across digital health technology-enabled RCTs.Copyright: © 2026 Harrison et al. title: The hearing healthcare workforce: insights into density, distribution and opportunities for capacity-development.
abstract: Hearing loss is a major global health concern, yet many countries lack the necessary workforce to provide hearing care services. This study aimed to evaluate the global distribution, availability, and training of hearing healthcare providers, including audiologists and other professionals involved in hearing care.A cross-sectional electronic survey was conducted from June 2022 to March 2024 by the Global Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery Initiative, collecting national-level data from 93 countries representing 77 percent of the world's population. Responses were analysed by income classification and geographic region based on World Bank and World Health Organization categories.The global density of audiologists was 1.48 per 100,000 people, with more than 70 percent of countries reporting fewer than one audiologist per 100,000. The overall hearing healthcare workforce density was 4.1 per 100,000 population. Training opportunities were limited in low-income countries, where 83 percent of audiologists were trained outside their home country. The African, Eastern Mediterranean, and South-East Asian regions were especially underserved. Workforce roles and service scope varied widely across regions and income levels.These findings highlight critical disparities and emphasise the need for targeted workforce planning and sustainable training programs to improve global hearing care.

abstract: Left atrial (LA) stiffening augments the LA V wave, pressurizing the pulmonary artery (PA) out of proportion to left ventricular end-diastolic pressure. We characterized the pathophysiologic, diagnostic, and clinical implications of LA stiffening, as defined by prominent V waves, in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.In this retrospective cohort study, patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and less than moderate mitral regurgitation at rest underwent invasive hemodynamic exercise testing. Patients with heightened operant LA stiffening were defined by the PA wedge pressure (PAWP) V wave exceeding mean PAWP by ≥10 mm Hg. A previously used formula for V wave-corrected PAWP was validated against the PAWP waveform pressure-time-area to explore impact of the V wave on transpulmonary pressure gradients. Clinical, echocardiographic, hemodynamic, and outcome data were compared for patients with and without prominent V waves.Compared with patients without prominent V waves (n=844, 79%), those with prominent V waves (n=225, 21%) were older and more likely to be women, with more severe LA myopathy, evidenced by greater LA volume index (42.2±15.0 versus 32.5±13.0 mL/m2, P<0.001), lower LA reservoir strain (16.4±7.5% versus 23.2±8.3%, P<0.001), more atrial fibrillation (61.3% versus 22.9%, P<0.001), and increased operant LA reservoir stiffness (0.59±0.25 versus 0.23±0.24 mm Hg/mL, P<0.001). Patients with prominent V waves had markedly higher PA systolic pressure than those without (54±16 versus 38±12 mm Hg, P<0.001) despite no difference in end-diastolic PAWP-PA pressure gradient (3±5 versus 3±4 mm Hg, P=0.950). Incorporating the V wave into PAWP improved correlation between directly measured PAWP pressure-time integral compared with mid-A wave PAWP (R2=0.96 versus R2=0.86, P<0.001 for comparison). In patients with prominent V waves, the prevalence of combined pre- and postcapillary pulmonary hypertension decreased from 60.2% to 29.3% after V wave correction for the transpulmonary pressure gradients. Despite similar corrected pulmonary vascular resistances in patients with and without prominent V waves, apparent PA compliance was much lower in patients with prominent V waves (3.03±1.56 versus 4.90±2.27 mL/mm Hg, P<0.001), augmenting right ventricular afterload, and these changes were coupled with more severe right ventricular dysfunction, tricuspid regurgitation, blunted cardiopulmonary exercise reserve, and increased risk of hospitalization for heart failure or death in patients with versus without prominent V waves (adjusted hazard ratio, 2.09 [95% CI, 1.53-2.86]; P<0.001).More than 1 in 5 patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction display prominent V waves in excess of end-diastolic PAWP. This augments right ventricular afterload due to backward transmission of the V wave, contributing to right heart failure that is independent of the pulmonary vasculature. Failure to account for the V wave during hemodynamic assessment overestimates the severity of pulmonary vascular disease present.

title: Regional practice differences significantly affect the benefit of post-HCT gilteritinib in FLT3-ITD AML.
abstract: BMT CTN 1506 (MORPHO) was a phase 3 study of post-hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) maintenance with gilteritinib vs placebo for patients with FLT3-ITD-mutated acute myeloid leukemia (AML) in first remission. Subgroup analysis indicated a significant benefit of post-HCT gilteritinib for participants in North America but no benefit for those in Europe or Asia. We conducted a post hoc analysis of the data focusing on the time from AML diagnosis to HCT, pre-HCT FLT3 inhibitor use, and FLT3-ITD measurable residual disease (MRD). Participants who underwent transplantation <120 days from AML diagnosis and/or those treated with FLT3 inhibition before HCT were more likely to have improved survival from post-HCT gilteritinib. Pre-HCT MRD levels were higher (P = .001) in participants who underwent transplantation within 120 days from diagnosis and in those treated with an FLT3 inhibitor before HCT and underwent transplantation within 120 days (P = .008). Pre-HCT MRD was dependent on both FLT3 inhibitor use and time to HCT, because participants treated with successive courses of chemotherapy + FLT3 inhibition had successively lower MRD by the time of HCT. Time from AML diagnosis to HCT and pre-HCT FLT3 inhibitor use both appeared to affect MRD levels immediately before HCT, and geographic differences in these 2 practice patterns likely accounted for the observed regional differences in benefit from post-HCT gilteritinib. Increasing the number of courses of treatment before HCT may lower MRD sufficiently to eliminate the need for post-HCT inhibition, but with a presumed risk of some patients experiencing early progression. title: Genomic architecture of IRF4 rearrangements in childhood and adult large B-cell lymphomas.
abstract: Large B-cell lymphoma with interferon regulatory factor 4 (IRF4) rearrangement (LBCL-IRF4) predominantly affects children and young adults (CAYA) and presents as localized disease with excellent prognosis. Although most tumors harbor IRF4 rearrangement (IRF4-R), the existence of cryptic rearrangements has been suggested. Whether LBCL with IRF4-R in adults represents the same biological entity remains unclear. To address this question, 35 CAYA diagnosed with LBCL-IRF4 and 7 adults (aged >40 years) with LBCL with IRF4-R were investigated by an integrative molecular approach. Targeted sequencing structural variant analysis confirmed IRF4-R in 84% of investigated cases. In CAYA, an enrichment (55% vs 29% in adults) of translocations involving immunoglobulin heavy chain (IGH), with a breakpoint cluster 3' to IRF4 (EXOC2) was observed, including a cryptic insertion of IGHM-IGHJ5 into the IRF4 locus. Novel translocations, IRF4::MIR142 in 2 CAYA (7%) and IRF4::BATF in 1 adult, were discovered. Whole-exome sequencing analysis identified unreported mutations in LBCL-IRF4 as YY1 and ZC3H12A (11% each). The high incidence of mutations affecting the B-cell receptor/NF-κB pathways in LBCL-IRF4 was confirmed in cases with diffuse component only. None of the CAYA tumors were classified by the LymphGen tool. Adult LBCL with IRF4-R showed higher levels of genetic complexity and a distinct mutational profile with mutations on KMT2D and DTX1 (43% each), and MYD88-L265P (29%), and were predicted as EZB or MCD (29% each). These differential genetic features were in line with different clinical presentations (extranodal involvement and advanced stage). In conclusion, IRF4-R architecture and mutational profile differ according to age, supporting that not all cases should be classified as LBCL-IRF4.Published by Elsevier Inc. on behalf of American Society of Hematology. title: Predictors of posttransplant measurable residual disease negativity and impact on clinical outcomes in multiple myeloma.
abstract: Measurable residual disease (MRD) is a powerful prognostic tool in multiple myeloma, but predictors of achieving MRD negativity after autologous stem cell transplantation (ASCT) are not well defined. We studied 814 patients who achieved at least a very good partial response after ASCT between January 2016 and January 2023 and underwent MRD assessment by next-generation flow cytometry. Overall, 387 (48%) achieved MRD negativity after ASCT. The presence of t(11;14) (odds ratio [OR], 2.1; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.4-3.2; P< .01) and pretransplant response less than complete remission (OR, 2.1; 95% CI, 1.2-3.7; P< .01) independently predicted MRD positivity. Patients who were MRD positive had inferior progression-free survival (PFS; hazard ratio [HR], 1.99; 95% CI, 1.53-2.58; P< .001) and overall survival (HR, 1.62; 95% CI, 1.10-2.28; P = .009). Despite lower MRD-negative rate, 5-year PFS was similar among t(11;14) MRD positive (58%) and patients who were MRD negative (63%; P = .12). In patients who were MRD negative, the 5-year PFS was 73% in those without ≥2 HRCA compared with 55% in those with ≥2 HRCA (HR 1.9, 95% CI 1.2-3.3; P = .01). In the MRD-positive cohort, 5-year PFS was 53% in patients without ≥2 HRCA vs 17% in those with ≥2 HRCA (HR, 2.4; 95% CI, 1.6-3.6; P< .01). In addition, higher residual clonal plasma cell burden within MRD-positive disease was associated with inferior PFS (HR, 2.4; 95% CI, 1.2-6.9; P = .002). title: Application of Hi-C sequencing to detect oncogene rearrangements for diagnosis and treatment of large B-cell lymphoma.
abstract: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), the most common type of lymphoma, arises from various pathogenic mechanisms, including gene translocations and fusions. Detection of gene rearrangements using fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) is a standard practice for DLBCL diagnosis and guides treatment decisions. High-throughput chromosome conformation capture (Hi-C) DNA sequencing is a next-generation sequencing-based technology to identify genome-wide rearrangements using a single assay. In this study, Hi-C sequencing was performed using formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissues from 159 patients with DLBCL, identifying 746 cancer genes at or proximal to the rearrangement breakpoints, with a total of 1903 occurrences. Focusing on clinically important rearrangements, Hi-C detected 102 rearrangements of MYC, BCL2, and/or BCL6 in 92 patients and revealed the fusion partners, including 25 rearrangements missed by FISH. Causes of FISH-negative results included FISH-cryptic breakpoints, complex or faint FISH signals, low percentage of FISH positivity, and issues related to tissue fixation. Moreover, in 20 patients (12.6%), Hi-C sequencing detected 22 rearrangements characteristic of other lymphoma types, including CCND1 rearrangements that could lead to reclassification as mantle cell lymphoma. Survival analysis of genome-wide rearrangements using machine learning models identified MYC, PD-L1, CCND1, BCL2, NTRK1/PRCC, RRAS, and FANCE rearrangements with significant prognostic effects in the DLBCL cohort. In conclusion, Hi-C sequencing detects gene rearrangements crucial for diagnosis in an unbiased and molecular manner and showed high sensitivity and specificity in our study. These advantages of Hi-C sequencing offer help to improve the workflow of clinical pathology laboratories, diagnostic precision, and treatment of large B-cell lymphoma.© 2026 American Society of Hematology.
