title: EOAD-Signature Atrophy Predicts Dementia in Early-Onset MCI due to Alzheimer Disease: An MRI-Based Prognostic Biomarker.
abstract: Early-onset Alzheimer disease (EOAD) is associated with substantial variability in clinical progression, and reliable biomarkers to predict the transition from mild cognitive impairment (MCI) to dementia remain limited. Structural MRI measures have demonstrated prognostic value in late-onset Alzheimer disease, but their utility for predicting progression in EOAD is less well understood. The goal was to examine whether baseline cortical atrophy predicts progression to dementia in patients with MCI because of EOAD.This study included a well-characterized cohort of patients with EOAD enrolled in the large multisite natural history Longitudinal Early-Onset Alzheimer's Disease Study. Participants underwent standardized clinical assessments and structural MRI at baseline. Participants were aged between 40 and 64 years with biomarker-supported sporadic EOAD at the MCI stage. Cortical atrophy was measured within the EOAD-signature, a set of predominantly parieto-temporal regions showing greater atrophy in EOAD than in controls. Clinical severity was measured with the global Clinical Dementia Rating. Cox proportional hazards models estimated the association between baseline EOAD-signature atrophy burden and the hazard of progression to dementia over time. We evaluated whether EOAD-signature atrophy improved prognostic performance beyond baseline clinical severity using likelihood ratio tests, Akaike Information Criterion (AIC), and Harrell concordance index.A total of 130 patients with MCI due to EOAD (mean age 59.6 ± 4.1 years; 49% female) and 97 cognitively normal controls (mean age 56.9 ± 6.0 years; 64% female) were included. Greater baseline atrophy within the EOAD-signature predicted faster progression to dementia (hazard ratio [HR] = 1.24 per 1-SD increase in atrophy; 95% CI 1.13-1.37; p < 0.002). Adding EOAD-signature atrophy burden to a model including baseline clinical severity significantly improved model fit (ΔAIC = -4.5; likelihood ratio test p = 0.011).Baseline cortical atrophy within the EOAD-signature predicts progression from MCI to dementia in EOAD and provides prognostic information beyond baseline clinical severity. These findings support the potential value of EOAD-signature atrophy as an MRI-based biomarker for individualized prognostication and clinical trial stratification.

title: Systematic Review of Pharmacologic Treatment for Migraine Prevention in Adults: Report of the AAN Guidelines Subcommittee and the American Headache Society.
abstract: This systematic review (SR) provides updated evidence-based conclusions regarding the use of pharmacologic migraine prevention in adults to inform a new joint American Academy of Neurology (AAN) and American Headache Society practice guideline.A multidisciplinary panel conducted an SR following the 2017 AAN Clinical Practice Guideline Process Manual. Randomized controlled trials evaluating pharmacologic preventive treatments for adults with episodic or chronic migraine were included. Searches encompassed MEDLINE, Embase, and ClinicalTrials.gov from database inception through June 6, 2024. Studies were screened in duplicate, with dual independent risk-of-bias assessment. Outcomes included change in monthly headache days, ≥50% responder rate, and validated patient-reported quality of life (QOL) measures. Raw mean differences, standardized mean differences, and risk ratios were calculated. A modified Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation process was used to classify certainty of evidence.A total of 217 studies met inclusion criteria. For episodic migraine, high-confidence evidence showed that galcanezumab and erenumab are more effective than placebo in reducing headache frequency. Moderate-confidence evidence supported benefit from atogepant, eptinezumab, fremanezumab, propranolol, topiramate, and valproate. Several additional oral agents including amitriptyline, bisoprolol, flunarizine, fluoxetine, levetiracetam, metoprolol, nifedipine, pizotifen, and telmisartan had low-confidence evidence suggesting possible benefit. For chronic migraine, high-confidence evidence supported reductions in headache frequency with fremanezumab, galcanezumab, and onabotulinumtoxinA. Moderate-confidence evidence supported benefit from atogepant, eptinezumab, erenumab, topiramate and valproate. Across both episodic and chronic migraine populations, erenumab, fremanezumab, galcanezumab, eptinezumab, rimegepant, atogepant, topiramate and onabotulinumtoxinA demonstrated improvements in patient-reported QOL outcomes on validated instruments. Evidence comparing active treatments was limited and generally of low or very low confidence, restricting conclusions about comparative effectiveness.This SR provides a comprehensive synthesis of evidence on pharmacologic migraine prevention in adults. High- and moderate-confidence findings confirm the efficacy of several established and newer preventive therapies and demonstrate improvements in patient-reported outcomes across multiple validated measures. These conclusions informed the development of evidence-based recommendations, presented in a companion publication, to guide clinicians in selecting preventive medications for adults with episodic and chronic migraine.

title: Pharmacologic Treatment for Migraine Prevention in Adults Practice Guideline Recommendations: Report of the AAN Guidelines Subcommittee and the American Headache Society.
abstract: This practice guideline provides updated evidence-based recommendations regarding the use of pharmacologic migraine prevention in adults. A multidisciplinary panel conducted a systematic review and developed practice recommendations following the process outlined in the 2017 edition of the American Academy of Neurology Clinical Practice Guideline Process Manual. The systematic review includes studies published through June 6, 2024, and is available in a companion publication. Recommendations are supported by structured rationales that integrate evidence from the systematic review, related evidence, principles of care, and inferences from evidence. Recommendations are provided on how to decide when it is appropriate to start a pharmacologic migraine preventive medication and how to decide which migraine preventive medication to start. Recommendations address decision making on appropriate choices of migraine preventive medications in specific situations and populations, including patients with fibromyalgia, obesity, or hypertension; considerations for older adults; treatment during pregnancy and lactation; sex-related factors in choosing medications; and treatment for patients with medication overuse. Recommendations on assessment of treatment efficacy, adverse effects, and discontinuing migraine preventive medications are provided.

title: Pearls & Oy-sters: DPPX Antibody-Associated Encephalitis in a Patient With Diarrhea, Tremor, Ocular Flutter, and Cognitive-Psychiatric Changes.
abstract: Dipeptidyl-peptidase-like protein-6 antibody-associated encephalitis (DPPXE) is an autoimmune, multisystem disorder characterized by a triad of gastrointestinal prodrome, cognitive-psychiatric change, and CNS hyperexcitability. We report a 57-year-old man with 2 months of progressive gastrointestinal symptoms despite extensive normal gastrointestinal evaluation. He then developed tremor, myoclonus, gait ataxia, hyperekplexia, insomnia, emotional lability, memory impairment, and abnormal eye movements. Examination showed ocular flutter, tremor, ataxia, and cognitive impairment. Brain MRI revealed bilateral T2/fluid-attenuated inversion recovery hyperintensities in the brainstem and limbic regions. CSF demonstrated lymphocytic pleocytosis and 10 unique oligoclonal bands. DPPX-immunoglobulin G was detected in serum and CSF, confirming the diagnosis of DPPXE. Acute immunotherapy with intravenous methylprednisolone and plasma exchange followed by maintenance treatment with rituximab led to dramatic improvement of his symptoms, with residual memory impairment and tremor at 3 months. This case underscores the characteristic gastrointestinal prodrome and syndromic breadth of DPPXE, highlights the diagnostic value of panel-based screening, and supports treatment with immunomodulation.

title: Development and Validation of an Adult Medical Urgency Score for US Donor Heart Allocation.
abstract: One in 5 heart transplant candidates in the US die or are delisted without transplant. Donor hearts are currently allocated by a 6-status therapy-based system criticized for limited risk stratification and susceptibility to gaming.To develop a new heart allocation policy based on an objective medical urgency score that ranks candidates based on the interaction between physiology and mechanical circulatory support.Registry-based observational study using data from the US organ transplant system. All adult (aged ≥18 years) heart transplant candidates from January 2019 to August 2025 were included, split into training (2019-2023), validation (2023-2024), and test (2024-2025) datasets.A marginal structural model of 6-week mortality without transplant was estimated (the US Candidate Risk Score [US-CRS]). Eight models were compared in held-out data by weighted time-dependent area under the curve (AUC) and calibration by status. Finally, US-CRS was converted into an allocation policy and a match-run simulation of waitlist reordering was performed compared with the current 6-status system.Adult heart transplant candidates were partitioned into consecutive training (n = 21 859), validation (n = 7897), and test (n = 8256) datasets (mean [SD] age, 53 [13] years; 74% male). The chosen US-CRS model included 5 laboratory values and 4 therapeutic devices (durable left ventricular assist device, intra-aortic balloon pump, microaxial flow pump, and advanced mechanical circulatory support). In test-set cross-sections of candidates actively waiting on the same calendar date, US-CRS had similar or significantly higher time-dependent AUC than the current 6-status system (mean AUC, 0.807 vs 0.693, respectively) and acceptable calibration by status, especially for candidates who received their status by exception. In match-run analysis (n = 45 530 donor hearts), a US-CRS-based system led to 67% of transplant recipients moving down in rank order and increased observed 6-week transplant-censored mortality for the first candidate on the match run from 11.2% (95% CI, 10.1%-12.5%) under the current system to 15.7% (95% CI, 13.9%-17.6%) under the US-CRS-based system.In this registry-based study of US heart transplant candidates, a US-CRS-based allocation system prioritized sicker candidates with higher mortality without transplant compared with the current medical urgency statuses.

title: Multichannel Dysfunction Associated With a Dominant-Negative KCNH2 Missense Variant, p.G604S, Results in Action Potential Duration Prolongation and Early Afterdepolarizations in a Patient-Specific, Reengineered Cardiomyocyte Model of Type 2 Long-QT Syndrome.
abstract: Type 2 long-QT syndrome results from KCNH2-encoded Kv11.1 loss-of-function, but whether secondary inward-current dysfunction amplifies dysfunction remains unclear.We characterized sodium (SCN5A, INa) and L-type calcium channel (CACNA1C, ICa) function in KCNH2-G604S and variant-corrected isogenic control induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (iPSC-CMs). Whole-cell patch-clamp measured action potential duration at 90% repolarization (APD90), and potassium (IKr), sodium (INa), and calcium (ICa, L) currents. Fluo-4 imaging quantified calcium transients. A modified Kernik-Clancy iPSC-CM model incorporated experimentally measured persistent INa,L and ICa,L fractions and simulated isolated and combined current defects.KCNH2-G604S caused severe IKr loss-of-function (72.5% reduction). APD90 was prolonged in G604S-iPSC-CMs (765±58 ms) compared with isogenic controls (368±37 ms; P<0.005), with early afterdepolarizations in 50% of G604S cells. Nifedipine, verapamil, and mexiletine successfully shortened APD90 and abolished early afterdepolarizations. Compared with isogenic control, INa,L (0.60±0.1% versus 0.26±0.06%; P<0.01), persistent ICa,L (2.88±0.55% versus 1.26±0.35%; P<0.05), and calcium transient decay times (P<0.0001) were greater in G604S iPSC-CMs. Increased persistent ICa,L was phenocopied by E-4031 in isogenic controls and reduced by nifedipine in G604S iPSC-CMs. In silico modeling revealed that the IKr defect alone prolonged APD90 to only 620 ms. The addition of the observed INa,L defect had a small additive effect (+20 ms); however, incorporating persistent ICa,L synergistically extended APD90 to 758 ms, replicating the experimental phenotype. Flux dynamics analysis indicated that this persistent Ca2+ entry suppresses the forward-mode sodium-calcium exchanger, forcing a compensatory reliance on sarcoplasmic-endoplasmic reticulum Ca-ATPase that primes for calcium instability.The KCNH2-G604S variant drives a severe multihit phenotype via primary IKr loss-of-function and secondary state-dependent gain-of-function in persistent ICa,L. These comprehensive validations demonstrate that the remodeled persistent ICa,L acts as the essential amplifier driving extreme action potential duration prolongation and Ca2+ mishandling.

title: Proton Radiotherapy Decreases Incidence of Radiation-Induced Second Malignant Neoplasms Compared to Photon Radiotherapy in Patients With Retinoblastoma.
abstract: Retinoblastoma is the most common primary intraocular neoplasm in children. Use of radiotherapy has decreased due to the incidence of second malignant neoplasms (SMNs). In our study, photon (n = 42) and proton (n = 66) radiotherapy cohorts had median follow-up of 28.7 and 18.2 years, respectively. The majority of patients (74%) had bilateral disease at diagnosis. Proton radiotherapy is associated with significantly lower cumulative incidence of in-field SMNs (0% vs. 11.1% at 15 years, p = 0.005), with three additional cases occurring > 20 years after photon radiotherapy. These findings suggest that when radiotherapy is indicated for patients with bilateral retinoblastoma, proton radiotherapy should be considered when feasible.© 2026 Wiley Periodicals LLC.

llm_summary: Retinoblastoma is the most common eye cancer in children, and while radiotherapy can be effective, it carries a risk of causing second malignant neoplasms (SMNs), or new cancers, in treated patients. Researchers compared outcomes between 42 patients who received photon radiotherapy and 66 patients who received proton radiotherapy, with median follow-up periods of 28.7 and 18.2 years respectively, to evaluate whether the type of radiation affected SMN development. Proton radiotherapy was associated with a significantly lower cumulative incidence of in-field SMNs at 15 years (0% versus 11.1%, p = 0.005), with three additional SMN cases occurring more than 20 years after photon radiotherapy. These findings suggest that proton radiotherapy may reduce the risk of radiation-induced second cancers compared to photon radiotherapy in patients with bilateral retinoblastoma. When radiotherapy is clinically necessary for bilateral retinoblastoma, proton radiotherapy should be considered as a treatment option when it is feasible to administer.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers examined radiation-induced second malignant neoplasms (SMNs) in retinoblastoma patients treated with proton radiotherapy (n = 66) or photon radiotherapy (n = 42), with median follow-up periods of 18.2 and 28.7 years respectively, in a cohort where 74% had bilateral disease at diagnosis. The primary endpoint was cumulative incidence of in-field SMNs. Proton radiotherapy was associated with significantly lower cumulative incidence of in-field SMNs compared to photon radiotherapy (0% versus 11.1% at 15 years, p = 0.005), with three additional SMN cases occurring beyond 20 years in the photon cohort. The longer follow-up duration in the photon group (28.7 versus 18.2 years) allowed detection of late-occurring malignancies that may not yet be apparent in the proton cohort. These findings suggest proton radiotherapy should be considered when radiotherapy is indicated for bilateral retinoblastoma, though longer follow-up of the proton cohort is needed.

title: Dupilumab Improves Esophageal Distensibility in EoE: 24-Week Results From the REMODEL Randomized Trial.
abstract: Eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) is a chronic, often progressive, type 2 inflammatory disease characterized by eosinophilic infiltration, and esophageal narrowing and dysfunction. This analysis presents 24-week outcomes from the phase 4 REMODEL trial, evaluating long-term esophageal distensibility in adults with EoE.Adult EoE patients were randomized 2:1 to dupilumab 300 mg once weekly or placebo. Patients were assessed overall and by low (<17 mm) and normal (≥17 mm) baseline distensibility plateau (DP) subgroups. Endpoints at week (W) 24 included: absolute change from baseline in esophageal DP diameter on endoluminal functional lumen imaging probe (primary), and changes from baseline in Endoscopic Reference Scores (EREFS) and EoE histology scoring system (EoEHSS) grade/stage scores. Safety was assessed.Sixty-nine patients (46 dupilumab, 23 placebo) were randomized. Evaluable patients in the DP subgroups were: 30 low (19 dupilumab, 11 placebo) and 33 normal (22 dupilumab, 11 placebo) baseline DP. At W24 overall, dupilumab improved esophageal DP diameter vs placebo; least squares mean (LSM) (±SE) absolute change from baseline: +1.28 mm (0.29) and -0.01 mm (0.42); LSM difference: +1.30 mm (95% CI: 0.31, 2.29; P < 0.05). LSM difference vs placebo in the low DP subgroup was +2.21 mm (95% CI: 0.78, 3.63; nominal P = 0.0024). Overall LSM difference for dupilumab vs placebo was -4.96 (-6.06, -3.85) in EREFS, and -0.71 (-0.86, -0.57) and -0.65 (-0.80, -0.51) in EoEHSS grade and stage scores, respectively (all P < 0.0001). No new safety signals were identified.Dupilumab significantly improved W24 esophageal distensibility outcomes, with greater improvements in the low baseline DP subgroup compared to the overall population. title: Anticoagulation after transcatheter and surgical bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement: A narrative review.
abstract: BackgroundBioprosthetic aortic valve replacement, specifically surgical (SAVR) and transcatheter (TAVR), is among the most frequently performed cardiac interventions globally, yet anticoagulation strategies after implantation remain incompletely defined. Atrial fibrillation, notably prevalent pre- and post-operatively in these patients, substantially amplifies thromboembolic risk and complicates decision-making in an already elderly, frail, and comorbid population.ObjectivesTo critically evaluate current anticoagulation strategies after bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement across sinus rhythm and atrial fibrillation in both SAVR and TAVR, and to identify evidence gaps and guideline inconsistencies.MethodsWe conducted a narrative review of major international guidelines (ESC/EACTS 2025, ACC/AHA 2020, and NICE 2021) and key clinical trials on antithrombotic therapy in valve replacement populations. Focus was placed on bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement, with mechanical and non-aortic valves excluded.ResultsAspirin monotherapy is the most consistently supported strategy after bioprosthetic TAVR in sinus rhythm, though guidelines diverge on duration and recommendation strength. In atrial fibrillation, all three guidelines apply uniform CHA2DS2-VASc-based frameworks irrespective of AF phenotype, procedural context, or detection modality, reflecting lacking evidence rather than deliberate clinical judgement. No trial has enrolled patients specifically with new-onset post-procedural AF or stratified by AF subtype, and subclinical AF after bioprosthetic AVR remains entirely uncharacterised.ConclusionsGuideline divergence reflects a structurally inadequate evidence base rather than genuine clinical equipoise. Individualised decisions informed by procedure type, AF phenotype, frailty, and bleeding risk are required to guide clinical practice, alongside an adequately powered stratified randomised trial incorporating mandatory continuous rhythm monitoring.

title: Mitral Valve Repair in Patients With Class I Obesity: A Propensity-Matched Analysis.
abstract: Obesity may increase the technical complexity of robotic mitral valve (MV) repair, but comparative outcomes with sternotomy remain poorly defined.This study aimed to compare perioperative and long-term outcomes of robotic vs sternotomy MV repair in patients with class I obesity.A total of 880 patients with class I obesity (body mass index 30-34.9 kg/m2) underwent MV repair at our clinic between 2008 and 2025. After excluding those with mitral stenosis, active endocarditis, prior sternotomy, or concomitant procedures, 429 patients remained. Propensity score matching (1:1) yielded 132 patients in each group who underwent either robotic or conventional sternotomy MV repair.Median age was 59 years (IQR: 52-66), and 81% were male. Cardiopulmonary bypass and cross-clamp times were longer in the robotic group than in the sternotomy group (86 vs 65 minutes and 60 vs 48 minutes, respectively; P < 0.001). Robotic MV repair was associated with shorter hospitalization (3.5 vs 5 days; P < 0.001) and a lower postoperative transfusion rate (1.5% vs 10.6%; P = 0.002). There were no operative deaths in either group. No sternal wound infections occurred. Thirty-day readmission was numerically higher after robotic repair (12.8% vs 4.3%; P = 0.064). Ten-year survival was 92% (95% CI: 87% to 97%) with no significant difference between groups (P = 0.83).In patients with class I obesity, the robotic approach in comparison to sternotomy was associated with lower transfusion rates, shorter hospitalization, and comparable operative mortality and long-term survival relative to sternotomy. title: Elucidating the Gene Expression Signature of Rosai-Dorfman Disease: A Study from the Atlas of Blood Cancer Genomes Initiative.
abstract: Rosai-Dorfman disease (RDD) is a rare histiocytic disorder characterized by accumulation of large histiocytes in nodal and/or extranodal sites. The underlying biology of RDD and factors that distinguish it from the other histiocyte disorders are poorly understood. To better understand the disease biology, we employed whole transcriptome RNA sequencing to study the gene expression profiles of RDD as part of the Atlas of Blood Cancer Genomes (ABCG) initiative. Gene expression profiles of RDD (N=23) were then compared to two other histiocytoses (Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH, N=15) and Erdheim-Chester disease (ECD, N=4), which are most often considered in the clinicopathologic differential diagnosis of RDD. We found that gene expression levels by RNA sequencing correlated well with known immunohistochemistry results for diagnostic markers for all three diseases, highlighting the ability to use RNA-based approaches for diagnosis of these tumors. RDD samples showed enrichment of gene sets related to B cells and the IL27 pathway. In contrast, LCH showed enrichment of gene sets related to resting dendritic cells and the HNF3A pathway. We found significant differences in the composition of the microenvironment with an enrichment of memory B cells, plasma cells and CD8 T cells in the RDD microenvironment and enrichment of dendritic cells in the LCH microenvironment. In summary, our study demonstrates unique gene expression signatures in RDD that show overlap as well as distinctive patterns from LCH or ECD. These novel gene expression signatures encompass pathways that could potentially contribute to the pathogenesis and targeted treatment of this rare histiocytic entity.

llm_summary: Rosai-Dorfman disease (RDD) is a rare disorder involving abnormal accumulation of immune cells, but its underlying biology and how it differs from related conditions remain poorly understood. Researchers used RNA sequencing to analyze gene expression patterns in 23 RDD samples and compared them to 15 Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH) and 4 Erdheim-Chester disease (ECD) samples, which are conditions often confused with RDD in clinical diagnosis. RDD samples showed distinct enrichment of genes related to B cells and the IL27 signaling pathway, while LCH samples were enriched for genes related to dendritic cells and the HNF3A pathway, and the immune cell composition differed significantly between the diseases. These findings suggest that RDD has a unique gene expression signature that could potentially inform both diagnostic approaches and development of targeted treatments for this rare disease. Further research will be needed to determine whether these gene expression differences contribute to disease development or could serve as therapeutic targets.

RNA sequencing-derived gene expression levels correlated well with immunohistochemistry results for diagnostic markers across all three histiocytic disorders. RDD samples demonstrated enrichment of B cell-related gene sets and the IL27 pathway, while LCH showed enrichment of resting dendritic cell-related gene sets and the HNF3A pathway. The RDD microenvironment was enriched in memory B cells, plasma cells, and CD8 T cells, whereas the LCH microenvironment showed dendritic cell enrichment. These findings identify distinctive gene expression signatures in RDD that may inform understanding of disease pathogenesis and guide targeted therapeutic approaches for this rare histiocytic entity.

title: Randomized Trial of Hypofractionated Postmastectomy Radiation Therapy in Women With Breast Reconstruction (RT CHARM, Alliance A221505).
abstract: Patients with breast cancer requiring postmastectomy radiation therapy (PMRT) often desire breast reconstruction. Reconstructions can be adversely affected by PMRT, and fear of reconstruction complications has discouraged adoption of short-course radiation therapy used after lumpectomy. To fill the evidence gap, we conducted a noninferiority trial of hypofractionated versus conventional PMRT in patients undergoing breast reconstruction. The primary outcome was reconstruction complication rate, a composite of wound healing, readmission, capsular contracture, unplanned reoperation, and reconstruction failure.Women with unilateral invasive breast cancer with planned immediate or delayed reconstruction and PMRT were randomly assigned (1:1) to 50 Gy (25 fractions/5 weeks) or 42.56 Gy (16 fractions/3 weeks). This study was designed with a noninferiority margin of 10%, assuming a 2-year reconstruction complication rate of 25% with conventional PMRT. Randomization was stratified by immediate versus delayed and autologous versus implant-only reconstruction.Between 2018 and 2021, 898 patients enrolled with a median follow-up of 3.9 years; 825 patients were evaluable for the primary end point. The 24-month reconstruction complication rates were 12.3% (52/422) with hypofractionated PMRT and 10.2% (41/403) with conventional PMRT, corresponding to an estimated difference of -2.1% (95% CI, -6.5 to 2.2). The complication rate was higher (regardless of arm) with implant-only versus autologous reconstruction (odds ratio = 1.65). There was no statistically significant difference in 36-month locoregional recurrence rates: 1.5% (95% CI, 0.7 to 3.2) with hypofractionated and 2.2% (95% CI, 1.1 to 4.3) with conventional PMRT. Acute and late toxicity rates were not statistically different.A 16-fraction course of hypofractionated PMRT is safe and noninferior to conventional PMRT in women undergoing breast reconstruction after mastectomy.

title: Meningioma in the modern era: Updates in stratification and therapeutic approaches.
abstract: Meningioma is the most common primary intracranial tumor in adults. Most meningiomas have an indolent growth pattern, but some can grow quickly. The World Health Organization (WHO) classification system is the gold standard for tumor grading and relies predominantly on histopathology and limited molecular alterations. It is increasingly recognized that the variability in tumor behaviour is incompletely captured using traditional systems. Contemporary advances have expanded tumor stratification beyond starting WHO grading, providing a more comprehensive framework for understanding tumor biology. Molecular profiling has identified independent biological classification systems and molecular signatures that capture important prognostic information beyond histopathology. Magnetic resonance imaging-based analyses and radiomics have enabled non-invasive characterization of tumor phenotype and growth potential. Therapeutically, surgical resection and radiation therapy remain the foundation of management, with evolving paradigms emphasizing maximal safe resection and risk-adapted radiotherapy strategies informed by integrated tumor characteristics. Systemic therapies have historically shown limited efficacy; however, recent efforts are shifting toward biomarker-driven, precision approaches guided by molecular alterations. Future directions focus on integrating multimodal data into unified, clinically actionable models that more accurately predict recurrence, progression, and treatment response. Such approaches aim to move beyond parallel classification systems toward individualized management strategies, ultimately advancing meningioma care into a precision-based paradigm.Copyright © 2026 The Authors. title: Large-scale integration of functional assay data for the resolution of germline BRCA1 and BRCA2 variants of uncertain significance.
abstract: Carriers of BRCA1 and BRCA2 pathogenic variants are at a significantly elevated risk for several cancers. Widespread germline genetic testing has led to a significant increase in the detection of variants of uncertain significance (VUSs) in these genes. To assess variant pathogenicity, we curated, harmonized, and integrated functional data for 3,247 BRCA1 and 6,177 BRCA2 missense variants derived from BRCA1/2 functional assays. Functional results were harmonized across studies by converting data into ordinal categorical variables. We applied ClinGen variant interpretation guidelines for each assay to assign evidence for or against pathogenicity. Final evidence criteria for each variant were obtained through the integration of results from different assays, and large case-control studies confirmed that benign and pathogenic variants categorized using the integrated functional framework are associated with low and high risk for breast cancer, respectively. title: Hypertension and clinical outcomes following thoracic radiotherapy.
abstract: Radiation therapy (RT) is highly efficacious in treating thoracic malignancies. However, RT has been linked to potential cardiotoxicity. Yet, the long-term incidence, severity, and implications of HTN-development post-RT are unknown.Leveraging a large US-based Comprehensive-Cancer-Center-cohort of patients treated with thoracic-RT from 2007 to 2019, we included patients ≥18 years old with histologically confirmed esophageal or lung cancers. The primary outcome was incidence of incident/new or worsened HTN [systolic-blood-pressure-(SBP) ≥130 mmHg] after RT-initiation. The secondary outcomes were major-adverse-cardiac-events (MACE- heart-failure, myocardial-infarction, arrhythmia, stroke, and sudden-death), disease-progression, and overall-survival, by HTN-status. Differences in outcomes by HTN-status were also evaluated via landmark-analysis, excluding those with undiagnosed HTN. Observed new HTN rates were compared to Framingham-predicted-rates, and absolute-excess-risks were estimated. Multivariate regression was used to define the relation between clinical and RT measures and both new or worsened HTN-development and survival-outcomes.Overall, 439 RT-treated patients (238 esophageal; 201 lung; 66.7% male; mean age 63.6 years; 65% baseline HTN) were identified. Over a median follow-up of 23 months, 255 (58.1%) developed new or worsened HTN; median SBP increase of 7 mmHg. In landmark-analysis, the cumulative incidence of new or worsened HTN by 1-year was 48.0% and 63.4%, respectively. Using the JNC-8 cutoff of ≥140/90 mmHg, the new HTN rate was 21.6% at 1-year, translating to a 3.4-fold higher rate than the Framingham-predicted-rate (RR 3.37, P < 0.001). In multivariate regression, RT-dose was consistently associated with new or worsened HTN-development (P < 0.05); those with RT-induced-HTN saw improved progression-free-survival and overall-survival (HR 0.67 and 0.54, P < 0.01, respectively). Beyond traditional factors, only RT-dose is consistently associated with MACE (P < 0.05). No specific antihypertensive class prevented RT-related HTN.These data suggest that thoracic-RT increases early HTN risk.Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Inc.

title: Advanced Practice Providers in Spinal CSF Leak Programs: A Multi-Institutional Study of Current Roles and Perceived Impact on Patient Care.
abstract: Advanced practice providers (APPs), including nurse practitioners and physician assistants, are increasingly integrated into radiology practices. However, their utilization and clinical responsibilities in dedicated spinal CSF leak programs have not been characterized. Using a multicenter survey, we investigated APP training, clinical responsibilities, perceived impact, and challenges of APP integration at US spinal CSF leak programs.A survey was distributed to physicians at US institutions with dedicated spinal CSF leak programs and APP involvement. Candidate institutions were identified through the International Society for Spinal CSF Leak and American Society of Spine Radiology. Survey questions addressed program characteristics, APP training and structure, clinical responsibilities, perceived impact, and challenges. Responses were summarized descriptively.Twelve institutions completed the survey. Eight (67%) reported caring for more than 250 spinal CSF leak patients annually. APPs included nurse practitioners at 4 centers (33%), physician assistants at 3 (25%), and both at 5 (42%); 7 centers (58%) had APPs dedicated exclusively to spinal CSF leak care. APP training was primarily informal and on-the-job at all institutions. Common primary APP responsibilities included obtaining outside imaging, patient intake and symptom review, procedure and sedation orders, informed consent, post-procedural follow-up, pain management, and treatment of rebound intracranial hypertension. Shared APP and physician responsibilities commonly included outside record review, determining evaluation urgency, preliminary imaging review, sedation assessment, and multidisciplinary coordination. Procedural responsibilities such as lumbar puncture, intrathecal contrast administration, myelography planning, and CSF leak treatment were primarily performed by physicians in most programs. At least 75% of respondents strongly agreed that APP participation improved continuity of care, patient communication/accessibility, clinic efficiency, patient satisfaction, physician administrative burden, and multidisciplinary coordination. Common barriers included funding/support, billing/reimbursement, and limited procedural privileges.APPs are widely integrated into dedicated spinal CSF leak programs, with substantial involvement in pre-procedural evaluation, care coordination, and post-procedural management, while advanced myelography and CSF leak treatment remain predominantly physician-directed. APP participation was perceived to improve patient care and clinical workflow. These findings provide a framework for APP integration into specialized spinal CSF leak programs.© 2026 by American Journal of Neuroradiology.

llm_summary: Advanced practice providers such as nurse practitioners and physician assistants are increasingly working in medical practices, but their specific roles in specialized spinal cerebrospinal fluid leak programs have not been well documented. Researchers surveyed twelve US institutions with dedicated spinal CSF leak programs to characterize how advanced practice providers were trained, what clinical responsibilities they performed, and how their involvement affected patient care. Advanced practice providers at these centers primarily handled pre-procedural tasks including patient intake, obtaining outside imaging, arranging procedures, obtaining informed consent, and managing post-procedural care, while physicians retained responsibility for advanced procedures such as lumbar puncture and CSF leak treatment. At least 75% of surveyed physicians reported that advanced practice provider participation improved continuity of care, patient communication, clinic efficiency, patient satisfaction, and multidisciplinary coordination. Common barriers to expanding advanced practice provider roles included funding limitations, billing and reimbursement challenges, and restricted procedural privileges, suggesting that broader implementation of this model may require addressing these structural and financial obstacles.
llm_summary_expert: A multicenter survey of twelve US institutions with dedicated spinal CSF leak programs examined the training, clinical responsibilities, and perceived impact of advanced practice providers (APPs), including nurse practitioners and physician assistants. Eight institutions (67%) reported caring for more than 250 spinal CSF leak patients annually, with seven centers (58%) employing APPs dedicated exclusively to spinal CSF leak care; APP training was primarily informal and on-the-job across all institutions. APPs commonly performed pre-procedural responsibilities including patient intake, procedure ordering, informed consent, and post-procedural follow-up, while physicians retained primary responsibility for advanced myelography and CSF leak treatment procedures. At least 75% of respondents strongly agreed that APP participation improved continuity of care, patient communication and accessibility, clinic efficiency, patient satisfaction, physician administrative burden, and multidisciplinary coordination. Common barriers to APP integration included funding and support limitations, billing and reimbursement challenges, and restricted procedural privileges.

title: Impact of endoscopic ultrasound in cholangiocarcinoma staging: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Accurate staging is crucial for managing cholangiocarcinoma (CCA). Endoscopic ultrasound with tissue acquisition (EUS-TA) may enhance cross-sectional imaging-based staging; however, the impact of EUS on CCA management decision-making is unclear.6 electronic databases were searched through to 10 July 2025 for studies on EUS-TA in staging CCA cases eligible for surgical resection or liver transplantation. The primary outcome was the pooled proportion of patients excluded from curative-intent surgery based on the EUS findings, which included newly detected findings and confirmation by EUS-TA of cross-sectional imaging findings. Secondary outcomes included the pooled incremental benefit of EUS (IBEUS) over cross-sectional imaging and EUS-specific adverse events. The IBEUS was defined as the proportion of patients with malignant lymph nodes identified by EUS-TA but not by cross-sectional imaging, relative to all patients who underwent cross-sectional imaging.9 studies with 831 patients were included. The rate of exclusion from curative-intent surgery based on EUS findings was 10% overall (95%CI 6%-18%; 9 studies), 7% for perihilar CCA (pCCA; 95%CI 2%-19%; 5 studies), 10% for those planned for resection (95%CI 4%-22%; 5 studies), and 8% for those planned for transplantation (95%CI 3%-22%; 3 studies). The pooled IBEUS was 3% (95%CI 1%-10%; 5 studies) overall, 4% (95%CI 1%-17%; 3 studies) for pCCA, 1% (95%CI 0%-3%; 2 studies) in patients intended for operative resection, and 7% (95%CI 1%-26%; 2 studies) in those intended for transplantation.EUS may impact CCA staging and support treatment decisions.Thieme. llm_summary: Accurate staging of cholangiocarcinoma, a bile duct cancer, is essential for determining whether patients can undergo curative surgery or transplantation. Researchers conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of nine studies involving 831 patients to evaluate whether endoscopic ultrasound with tissue sampling (EUS-TA) could improve staging beyond standard imaging methods like CT or MRI scans. The analysis found that EUS-TA led to exclusion from curative-intent surgery in 10% of patients overall, with rates of 7% for perihilar cholangiocarcinoma, 10% for those planned for resection, and 8% for those planned for transplantation. The incremental benefit of EUS over cross-sectional imaging alone was modest, identifying additional malignant lymph nodes in 3% of patients overall, though this increased to 7% in patients intended for transplantation. These findings suggest that EUS-TA may provide clinically meaningful information to support treatment decisions in cholangiocarcinoma staging, though the overall impact appears limited in most patient populations.

The primary outcome was the pooled proportion of patients excluded from curative-intent surgery based on EUS findings, while secondary outcomes included the incremental benefit of EUS (IBEUS) over cross-sectional imaging and adverse events. EUS findings led to exclusion from curative-intent surgery in 10% of patients overall (95% CI 6%-18%), with 7% for perihilar cholangiocarcinoma, 10% for resection candidates, and 8% for transplantation candidates. The pooled IBEUS was 3% overall (95% CI 1%-10%), indicating that EUS-TA identified malignant lymph nodes not detected by cross-sectional imaging in a small proportion of patients. These findings suggest EUS may impact cholangiocarcinoma staging and treatment decisions, though the clinical magnitude of this impact remains modest.

title: Determinants of Etoposide Hypersensitivity Span all of the Top2 alpha Catalytic Domains.
abstract: Type II topoisomerases are found in all kingdoms of life and perform key biological functions during replication, transcription, and other DNA metabolic events. These enzymes are also the targets of important classes of anti-bacterial and anti-cancer drugs. Clinically active drugs targeting topoisomerase II primarily act as poisons rather than as enzyme inhibitors. During the normal enzymatic reaction, topoisomerase poisons stabilize the normally reversible covalent enzyme/DNA adduct leading to DNA damage. More recently, Top2 mutants have been identified that exert the same effect as these small molecules, and expression of these mutants in cells leads to genome instability. Mutations that increase the potency of topoisomerase targeting drugs have the potential to mimic drug action and expand insight into the drug mechanism. Here we carried out an extensive screen of mutations in human Top2α to identify mutations that result in elevated levels of sensitivity to the anti-cancer drug etoposide. This screen was conducted by expressing a library of mutagenized human Top2α that complemented a yeast temperature sensitive Top2 allele in rad52- yeast strains. Etoposide hypersensitive mutations were identified throughout the catalytic domains of Top2α. Mutants were typically hypersensitive to other Top2 inhibitors, although some mutants had hypersensitivity that was specific for etoposide. Several examples of mutant proteins identified in the screen were purified and characterized biochemically. These proteins exhibited a broad range of alterations in enzyme activity including altered requirements for divalent cations, altered relaxation and decatenation activity, altered utilization of ATP, and enhanced DNA cleavage in the absence of inhibitors. Our results suggest that diverse mechanisms influence the ability of small molecules to convert type II topoisomerases to DNA damaging agents, and the etoposide hypersensitivity mutations found provide landmarks for the development of small molecules with improved potency.Copyright © 2026. llm_summary: Researchers examined how mutations in human topoisomerase II alpha (Top2α), an enzyme targeted by cancer drugs like etoposide, could increase cellular sensitivity to these drugs by screening a library of mutagenized Top2α variants in yeast cells. Etoposide hypersensitivity mutations were identified throughout the catalytic domains of Top2α, with most mutants showing increased sensitivity to multiple topoisomerase inhibitors, though some displayed hypersensitivity specific to etoposide. Biochemical characterization of purified mutant proteins revealed diverse alterations in enzyme function, including changes in requirements for divalent cations, altered DNA relaxation and decatenation activity, modified ATP utilization, and enhanced DNA cleavage without drug present. These findings suggest that multiple distinct mechanisms can influence how small-molecule drugs convert topoisomerase II into DNA-damaging agents, potentially informing strategies to develop more potent therapeutic compounds. The etoposide hypersensitivity mutations identified in this screen provide molecular landmarks that could guide the rational design of improved topoisomerase-targeting drugs for cancer treatment.

title: Safety and efficacy of ticagrelor versus clopidogrel for carotid artery stenting: propensity score matched analysis.
abstract: Dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) is recommended around carotid artery stenting (CAS) to reduce periprocedural stroke risk. Clopidogrel is widely used, but response variability related to pharmacokinetics and CYP2C19 polymorphisms may limit its effectiveness. Ticagrelor is a more potent, direct-acting P2Y12 inhibitor; however, its comparative effectiveness in CAS remains uncertain.We conducted a retrospective cohort study in the TriNetX database, identifying adults with carotid artery stenosis who underwent CAS between January 2016 and August 2025 and received either ticagrelor or clopidogrel. Primary outcomes at 180 days included ischemic stroke, major hemorrhage, intracranial hemorrhage, and all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included inpatient readmission and emergency department (ED) visits. Propensity score matching (1:1), Kaplan–Meier survival and Cox proportional hazards analysis were used.Among 6,996 patients, 378 received ticagrelor and 6,618 received clopidogrel; aspirin co-use was similar (89.7% vs 91.7%). After matching, 377 patients remained in each cohort. Ischemic stroke (2.7% vs 4.2%; HR 0.56, 95%CI 0.25–1.27; p=0.159) and major hemorrhage (2.9% vs 4.8%; HR 0.61, 95%CI 0.29–1.30; p=0.197) were numerically lower with ticagrelor. Rates of intracranial hemorrhage was similar (2.7% vs 2.7%; HR 0.61, 95%CI 0.14–2.53; p=0.488). Mortality was numerically higher with ticagrelor (3.4% vs 2.7%; HR 1.64, 95%CI 0.68–3.97; p=0.263). ED visits were similar (14.3% vs 14.6%; HR 0.97, 95%CI 0.67–1.42; p=0.895). Inpatient readmission was numerically lower with ticagrelor (15.9% vs 19.1%; HR 0.81, 95%CI 0.57–1.14; p=0.223).Ticagrelor and clopidogrel showed comparable safety and effectiveness following CAS. Future prospective genotype-informed trials are warranted to confirm these findings.

title: Cold and Room-Temperature Platelets in Cardiac Surgery: The CHIPS Randomized Clinical Trial.
abstract: Patients undergoing cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass often require platelet transfusions for bleeding. Platelets are routinely stored at room temperature (20-24 °C) for up to 5 to 7 days; however, cold storage (1-6 °C) may allow for increased storage duration without loss of hemostatic function.To determine the maximum cold-storage duration, up to 21 days, for which cold-stored platelets (CSPs) are noninferior or superior in hemostatic efficacy to room-temperature platelets (RTPs) when transfused in actively bleeding patients undergoing cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass.A phase 3, multicenter, randomized, partially blinded, adaptive, noninferiority, storage duration-ranging trial conducted in pediatric and adult patients undergoing cardiac surgery with planned cardiopulmonary bypass at 27 sites in the US and Australia from December 2021 to March 2025. Statistical analysis was conducted from September 9 to October 3, 2025.Patients were randomized 2:1 to receive CSPs with a maximum of 21 days of storage vs RTPs with a maximum of 7 days of storage.The primary outcome was a hemostatic efficacy score with values ranging from 1 to 5 and higher values indicating greater bleeding. The noninferiority margin was 1 point. The success criterion was met if at least 1 cold-storage duration of 7 days or more had a posterior probability of noninferiority of at least 97.5%. The secondary outcome was 24-hour chest tube output.Of the 1000 patients who underwent platelet transfusion, 989 were included in the primary analysis (650 CSPs and 339 RTPs). The cohort had a mean (SD) age of 42.1 (30.1) years and 67.8% were male. CSPs were noninferior to RTPs for the primary outcome, with a probability of greater than 99.9% for all cold-storage durations. Pooled across storage durations, CSPs had a mean difference from RTPs of 0.09 (95% credible interval, -0.06 to 0.23). Median (IQR) chest tube output at 24 hours (8.9 mL/kg [5.2-15.4] for CSPs vs 8.4 mL/kg [5.5-15.9] for RTPs; difference in medians, 0.4 [95% CI, -1.0 to 1.5]) was not statistically different between study groups. In a post hoc analysis, as all storage durations were noninferior, considering the CSPs as a single group, the hemostatic efficacy score was similar between both groups: mean (SD) of 3.08 (1.15) CSPs vs 2.99 (1.10) RTPs. There were no differences in venous or arterial thrombotic events, transfusion-associated adverse events, acute respiratory distress syndrome, kidney failure, septic shock, and mortality between the study groups, except for increased reexploration rates in the CSP group.For patients undergoing cardiac surgery, CSPs stored up to 21 days are noninferior to RTPs for the control of active surgical bleeding. Use of CSPs may allow for increased availability of platelets by reducing wastage and shortages and may allow for incorporation of platelets into inventory at locations where platelets cannot be maintained due to the 5- to 7-day shelf life of RTPs.ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04834414.

title: Musculoskeletal Histopathology of Klippel-Trénaunay Syndrome: A Clinicopathologic Study of 21 Cases With Long-Term Orthopedic Follow-Up.
abstract: Klippel-Trénaunay syndrome (KTS) is a rare congenital vascular-overgrowth disorder within the broader spectrum of PIK3CA-related overgrowth syndromes. Although clinical, radiologic, and orthopedic manifestations are well described, the histologic spectrum of KTS-associated pathology remains under-characterized. Clinicopathologic findings from 21 patients with clinically established KTS were reviewed, including 18 with longitudinal clinical follow-up and 3 consultation cases of rare malignant mesenchymal neoplasms. Cases were identified from institutional pathology and clinical databases, and available hematoxylin and eosin-stained sections and ancillary studies were reviewed. The cohort included 11 males and 10 females. Among the 18 clinically followed patients, 12 had limb length discrepancy or asymmetric limb overgrowth, 9 had documented deep vascular malformations, 4 had intra-articular/synovial malformations, and 10 underwent initial orthopedic evaluation or intervention before age 18. Orthopedic morbidity clustered into mechanical overgrowth-related, vascular malformation-related, and soft tissue/wound-related complications. Histologic findings included superficial and/or deep slow-flow vascular malformations, ulceration and granulation tissue, hemosiderin-laden reactive synovium, and destructive hemorrhagic arthropathy. Intra-articular disease recapitulated a hemophilic arthropathy-like pattern, with hemosiderotic synovitis, papillary synovial hyperplasia, and progressive joint destruction with loss of articular cartilage, exposed subchondral bone destruction and remodeling, all attributable to long-standing intra-articular hemorrhage. Three consultation cases showed malignant mesenchymal neoplasia, including 2 angiosarcomas. Recognition of these patterns is important for pathologists evaluating specimens from patients with known or suspected KTS, particularly when findings mimic hemophilic arthropathy, diffuse-type tenosynovial giant cell tumor, nonsyndromic vascular malformation, and/or end-stage destructive arthropathy.Copyright © 2026 Wolters Kluwer Health, LLC. title: Phase II study of selpercatinib in children and young adults with RET-altered tumors: Arm N of the NCI-COG Pediatric MATCH trial (APEC1621).
abstract: This is a phase II subprotocol of the National Cancer Institute-Children's Oncology Group Pediatric Molecular Analysis for Therapy Choice (MATCH) precision oncology platform trial evaluating selpercatinib, a RET inhibitor, in children and young adults aged 1-21 years with relapsed or refractory solid tumors with RET alterations.Selpercatinib was given at 90 mg/m2/dose (maximum dose 160 mg/dose) orally twice daily for 28-day cycles until progression or intolerable toxicity. The primary aim was to determine the objective response rate (ORR) and secondary objectives included assessing the tolerability of selpercatinib and estimating the progression-free survival (PFS).Two patients with papillary thyroid carcinomas harboring CCD6C-RET fusions matched to the subprotocol. One patient was deemed ineligible as they had not yet experienced tumor recurrence. The other patient enrolled and received selpercatinib at 90 mg/m2/dose, completing all 26 cycles of protocol therapy and achieving a Partial Response confirmed by central imaging review. There were no dose-limiting toxicities, and the patient experienced only grade 1 adverse events (AEs) attributable to selpercatinib.There was a low match and accrual rate on this MATCH subprotocol, resulting in early termination of the study. The basis for low accrual was likely multifactorial, including the overall rarity of this genetic alteration across pediatric tumor types and accelerated FDA approval of selpercatinib in children ≥ 12 years old prior to the opening of this subprotocol.NCT04320888.Andrea T. llm_summary: This phase II subprotocol of the Pediatric MATCH precision oncology trial evaluated selpercatinib, a targeted drug that inhibits RET protein, in children and young adults aged 1-21 years with relapsed or refractory solid tumors harboring RET genetic alterations. Only one eligible patient with papillary thyroid carcinoma carrying a CCDC6-RET fusion enrolled and completed all 26 cycles of oral selpercatinib treatment at 90 mg/m² twice daily. The enrolled patient achieved a partial response confirmed by central imaging review and experienced only grade 1 adverse events with no dose-limiting toxicities. The study terminated early due to low accrual, which the researchers attributed to the rarity of RET alterations across pediatric tumor types and accelerated FDA approval of selpercatinib in children aged 12 years and older prior to the subprotocol's opening. The limited enrollment prevented comprehensive evaluation of selpercatinib's efficacy and tolerability in this pediatric population, though the single patient's favorable response and safety profile provide preliminary supportive evidence.
llm_summary_expert: This phase II subprotocol of the NCI-COG Pediatric MATCH trial evaluated selpercatinib, a RET inhibitor, in children and young adults aged 1-21 years with relapsed or refractory solid tumors harboring RET alterations, administered at 90 mg/m2/dose orally twice daily in 28-day cycles. The primary endpoint was objective response rate, with secondary endpoints including tolerability and progression-free survival assessment. Only one patient with papillary thyroid carcinoma harboring a CCDC6-RET fusion enrolled and completed all 26 protocol cycles, achieving a partial response with no dose-limiting toxicities and only grade 1 adverse events. The study terminated early due to low accrual and match rates, attributed to the rarity of RET alterations across pediatric tumor types and accelerated FDA approval of selpercatinib in children aged 12 years and older prior to subprotocol activation. The minimal enrollment substantially limits the ability to draw conclusions regarding selpercatinib efficacy and tolerability in this population.

title: Metaproteomic analysis of human sonicate fluid highlights neutrophil extracellular trap formation associated with periprosthetic joint infection.
abstract: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) is a devastating complication of total joint arthroplasty that can be challenging to diagnose and treat. Neutrophils are a prominent feature in PJI, with neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) known to be present; little is known, however, about the physiology of PJI-associated NETs. Here, the proteomes of PJI and non-infectious arthroplasty failure (NIAF), analyzed using liquid chromatography tandem mass-spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) and proximity extension assay (PEA)-based profiling of fluids derived from sonication of arthroplasty components removed from patients who had undergone revision arthroplasty, were compared, with a focus on NET formation. In addition, in vitro effects of synovial fluid components on Staphylococcus aureus-induced NET formation were characterized. LC-MS/MS (PJI n = 85, NIAF n = 26) and PEA (PJI n = 95, NIAF n = 39) showed NET formation and neutrophil degranulation to be associated with PJI, with the complement cascade and platelet activation pathways identified as potential contributors. In vitro studies showed delayed NET formation in artificial synovial fluid compared to standard cell culture media conventionally used to evaluate NETs. Together, these results demonstrate the presence of NETs in PJI, identify potential pathways involved in PJI-associated NETosis, and point to an influence of synovial components on NET formation during PJI.Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) is a major complication of joint replacement, placing a significant burden on patients and the healthcare system. Our research reveals that neutrophils and their antimicrobial "traps" are dominant features of the immune response at the infection joint site. Importantly, we found that the unique environment of the joint delays the formation of these traps, potentially contributing to the pathogenesis of PJI. By establishing a new experimental platform tailored for the infected joint, this work provides a foundational platform for probing these mechanisms and supports the development of improved diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

llm_summary: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI), a serious complication following joint replacement surgery, is difficult to diagnose and treat, prompting investigation into the immune mechanisms involved. Researchers compared protein profiles from fluid samples obtained by sonication of removed joint implants from patients with PJI (n=85 for mass spectrometry, n=95 for protein profiling) versus those with non-infectious implant failure (n=26 and n=39 respectively), focusing on neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs), which are web-like structures that neutrophils form to trap bacteria. Both analytical methods identified NET formation and neutrophil degranulation as associated with PJI, with the complement cascade and platelet activation pathways emerging as potential contributors to this process. Laboratory experiments revealed that synovial fluid components from the joint environment delayed NET formation compared to standard culture conditions, suggesting that the unique joint environment may influence how neutrophils respond to infection. These findings establish that NETs are present in PJI and identify potential mechanisms involved, providing a foundation for developing improved diagnostic and therapeutic approaches for this serious infection.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers examined sonicate fluid from arthroplasty components removed during revision surgery, comparing proteomes from 85 periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) cases and 26 non-infectious arthroplasty failure (NIAF) controls using liquid chromatography tandem mass-spectrometry and proximity extension assay-based profiling. Metaproteomic analysis identified neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation and neutrophil degranulation as associated with PJI, with the complement cascade and platelet activation pathways implicated as potential contributors. In vitro studies demonstrated that synovial fluid components delayed Staphylococcus aureus-induced NET formation compared to standard cell culture media. These findings establish NETs as a dominant feature of the immune response in PJI and identify potential pathways involved in PJI-associated NETosis. The results are limited by their observational nature and the in vitro demonstration that the joint microenvironment influences NET kinetics, which may affect interpretation of mechanisms in vivo.

title: Immediate Resumption of Positive Airway Pressure Following Sinus Surgery: A Prospective Controlled Multicenter Study.
abstract: Untreated obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) in the perioperative period confers significant cardiopulmonary risk. However, many otolaryngologists defer restarting positive airway pressure (PAP) therapy following functional endoscopic sinus surgery (FESS) due to perceived risk of epistaxis, mucosal injury, and wound healing. Thus, the objective of this study was to evaluate the immediate resumption of PAP therapy in OSA patients undergoing FESS.Multicenter prospective controlled study.Academic medical centers.Patients with a history of OSA on PAP therapy scheduled for FESS were prospectively enrolled (OSA/PAP group) along with a control group of non-OSA FESS patients (non-OSA group). Patients in the OSA/PAP group restarted PAP therapy on post-operative Day #0 or #1. The primary outcome was change in Lund-Kennedy endoscopic scores (LKES); secondary outcomes of interest included change in post-operative SNOT-22 scores, Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) scores, complications, and epistaxis severity scores.A total of 100 patients were enrolled, of whom 49 were in the OSA/PAP group, and 51 were in the non-OSA group. In multivariate adjusted models, early PAP resumption was not independently associated with higher LKES compared to the control group at POV1 or POV2, higher SNOT-22 compared to the control group at POV1 or POV2, or higher postoperative epistaxis scores compared to the control group. There were no PAP-related complications such as orbital emphysema or pneumocephalus.Early resumption of PAP in OSA patients undergoing FESS does not appear to be associated with worsened post-operative endoscopic scores, quality-of-life scores, or an increased risk of post-operative epistaxis.© 2026 The Author(s). llm_summary: Untreated obstructive sleep apnea poses significant cardiopulmonary risks during surgery, yet many otolaryngologists delay restarting positive airway pressure (PAP) therapy after sinus surgery due to concerns about nosebleeds and wound complications. Researchers conducted a multicenter prospective study comparing 49 patients with obstructive sleep apnea who resumed PAP therapy immediately after functional endoscopic sinus surgery with 51 control patients without sleep apnea who underwent the same procedure. Early PAP resumption was not associated with worse endoscopic healing scores, quality-of-life measures, or increased nosebleed severity compared to the control group, and no serious complications such as orbital emphysema occurred. These findings suggest that the perceived risks of immediate PAP therapy resumption may not be substantiated, potentially allowing clinicians to mitigate perioperative cardiopulmonary risks in sleep apnea patients undergoing sinus surgery. Future research with larger sample sizes and longer follow-up periods would help confirm whether this practice can be safely adopted as standard clinical care.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers examined whether immediate resumption of positive airway pressure (PAP) therapy following functional endoscopic sinus surgery (FESS) increases postoperative complications in a prospective controlled multicenter study enrolling 49 OSA patients on PAP therapy and 51 non-OSA control patients. The OSA/PAP group restarted PAP on postoperative day 0 or 1, with primary outcomes including change in Lund-Kennedy endoscopic scores (LKES) and secondary outcomes of SNOT-22 scores, Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index scores, and epistaxis severity. In multivariate adjusted models, early PAP resumption was not independently associated with higher LKES, higher SNOT-22 scores, or higher postoperative epistaxis scores compared to controls at either postoperative visit. No PAP-related complications such as orbital emphysema or pneumocephalus occurred in the treatment group. Early PAP resumption in OSA patients undergoing FESS does not appear associated with worsened postoperative outcomes or increased epistaxis risk.

title: Disagreement Between Outpatient Complications in the USNWR ENT Ratings and Clinical Adjudication.
abstract: In 2024, the US News and World Report (USNWR)'s Best Hospitals began reporting complications following elective outpatient otolaryngology procedures in its ears, nose, and throat (ENT) ranking. However, this methodology has not been clinically adjudicated in a peer-reviewed domain. We aimed to conduct manual health record adjudication to assess whether the USNWR methodology accurately attributes complications following elective outpatient otolaryngology procedures.Case-cohort.A case-cohort of n = 80 elective, outpatient otolaryngology procedure/complication pairings from January 2019 to October 2023 across four academic medical centers using the 2024 USNWR otolaryngology procedure subgroups and Solventum Ambulatory Potentially Preventable Complications (AM-PPC) software.We used the AM-PPC-defined complication types as our standard of comparison for our clinical adjudication. Using the electronic health record, we adjudicated: (1) Was there agreement (yes/no) on complication type between our clinical adjudication and the Solventum AM-PPC software? (2) Was the complication clinically related to, or a sequela of, the index otolaryngology procedure (yes/no)?The clinical adjudication agreed on complication type in 59/80 (74%) of patients, and 63/80 (79%) were judged to be clinically related to the index otolaryngology procedure. In total, 50/80 (63%) complications were adjudicated to be in agreement on both the complication type and clinical relatedness to the index procedure, while 9/80 (11%) complications did not agree with the complication type nor were clinically related to the index procedure.Outpatient complications reported in the USNWR ENT rating lack the specificity to exclude patients whose complications are sequelae of chronic underlying conditions or related to concurrent, non-otolaryngology procedures.© 2026 American Academy of Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery Foundation.

llm_summary: The US News and World Report began reporting complications from outpatient ear, nose, and throat procedures in its 2024 hospital rankings, but this methodology had not been clinically validated by independent experts. Researchers manually reviewed 80 cases of complications following elective outpatient otolaryngology procedures from four academic medical centers to determine whether the automated Solventum software used by USNWR correctly identified complication types and their relationship to the procedures performed. Clinical adjudication agreed with the software on complication type in 59 of 80 cases (74%), and 63 of 80 complications (79%) were judged to be clinically related to the index procedure, with only 50 of 80 cases (63%) meeting both criteria simultaneously. The findings suggest that the USNWR methodology lacks sufficient specificity to distinguish between complications directly caused by otolaryngology procedures and those arising from chronic underlying conditions or unrelated concurrent procedures. The reported complication rates in the USNWR ENT rankings may therefore include cases that are not truly attributable to the procedures being evaluated.

Clinical adjudication using electronic health records assessed agreement on complication type between the Solventum Ambulatory Potentially Preventable Complications software and expert review, and determined whether complications were clinically related to the index procedure. title: Machine learning in comparative effective research of pharmacological interventions: a scoping review.
abstract: Machine learning (ML) is rapidly transforming the evaluation of the comparative effectiveness research (CER) of pharmacological interventions. It offers an attractive data-driven alternative to traditional statistical causal inference methods for estimation of heterogeneous and individualized treatment effects and is particularly well-suited for high-dimensional real-world data. While variety of ML algorithms have been applied to CER, methodological challenges and limitations remain, and recommendations for conducting, reporting, and evaluating such studies have only recently been proposed.This paper conducts a scoping review of ML approaches used in CER for pharmacological interventions. We searched multiple databases from January 2020 to January 2026, supplemented by reference mining, and included 28 primary studies. We focused on research topics, ML methodologies, reporting, validity, and robustness of the findings, and appraised risk of bias.Although the use of ML methods in CER of pharmacologic intervention is relatively recent, it is expanding and consolidating around few specific methods, notably doubly robust estimators paired with ensemble learners. However, methodological rigor and reporting consistency remain uneven, yielding a moderate risk of bias. Standardized methods, transparent reporting, and dedicated appraisal tools are needed before these approaches can reliably inform research, clinical practice, and policy.

title: Survival in Patients With Pituitary Carcinoma.
abstract: Pituitary carcinoma (PC) is defined by the presence of metastasis from a pituitary tumour. PC is rare, therefore information regarding survival and factors influencing survival are limited. We sought to assess overall survival following the diagnosis of PC and to determine factors associated with outcome.Retrospective case series.Patients with PC who attended the Mayo clinic between 1997 and 2025.Information regarding patient demographics, tumour characteristics, management and outcomes were extracted.In total 25 patients (11 women, 44%) were diagnosed with PC (median age 56 years, range, 44-78). The most common cell type was a corticotroph tumour (n = 15, 60%). All but one patient had pituitary directed surgery and all received pituitary adenoma (PA) directed radiation therapy. Metastases were identified a median 6 years (range, 1-32) after initial PA diagnosis. At last follow-up, 10 (40%) patients were alive, 12 (48%) died of PC, and 3 (12%) died from other causes. The median survival time of patients from PC diagnosis was 3 years. The 1-, 5- and 10-year survival rates were 59%, 37% and 15%, respectively. Increased survival probability was associated with temozolomide treatment (n = 9) at some point in treatment plan (p = 0.026), the use of systemic therapy vs locoregional treatment (p = 0.045), female sex (p = 0.011), and in nonfunctional tumours (p = 0.023).PC carries a poor prognosis, with a median survival of only 3 years. Improved survival was associated with temozolomide exposure, female sex, and nonfunctional tumour subtype and underscores the prognostic relevance of tumour biology and treatment approach.© 2026 John Wiley & Sons Ltd.

title: MGMT promoter methylation as a molecular biomarker in neuro-oncology: current practices, challenges, and future directions.
abstract: MGMT promoter methylation (MGMTpm) is a well-established molecular biomarker in neuro-oncology. We review current practices, challenges, and future directions for MGMTpm as a biomarker in central nervous system (CNS) tumors.The literature on MGMT function, and MGMTpm clinical significance and testing in CNS tumors was reviewed.We discuss the biological role of MGMT in DNA repair and the mechanisms by which MGMTpm leads to increased tumor sensitivity to alkylating agents. We summarize the clinical significance of MGMTpm in glioblastoma and its emerging relevance in other CNS tumors. Testing practices using methylation-specific PCR, pyrosequencing, and genome-wide methylation array-based approaches are discussed, along with challenges related to testing variability and "gray-zone" methylation, and emerging technologies such as nanopore sequencing.Despite ongoing technical and interpretative challenges, MGMTpm remains a robust and clinically valuable biomarker in neuro-oncology.© 2026. llm_summary: MGMT promoter methylation (MGMTpm) serves as an important molecular biomarker for predicting treatment response in brain tumors because it affects how tumor cells repair DNA damage from chemotherapy. Researchers reviewed the scientific literature on MGMT's biological function and the clinical significance of MGMTpm testing across central nervous system tumors, with particular emphasis on glioblastoma. The review discusses how MGMTpm increases tumor sensitivity to alkylating agent chemotherapy and summarizes current testing methods including methylation-specific PCR, pyrosequencing, and genome-wide methylation arrays. title: Translating Evidence Into Practice: Implementing Caregiver Burden Assessments in Palliative Care Clinic.
abstract: BackgroundCaregiver burden assessments lack clinical uniformity in palliative care. Existing evidence-based interventions often impose resource demands that are prohibitive for smaller programs.Objectives(1) Demonstrate the practical utility of routine caregiver screening paired with an interdisciplinary team (IDT) response protocol. (2) Identify patient and caregiver factors influencing burden.DesignSetting: Cross-sectional study in a US outpatient palliative care clinic.Measurements: The 12-item Zarit Burden Interview (ZBI-12) was administered by a nurse or social worker. Scores guided immediate, point-of-care IDT interventions.ResultsOf 81 approached caregivers, 74 completed the ZBI-12 (72% female; median age 56). Burden was stratified into mild (n = 37), mild-moderate (n = 22), and high (n = 15) tiers, with median scores increasing significantly (6 vs 16 vs 28; P < 0.001). General counseling was consistent across tiers (∼54%). However, high-intensity supportive interventions rose significantly with burden severity: social work telephone follow-ups increased (0% vs 13.6% vs 33.3%; P < 0.001), support group referrals rose (2.7% vs 31.8% vs 46.7%; P < 0.001), and psychotherapy referrals increased (0% vs 4.5% vs 13.3%; P = 0.030). Multivariable linear regression showed lower patient Palliative Performance Scale (PPS) scores independently predicted higher caregiver burden. Each 10-point decrease in PPS correlated with a 2.4-point increase in total ZBI-12 score (β = -0.240; 95% CI, -0.433 to -0.048; P = 0.015).ConclusionThis workflow provides a replicable roadmap to transition caregivers from "invisible patients" to actively supported extensions of the care unit, reinforcing dyadic assessments as standard practice in outpatient palliative medicine.

title: Phonological Posterior Probabilities as Interpretable Markers of Articulatory Impairment in Motor Speech Disorders.
abstract: This study examined whether phoneme-level posterior probabilities generated by an articulatory-informed deep learning model (Phonet) can serve as interpretable and sensitive markers of articulatory impairment in motor speech disorders (MSDs). The goal was to determine whether these features distinguish individuals with and without MSDs and reflect varying severity levels of articulatory impairment.A total of 676 participants (199 with MSDs, 477 without MSDs) completed a remotely captured word repetition task. Speech recordings were phonetically aligned, and posterior probabilities were extracted using a retrained version of the Phonet model, which estimates frame-level probabilities for 23 phonological classes. Segment-level posterior values were computed and compared across groups and severity levels using linear mixed-effects regression models.Posterior probabilities were significantly reduced in the MSD group across all phoneme types. Within the MSD group, posterior probabilities decreased progressively with greater clinical severity, as measured by both perceptual sound distortion ratings and a cumulative articulation error score. Segment-specific analyses revealed systematic differences across phoneme classes, indicating that posterior probabilities capture distinct patterns of articulatory degradation associated with motor speech impairment.Phoneme-level posterior probabilities serve as interpretable, segment-specific indicators of articulatory impairment in MSDs. These features differentiate clinical status and reflect gradations of severity, making them promising tools for augmenting traditional perceptual speech assessments. Their linguistic transparency and scalability support future clinical applications in diagnosis, monitoring, and targeted intervention.
